News.title: Further tax hikes will be ‘final nail’ for Britain’s high streets, top retail bosses warn Healey ahead of Budget
News.content:
Next

TOP retailers have warned further tax hikes will be the “final nail” for Britain’s high streets.

Big firms fear being stung in Chancellor John Healey’s Budget later this month.



John Lewis boss Jason Tarry said targeting the biggest names in “a crude ‘large versus small’ equation doesn’t add up”.

He told the Daily Telegraph: “Penalising anchor retailers through higher business rates risks harming the smaller businesses operating in their orbit.”



Meanwhile, Marks & Spencer boss Stuart Machin hit out at former Chancellor Rachel Reeves over her tax raises.

He urged Mr Healey to reverse “the mistakes of the last two Budgets”.

It comes as figures show UK employers pay almost £2,000 more in tax on an employee earning £30,000 compared to bosses of firms in Florida.

The British Chambers of Commerce said more taxes in the Budget would be fatal for the country’s economic outlook.

Kate Shoesmith, its director of policy, said the Chancellor must cut business costs to enable firms to grow. She added: “Any further tax rises on firms in the budget would be the final nail in the coffin for the country’s economic ambitions.”

Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith said: “Thanks to Labour’s Jobs Tax and employment red tape, unemployment is up, leaving hundreds of thousands out of work and living off welfare.”



A Treasury spokesman said: “We are backing firms through business rates cuts, a cap on corporation tax and a £4.3billion package to help businesses manage costs and keep investing.”

Treasury sources said there are no plans for a warehouse tax.

News.title: Group of researchers travelling 830 miles to remote island in quest to find Amelia Earhart’s plane
News.content:
HUNT FOR ANSWERS Group of researchers travelling 830 miles to remote island in quest to find Amelia Earhart’s plane







Next

A TEAM of researchers have set off on an 830-mile odyssey to examine an object that could be the wreck of Amelia Earhart’s plane.

The group are roughly halfway through an epic voyage to the remote atoll and have high hopes that they could solve the mystery of the famed aviator’s disappearance.



Earhart vanished in 1937 while attempting to become the first female pilot to circumnavigate the globe.

Researchers from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University are headed to Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean.



There they will scour the sea for what has been called the Taraia Object, a mystery wreck visible via satellite that was first spotted in 2020.

It was later confirmed that the object – which visually resembles an aircraft fuselage and tail – can be seen in photos of the island as far back as 1938.

The team is undertaking the arduous journey aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel.

They left Kiribati’s remote capital on Wednesday and are steaming towards Nikumaroro.

When they arrive they will need to navigate through a narrow gap in the atoll’s reef.

Expedition leader Richard Pettigrew said: “Finding Amelia Earhart’s Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime.”



Earhart was travelling with her navigator Fred Noonan when she disappeared.

Her Lockheed Electra 10E plane is thought to have crashed into the sea when it ran out of fuel.

Both Earhart and Noonan were either killed on impact or were unable to escape the sinking aircraft and drowned.



As part of the expedition, the team will first document the site through photos and videos before using remote sensing techniques.

Only then will the team undergo the painstaking process of underwater excavation to bring the object to the surface for definitive identification.

The team will also conduct an exploration of nearby islands to search for any debris that may have washed up in the waves.

The next step would be to return what is left of the wreckage to the US and Purdue University.

Experts previously thought they’d made a breakthrough when they noticed code on an aluminium panel found washed up on Nikumaroro in 1991 believed to be part of her missing aircraft.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, further analysis revealed that it actually belonged to a plane that crashed during World War Two at least six years later.

A separate team of scientists claimed they had successfully pinpointed the location of the wreckage as nearby Howland Island using a radio restored from 1937.

News.title: RAF Fairford ‘bomb’ plot was carried out by ‘low-level criminals being directed by Iran’, cops believe
News.content:
Next

THE suspected RAF Fairford bomb plot was carried out by low-level criminals being directed by Iran, cops believe.

Seven men have been arrested after three “suspicious vehicles” pulled up outside the Gloucestershire base in the early hours of September 27.



Five men in their early 20s were arrested near the base shortly after, before a Brit-Iranian dual national was arrested in London on October 1.

The seventh suspect, a 22-year-old British man, was also arrested in the capital, Counter Terrorism Police confirmed on Tuesday.



US President Donald Trump has since pulled all American bombers from the base over fears of an Iranian drone attack.

And detectives are now reportedly probing suggestions the suspects are low-level crooks who were being directed by a Middle East-based recruiter.

Cops are also examining potential links to firebombing attacks against Jewish Londoners earlier this year, The Times reports.

The Met was investigating the possibility that Iranian proxy Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia could be behind the incidents in March and April.



But they were allegedly masterminded from a bunker in Iraq by 33-year-old Mohammad al-Saadi.

Al-Saadi is accused of conspiring to provide material support to Iran‘s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

He is alleged to have hired proxies in Britain and directed them through FaceTime calls, according to US authorities.

Officers were alerted to three “suspicious vehicles” by a local farmer who dialled 999 after getting no answer from the guardroom at the base.

A report later claimed one of the suspects had phoned 999 on himself before their arrest.



The five suspects, from London, were bailed after police said a substance in drums in their three vans was found not to be a viable explosive.

The Sun understands it was petrol.

Speculation grew that the men could have been fuel thieves, after the UK’s counter-terror chief said a “quantity of petrol” was found.

Cops are also said to be probing whether the incident was for surveillance, a “dry run” to test security or to send a message to the Government.

Mr Trump has hit out repeatedly at UK cops for bailing the suspects, who he dubbed “seriously bad people” and “terrorists”.



He said the US had been involved in a “longstanding investigation” against the suspects.

The US President had previously said the men should not have been bailed, while his secretary of state claimed a “foreign actor” was involved.

Last week, the Pentagon confirmed every American bomber – including at least 10 B-1 bombers – deployed to Fairford had now returned home.

According to US media reports, the withdrawal appears to be in response to fresh or renewed security concerns about safety on the base.

Two officials told the New York Times that the hasty withdrawal followed “new threats” about a potential Iran-backed plot concerning the base.



Fears of a sinister foreign hand intensified after Andy Burnham said there were “strong indications” Iran played a role in the incident.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The alleged scheme came two months after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said the base was a “legitimate target”.

Tehran has “categorically” denied any involvement.

News.title: Inside Freddie Foreman’s wild life of crime – from cleaning up for Krays to newly-revealed role in VERY famous robbery
News.content:
Next

FREDDIE FOREMAN took another swig of his ice-cold beer in the Spanish sunshine as he reflected on his life of crime.

The Krays’ feared fixer — known as “Brown Bread Fred” — had more than a few regrets after losing some of the best years of his life away from his family while behind bars.





Foreman, who died yesterday aged 94, told me from a hillside villa on his beloved Costa del Sol: “Crime is a mug’s game.

“I spent 16 birthdays and Christmases banged up. Say it quickly and it doesn’t seem so bad.

“But I missed my children growing up and, when I weigh up the pros and cons, it doesn’t come out in my favour and certainly not my family’s.”

Freddie was Ronnie and Reggie Kray’s clean-up man who knew where the bodies were buried — because he left them there.

He was acquitted of two notorious 1960s murders — those of Tommy “Ginger” Marks and Frank “the Mad Axeman” Mitchell, both of which he later admitted.

But he was sentenced to ten years in 1969 for his part in the gangland slaying of Jack “The Hat” McVitie.

He helped dispose of the body at sea, with McVitie’s body wrapped in chicken wire, attached to weights and dumped in “muddy waters”.

As well as being known as “Brown Bread” — cockney slang for dead — he was also “The Guv’nor”, “The Undertaker” and “Mean Machine”.





All reflected his long and violent criminal history — as an enforcer and body disposer for the Krays and a record-breaking armed robber.

He died yesterday at a West London care home after a short illness, with eldest son Greg at his side.

He is also survived by another son, former EastEnders and film actor Jamie and daughter Danielle.

Godson Nick Reynolds, son of Foreman’s close friend, the late Great Train Robber Bruce, said: “I saw Fred a few months ago when he was in St Mary’s Hospital and he was in great form.

“Like a lot of old villains, Fred was a mixture of being feared by some and loved by many.

“He was a formidable character and a major underworld figure. But he was an old-fashioned gentleman.”

Michael Biggs, son of Great Train Robber Ronnie, recalled how Foreman helped his father flee the country following his 1965 escape from Wandsworth Prison.

He said: “It was Fred who organised passports and travel arrangements. He kept in touch with my dad and came to visit him in Brazil.



“Fred had a lot of history but I could not fault him. He was a gentleman to me.”

Foreman was born on March 5, 1932 and raised in Battersea, South London, the youngest of five sons.

His father was a taxi driver but Foreman drifted into crime, appearing at the Old Bailey for the first time aged 16, charged with affray.

He worked as a minder for a gang of female shoplifters from South London’s Elephant and Castle known as the “Forty Thieves”, and went on to work for 1950s godfather Billy “King of the Underworld” Hill.

During the 1960s, Foreman was part of an elite team of robbers, including notorious hitman Alfie Gerard and Ronnie Everett.

As well as Reynolds, he was close with several other train robbers and ran a club with Buster Edwards.

The Sun on Sunday can reveal that Foreman left £47,245 in a South London phone box for police four months after the August 1963 Great Train Robbery, in which 15 bandits got away with £2.6million — £60million in today’s currency.

The cash was left on behalf of Harry Smith, one of three train robbers who got away with the crime, amid suspicions of police corruption.



At the time, Foreman lived with wife Maureen and their young children in Lambeth, South London, and owned a bookies and pub.

He became allied to the Krays after they provided him with a flat when he was on the run.

Foreman lent the brothers his “professional services” in exchange for a cut in their rackets.

Foreman had already forged a formidable reputation, after gunning down Tommy “Ginger” Marks in January 1965 as he walked with safe-blower George “Jimmy” Evans.

Foreman later admitted: “Alf drove the car past Marks and Evans. I pulled out a .38 and started shooting. The pair of them danced about like puppets on a string. But Evans was a coward and used Marks as a shield.”

The body of family man Marks was never found.

In December 1966, Foreman took part in the execution of Frank “The Mad Axeman” Mitchell, sprung from Dartmoor Prison by the Krays 11 days earlier.

Foreman said: “Taking Mitchell out of prison was like unleashing a mad rottweiler on the public. The twins cosied him up with a girl in a flat but he became a nuisance and had to go.”



As with Marks, his body was never recovered.

By this time the Krays reigned supreme in London after years of simmering tensions with the Richardson brothers, Charlie and Eddie, who ran a scrapyard in Camberwell, South London.

Foreman had a lifelong grudge with Eddie Richardson, who died in August, which boiled over in a scrap between the elderly pair at the 2017 funeral of Great Train Robber Tommy Wisbey.

In October 1967, the Krays murdered Jack McVitie. Afterwards Foreman buried him at sea, as he had done with Marks and Mitchell.

In 1969, Foreman was jailed for ten years after being convicted of being an accessory to McVitie’s murder.

He told me the worst moment of his life was on the day he was jailed with the Kray gang — when police told him he would be charged with Mitchell’s murder.

Foreman said: “My wife Maureen came to see me at the back gate of the Old Bailey and tried to console me over the ten years I had got.

“I had to tell her I was due to be charged with Mitchell’s murder. Her face crumpled.”

After release, Foreman moved to the US and ran a gaming machine business before returning to Britain.

He was part of a gang who broke into the Security Express depot in Shoreditch, East London, in Easter 1983.



The robbers doused guards in petrol and threatened to torch them unless they complied with their demands.

Foreman was one of five linked to the robbery who moved to Spain, which did not have an extradition treaty with the UK then.

Among the five was Ronnie Knight, married to actress Barbara Windsor, who Foreman had known well since the Kray days.

But the good life ended in 1990 when Spanish cops arrested him at his Marbella apartment, for being “undesirable”.

Still dressed in shorts and sandals, he was bundled on to a flight back to the UK, where he was jailed for nine years for handling proceeds of the robbery.

He was released in 1995, when he was a pallbearer for Ronnie Kray’s coffin.

He set up the Punchbowl pub in London with son Greg, which was later sold to Guy Ritchie.

By then, Foreman had separated from his wife Maureen after starting another relationship with new partner, Janice, while in Spain.

Foreman wrote eight books and was an adviser during the filming of Kray movie Legend, starring Tom Hardy.

During my time with him in Spain in 2011, Foreman took no pride in his criminal exploits.



He dismissed the Kray twins as a “pair of mugs” and revealed there had been plans to kill them before their arrests.

Maureen Flanagan, former Page Three model and close friend of the Krays said: “Ronnie told me that if he was facing ten men and could have two with him then it would be Fred and Reggie. He told me he trusted Fred with his life.”

Foreman took a dim view of today’s criminals.

He told me: “Nowadays you have got smackheads beating up old women and getting a smacked wrist. You tell me if things have changed for the better.”

News.title: I run cat cafe where people pay £6 an hour to let moggies sit on their laps – they make people so happy
News.content:
Next

WITH a fluffy Maine Coon cat peacefully nestled in my lap, an overwhelming sense of calm washes over me.

After just ten minutes of stroking “gentle giant” Mouse, my heart rate drops from 86 beats per minute to just 62.



The incredible effects should come as no surprise.

In a new survey, two in three cat owners (64 per cent) said their pets help them feel calm and relaxed.



And research shows that people who have moggies are generally in better shape when it comes to health, wealth and happiness.

Teams from universities in Finland and the US analysed data from 93 countries, and found that nations with higher feline counts often reported higher levels of happiness.

Finland came top of the list, followed by Denmark and Iceland.

While the UK, which is home to around 13million cats — roughly one for every five people — came in at number 18.

But can having a kitty really improve your lot in life?

To find out, The Sun on Sunday headed to The Cats’ Den Coffee House in Darlington armed with a heart-rate monitor to conduct an experiment.



Owner Liz Handley opened her dream cafe a year ago, and shares her own cats with customers.

Toys and grooming mitts are laid out to entice them on to people’s laps.

Liz, 47, said: “I don’t need a study to tell me that cats make us happy — I know the benefits of having them.



“I suffered from depression, but having my cats has been a saviour.

“I am a genuine crazy cat lady and have 14 at home. But I only bring the eight that are happy to be among people and love the attention into the cafe.

“A lot of customers who suffer with anxiety come here for some relaxation and I love seeing people chilling with a cup of tea and a cat on their knee.

“The cats make people so happy. There is no better job satisfaction than this.”

Liz added: “I love it when pensioners come here.



“Some get lonely, but they may not want to sit and chat to other people. With a cat, you don’t have to. You just give them some love and warmth and they return the favour.

“They can sit on your knee, they can purr to show how happy they are and by stroking them, the body naturally experiences a calming effect, too.”

With eight cats to entertain a steady flow of customers, Liz says there is never a dull moment.

“Some rest on the high perches, others play fight and others just want to be loved,” she said.



“I say people shouldn’t just go and pick them up, but the cats come to them naturally. They love the attention. It’s a win-win situation.”

And as a trio of moggies called Diesel, Fury and Garfield sidled over to join Mouse and enjoy some of my tasty treats, I realised that Liz was right.

It costs £6 an hour to hang out with the pets — or £4 if you are over 65.

There is something incredibly rewarding when cats — often renowned for being aloof and picky — choose to come and hang out with you.



“I also felt a great sense of pride when the moggies purred as I tickled them under the chin.

I realised I must have been doing something right.

Researchers have also found there is a huge reduction in the stress hormone cortisol when people interact with cats.

Prof Patricia Pendry, of Washington State University, branded the discovery “exciting, because it may, over time, have significant benefits for physical and mental health”.

In February 2025, another study found that cat owners who spent 15 minutes stroking, hugging or quietly holding their pets experienced higher levels of a happiness hormone called oxytocin.



Saliva tests showed the cats benefited in a similar way, as long as they were free to walk away whenever they wanted to.

And do not forget the purring.

Cats typically purr at frequencies between 20–140 Hz — a range found to have healing effects on things like pain and inflammation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

After spending a good 30 minutes in Mouse’s company, I felt more relaxed than I had in ages.

I suppose you could say I had the purr-fect day.

News.title: Four more UK cities consider banning ‘intimidating’ balaclavas as masked thugs wreak havoc on streets
News.content:
BALLY BANS Four more UK cities consider banning ‘intimidating’ balaclavas as masked thugs wreak havoc on streets







Next

FOUR more UK cities are considering banning balaclavas, as masked thugs wreak havoc on the streets.

Cops have said face coverings are hampering their efforts to identify potential offenders.



Officials in Newport, Coventry, Stafford and Wolverhampton are all mulling ways to strengthen existing powers to challenge those wearing balaclavas.

It comes after Nottingham introduced a ban in its city centre on September 15.



Nottinghamshire Police added that more than 180 city centre incidents involving face coverings or balaclavas had been identified between June 2025 and June 2026.

Jeweller Annette Farmer said she was “devastated” to move her shop online following two burglaries and a shoplifting incident involving people wearing balaclavas between June and August.

She told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast: “I didn’t feel safe any more.

“There are gangs hanging around with balaclavas.

“They’re on bikes as well, speeding around the city, speeding around the river front… just basically doing what they want.

“It’s intimidating, it’s frightening.”



Councillor David Fouweather said there had been incidents where residents had been left “feeling intimidated”, prompting the proposed ban on balaclavas.

Matthew Evans, one of two Newport councillor who had proposed the ban, said people wore “intimidating” face coverings to “rob, burgle and deal drugs in our city centre” and “avoid detection”.

He had proposed “exemptions for religious reasons” and added it was not an “attack on the human rights of young people”.

The move comes after a recent crackdown in a joint effort between the police and the local council.

Operation Krypton has led to hundreds of arrests.



Gwent Police’s Supt Esyr Jones said 321 arrests had been made since July to tackle crime and anti-social behaviour across Newport.

Newport Council said the current Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO) was up for review, “and any potential amendments can be considered as part of that process”.

It added the PSPO could potentially include face coverings “and this too is being explored in relation to its practical implication and legalities”.

However, it said there would be “exemptions for legitimate reasons, including religious, cultural, medical, occupational, weather or personal safety reasons”.

Cops in Nottingham are now allowed to ask people to remove their face covering if they “reasonably believe” they are being used to conceal their identity to commit crime or antisocial behaviour.



Anyone refusing to comply could face a fixed penalty notice of £70 or a maximum fine of £1,000.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said last month that it was “not the British way” after anti-migrant protesters in Dover covered their faces with masks and balaclavas.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has called for full face coverings, including those worn for religious reasons, to be banned in public.

News.title: If Healey dishes out a punishment beating to firms in Budget you can kiss goodbye to jobs and the high street
News.content:
No11 has to stop bashing business







Next

BRITAIN is drowning in taxes.

Employment tax, business tax and a tidal wave of personal taxation have crippled the economy, strangled growth and left millions of workers struggling to pay the bills.



In her two Budgets, Rachel Reeves put up taxes by £60billion to help pay for our £300billion welfare bill.

So it is any surprise that retail bosses are warning any new tax raid in Chancellor John Healey’s Budget could be the death knell for the high street?



M&S chief Stuart Machin said Reeves’ efforts were a “disaster”.

John Lewis chairman Jason Tarry warned further costs could lead to mass closures of stores.

Together these two employ almost 140,000 workers and their analysis comes from bitter experience.

They have seen the impact of extra business levies, National Insurance increases and the effects of Angela Rayner’s ruinous Employment Rights Act.

It is demonstrated by the fact that a single employee on £30,000 costs a British employer almost £2,000 more in tax than it does a similar boss in Florida.

Now the Chancellor is no mug.



John Healey knows the only route out of our economic mire is to generate growth.

The problem is Andy Burnham thinks you have to spend in order to get it.

Rather than leave growth to the free market, the deluded PM seems to favour a planned economy in a state-run socialist paradise.

This week Mr Healey will host nervous retail and hospitality bosses in Downing Street.

He must reassure them there will be no new business taxes when he delivers his Budget in just over two weeks.



Because dishing out a punishment beating to firms means one thing:

You can kiss goodbye to jobs, the high street and any chance of economic growth.

Open season

QUESTIONS are piling up for Andy Burnham over the Manchester City fiasco.

After The Sun’s revelation that Labour MPs received nearly £300,000 of UAE-funded freebies, the Tories demand all correspondence between ministers and officials at the scandal-hit club are made public.

The PM blundered in expressing “concern” for the owners of City amidst the widespread financial rule-breaking.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

So there must be total clarity about his dealings.

And as City resume their season today his silence will only increase the clamour for answers.

News.title: Celeb BBL doctor assassinated in Marbella clinic had been banned from practising in UK for 10 years
News.content:
BBL BAN Celeb BBL doctor assassinated in Marbella clinic had been banned from practising in UK for 10 years







Next

THE celebrity supercharged BBL surgeon shot dead in his Costa del Sol clinic this week had reportedly been banned from practising in UK a decade ago.

Brit-trained Dr Alexander Aslani, 57, who assassinated in front of horrified customers on Wednesday, could not legally work as a doctor in the UK despite 70 per cent of his customers jetting in from Britain.



Cops think he could have been killed by a contract killer believed to have been hired by a disgruntled ex-patient.

A report from the Olive Press uncovered that the surgeon was slammed with extensive working restrictions agreed with the General Medical Council (GMC) since 2012.



The GMC ordered Aslani to tackle six deficiencies: patient assessment, record keeping, patient consent, prescribing, “working within limits” and post-operative care.

He was barred from engaging in any medical work in the UK without written permission after surrendering his licence altogether four years later.

Aslani was then listed as registered without a licence – meaning he couldn’t legally work as a doctor in the UK.

The register does not reveal what caused the restrictions to be imposed, or why his licence was scrapped.

The Olive Press claimed he continued to teach and train UK surgeons after the ban.

A Swedish national, 18, was arrested 24 hours after the Marbella gun attack.



A disgruntled customer at the Cirumed Clinic reportedly sent threatening messages hours before the shooting.

On Friday night, local outlet Sur reported Aslani had gone to cops in April to complain he had been receiving “work-related” threats.

It was not clear whether he had pointed the finger at named individuals in his police statement or not.



It comes after The Sun revealed Aslani had been embroiled in a bitter High Court battle with an influencer who accused him of botching three operations.

Up to 70 per cent of his patients travelled from the UK, including Towie’s Chloe Sims and Love Island’s Hannah Elizabeth.

The figure emerged in a High Court judgment issued after Aslani sued a former patient who had undergone three Brazilian butt lift operations.

Influencer Paulina Sobierajska complained she needed reconstructive surgery and warned women considering using Aslani: “DON’T DO IT.”

Aslani successfully sued her for libel after she failed to defend the case.



Mr Justice Saini awarded him £40,000 damages in 2021, saying the sum reflected the “total falsity” of the allegations.

Other court records show one customer successfully sued the Brit-trained doctor for medical malpractice after an operation from him and inadequate follow-up care left her with an infection and a fistula, a tunnel between two organs.

Her lawyers said Dr Aslani failed to cut the fistula out after it was revealed by an ultrasound.

Aslani, the hospital he worked for and its insurers were ordered to pay £19,932.66 after a Spanish court ruled they had been medically negligent in 2018.

Another client raged online that Aslani had botched her BBL, claiming that just four weeks after surgery, one buttock was completely deflated.



A recipient of his speciality supercharged BBL wrote they woke up “in excruciating pain and could hardly move” after an op, but that staff at Aslani’s clinic “only seemed interested in obtaining pictures that could be used on Instagram”.

Investigators said the gunman entered the clinic with several customers inside and opened fire.

Dr Aslani was pronounced dead at the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tragically, the surgeon’s wife Jeannine, who was his director of nursing, was in the clinic when her husband was killed.

The shooter was reportedly dressed in black head-to-toe, fleeing on a motorbike driven by an accomplice.

News.title: Nine dead in horror Pennsylvania mass shooting including two children and pregnant woman
News.content:
Nine dead in horror Pennsylvania mass shooting including two children and pregnant woman

A local police chief said the city had never witnessed such 'loss of life and devastation' as he confirmed two children and a pregnant woman had been among the eight victims

View 3 Images Police said the eight victims included two children and a pregnant woman (Image: Getty Images)

Nine people have died, including two children and a pregnant woman, after a mass shooting at a family home.

‌



‌



Police in Erie, Pennsylvania said officers arrived on the scene on Friday evening to find two women dead outside. Inside the house, they found the bodies of a five-year-old boy, a one-year-old girl, two more women, two young men, and the shooter.

‌



Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said the 45-year-old male gunman was related to seven of the victims, while the eighth was a friend of the pregnant woman. CCTV footage showed two "distressed" women arriving at the home shortly before 5pm and banging on the door, he said, before the gunman shot them and returned inside.

‌



View 3 Images Firefighters were seen cleaning the scene after the mass shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump takes control of horror decision to live stream execution by firing squad READ MORE :

Detectives would now speak to the victims' relatives and go through their mobile phones to attempt to piece together a motive for the shooting, Chief Lorah said, adding: "They knew something was going on at that house - we have to figure out what that is."

The police chief had told a local news station earlier in the day: "I have not seen anything like this in my 28-plus years. I'm not sure that the city of Erie has ever seen the loss of life and the devastation that we just witnessed."

‌



Officers had received an alert about the incident via ShotSpotter, an app that uses AI and a network of microphones to identify and report gunshots.

View 3 Images Police were alerted to the incident by an AI gunshot detection app (Image: WJET via AP)

Governor Josh Shapiro said he had offered his administration's "full support" to Erie Mayor Daria Devlin.

‌



He wrote on X: "I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night, killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians. My heart breaks for this family. Lori and I are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community."

A statement issued by the City of Erie said: "We understand that this news brings deep shock and sorrow to our residents, and we want to assure the public that the situation has been contained.

"The shooter is deceased, and there is no ongoing threat or danger to the public at this time.

Article continues below

"Our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone impacted by tonight’s tragedy.

"We will continue working closely with our Erie Police Dept, and will provide updates as soon as verified information becomes available."

News.title: 'Told I'd never walk again after deadly crash, now I've broken world record'
News.content:
He was told he would never walk again after a horrific coach smash left him paralysed. But 36-year-old Paralympian Zach Washington-Young has become the first ever person with a spinal cord injury to swim the Strait of Gibraltar - the gruelling 15-mile stretch from Europe to Africa, across one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

And as he celebrated with a kiss from girlfriend, Juls Tobon, who was in the accompanying boat, the physical pain and deep torment of the last 14 years finally washed away. Zach said: "The elation as I drew close to the finish after four hours in the water to reach Africa was immense.

"I’ve always wanted to combine my physical recovery with my passion for being alive and turn the whole process into adventures, this was one of those moments."

Just a few weeks earlier, Zach suffered hypothermia after a practice swim in the Strait, which almost dashed his hopes of attempting the challenge.

‌



View 7 Images Zach during intensive rehab, following the horrific Bestival bus crash (Image: Collect Unknown)

The swim, completed last month, (Sept) showed Zach how far he had come since severing his spinal cord in a crash which claimed the lives of two of his friends and left him paralysed from the waist down.

He said: “Knowing that after everything I’d been through I was somehow able to swim between two continents made it really special. I reflected on the life I have now with Juls and my son, it made me really emotional.”

Zach was travelling home to Liverpool from Bestival music festival on the Isle of Wight in September 2012, when a tyre on the coach he was in exploded causing it to career off the road and crash into a tree. Then 22, Zach was thrown through the windscreen. His two friends, Michael Molloy, 18, and Kerry Ogden, 23, died instantly, along with the driver.

‌



Doctors were amazed that Zach survived the crash in Hindhead, Surrey, but repeatedly told him he would never walk again. He recalled: “The doctor said my injuries were so severe that if I walked again he would eat his tie, that stuck with me.”

View 7 Images After completing the Rock n Roll Half Marathon in Liverpool. (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Always a keen sportsman, making into Everton Football team as a young man and before the crash becoming an emerging talent in Mixed Martial Arts, Zach suddenly felt as if his whole world had collapsed.

He said: “I was so grateful to be alive but the news that I would spend the rest of my life in a wheelchair was devastating. I had been studying Law at Liverpool John Moores University. In an instant everything was taken away.”

‌



Zach’s mum, Emma, searched for a facility where her son could be helped towards his dream of walking again. And he spoke to Claire Lomas MBE, who had been paralysed after a fall at the Osberton Horse Trials.

Told she’d never walk again, she defied the odds, and pointed him towards PrimePhysio - a revolutionary rehab clinic near Cambridge where, in December 2014, he took his first steps. Sadly, Claire, who also completed the London Marathon, died from injuries sustained in a microlight crash in August 2024, while filming for an Apple commissioned series in Jordan.

View 7 Images Zach competes in the Men's MC 400m Freestyle during Day Three of the Citi Para Swimming World Series in 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Zach used equipment including an exoskeleton suit and a DEN2X stimulation machine, which made his paralysed muscles contract, creating healthier muscle tissue. In November 2015, he did a one mile walk around a lake with a Zimmer frame.

‌



Then he completed the Liverpool Half Marathon in 2017 on crutches. And, in 2018, ran the London Marathon on crutches - then summiting Mount Snowden in 2020.

Then he asked Paralympian royalty Ellie Simmonds’ coach, Billy Pye MBE, to train him. He said: “I’d always loved swimming and I approached Billy Pye at an event and asked him to train me. It was an amazing experience training with Ellie and Billy at 5:30am, I couldn’t believe that I was training with the best of the best.

“In the water I felt free and in 2021 I went for a trial and was offered a place with Team GB. After everything that had happened, I finally felt as if things were going my way. I swam freestyle and was 12th in the world in the 400m freestyle.”

View 7 Images Zach, his son Chance and partner Juls

‌



During this time, Zach had a chance meeting with Juls, as he checked in at the airport in Tenerife. He said: “I saw this beautiful woman behind me and I kept seeing her in the airport. As fate would have it, we were seated next to each other on the flight to Barcelona, but I was shy and didn’t speak to her, even though I really wanted to.

"As we made our way through the airport, we ended up in a lift together and began chatting. We shared a taxi into the city and I asked her out on a date the next night. We hit it off and have been inseparable ever since.

“When I found out Juls was pregnant, it was a big shock as I was training hard for GB and knew I’d have another job on my hands then. I had always been told that it would be impossible to have a child naturally, but I could try IVF. Once it sunk in that she had conceived naturally, I realised how amazing it really was.

“We named our son Chance, as that is our story. He is a miracle and the chances of him existing were so small, almost impossible odds. To have gone from that place of no hope back in the dark days after the accident, to walking the London Marathon, swimming for Team GB, meeting Juls and having a son, was just unbelievable.”

‌



View 7 Images Happy families: Zach, little Chance and Juls

His son, Chance, waved him off from the beach at Tarifa for his latest challenge and his actor dad, Peter Washington, was also in the boat accompanying him.

Zach said: “The swim from Europe to Africa was my latest endeavour. After the hypothermia, I did feel as if I may not be able to do it and I even went in the boat on another swim someone else was doing, so I could feel the water, as I was told the first 45 minutes is the coldest and then it warms up.

“I wanted to know what I was letting myself in for after the shock of hypothermia. I kept my energy up by eating mashed sweet potato with pear every hour, dates, coconut water, and warm tea with honey. It’s important to keep the blood sugar levels up when you’re dealing with cold temperatures.”

‌



Zach has also sold the rights to his life story to a production company, with a film now in development to tell his inspirational story. He is now planning on setting up the ZWY Spinal Foundation to help others in a similar position. He said: “I found it so hard to get the help I needed, so I want to help others achieve what I have.”

View 7 Images Zach during his record breaking Gibraltar swim

Zach said his next goal is to be able to walk unaided without any crutches and says he is willing to go to America to try stem cell therapy to achieve that.

“I want to be able to do things with my son without limits,” he explained. I’d also love to do a cycle challenge and go from Lands End to John O’Groats, I’d need to adapt a bike with stabilisers and then who knows, I believe anything is possible if you really apply yourself. I’m always challenging myself, I love to do things with a sense of adventure and the feeling of being truly alive.

‌



“Everyday when I wake up I take a few minutes in gratitude to appreciate that I’m still here, I have a scar on my right hand side, which is the side Michael, Kerry and the driver Colin were on, every time I look at it, it reminds me how close I came to not making it.

“Surviving gave me another shot at life and I’m determined to make the most of it and not waste a second.”

News.title: How hero Yorkshire Wildlife Park zookeepers ended tiger's fatal attack on man who 'jumped into enclosure'
News.content:
How hero Yorkshire Wildlife Park zookeepers ended tiger's fatal attack on man who 'jumped into enclosure'

Disturbing footage posted online appeared to show the victim standing inside the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster while pointing at a tiger

View 9 Images The scene at Yorkshire Wildlife Park which was evacuated and closed after the incident (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

Horrified families screamed in terror as a man was mauled to death in a zoo's tiger enclosure today.

‌



‌



Disturbing footage posted online appeared to show the victim standing inside the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster while pointing at a tiger. He was seen being bitten and shoved around by the big cat while crying out “no, no” and "back", as visitors desperately shouted from a viewing gantry in a bid to distract the animal.

‌



One male onlooker was heard exclaiming “Jesus Christ”, while a woman was heard saying: “I tried to stop him”. She was also heard telling a fellow witness: “Don't look,” as the horror continued.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 9 Images Altai, one of Yorkshire Wildlife Park's Amur Tigers, pictured there last year (Image: Yorkshire Wildlife Park / SWNS)

Hurricane Isaias tears through US with horror 120mph winds and three confirmed dead READ MORE :

Hero keepers later managed to scare the animal away by firing several gunshots into the air, causing it to flee to a nearby hide. It was left uninjured.

‌



Visitor Tia Hanson said: "It looks as if someone has jumped into the enclosure. There were loads of police and ambulance people and a stretcher in the enclosure as well. It wasn’t nice - there were lots of people who looked really upset. They put up all sort of black tarpaulin so you couldn’t really see."

View 9 Images Police at the scene this afternoon (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

Police and ambulance workers rushed to the scene before a “black screen” was later erected around the enclosure. An insider said: "Shots were fired into the air to make a noise and distract the tiger. The animal wasn't shot and is absolutely fine and not injured.

‌



"The barriers are huge. You would have to really want to get inside the enclosure to be able to do it. From start to end the incident was over within minutes. The keepers did everything they could. It's horrific."

View 9 Images The scene at Yorkshire Wildlife Park (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, was on a family day out when staff told them the park was being evacuated. She said: "We were in a lemur enclosure and somebody asked us to start leaving. Then, all of a sudden, we were being ushered further and further into the park."

‌



She said she had then heard several gunshots before a helicopter began circling. She said: "That's when we started thinking, 'Oh, something's happened'."

A woman who was visiting the park with her husband and two children, aged six and three, described seeing blood where the tiger had dragged the man as visitors shouted in a bid to distract the animal.

View 9 Images The park was evacuated earlier today (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

‌



"You could see the blood where the tiger had dragged the man. Someone who saw it said it had him by the neck," midwife Amy Wright, 36, told The Sun. "There was a lot of blood. People were shouting to try and distract it."

Doncaster Mayor Ros Jones said in a statement she was "deeply saddened to hear of the tragic incident that has taken place today at Yorkshire Wildlife Park". She added: "My thoughts and prayers are with all those involved at this immensely difficult time."

Yorkshire Wildlife Park was opened in April 2009. In 2011, its Land of the Tigers’ attraction opened allowing visitors to view the cats from a 300 meter-long raised walkway above the enclosure. The park has two Amur tigers, a 17-stone female called Tschuna and a male called Altai, who only arrived in March last year.

‌



View 9 Images Police rushed to the park before closing off the entrance to the park on Saturday afternoon (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

A statement on the park's website said: “We can confirm a serious incident has occurred at the tiger enclosure. Our emergency response procedures were immediately activated.

“We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened. The safety and wellbeing of our visitors, staff and animals remain our highest priority The park is now closed and will remain closed tomorrow..”

‌



A South Yorkshire Police spokesman said: “At 1.35pm today (Saturday 10 October) we received reports of a man entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.

View 9 Images Police at the park's entrance (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

"The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury. Emergency services attended and sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



"The man's family is aware and is being supported by specialist officers. Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time. Regarding rumours surrounding the condition of the tiger, the animal was uninjured and remained in the enclosure following the incident and there is no wider risk to the public.

View 9 Images Witnesses said a “black screen” was erected around the tiger enclosure after the horror (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

"Following the incident, Yorkshire Wildlife Park was evacuated and officers remain on scene carrying out enquiries."

‌



A Yorkshire Air Ambulance spokesperson said: “We can confirm that Yorkshire Air Ambulance was dispatched to an incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park today, alongside other ambulance resources."

View 9 Images A black screen was erected around the tiger enclosure (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

The horror comes after a three-year-old boy was seriously injured after being thrown into a crocodile enclosure back in July. The boy was visiting Johnsons of Old Hurst, near Huntingdon in Cambridgeshire, on 18 June when he ended up in the crocodile enclosure before being attacked.

Article continues below

A 30-year-old man from Norfolk, understood to have learning difficulties, was later arrested on suspicion of attempted murder following the incident and was later bailed as police said he was “assessed as not being fit for interview”.

News.title: 'The royals don't just cost us - they work for us - and let's be honest, we come out ahead'
News.content:
Every few months, like clockwork, someone in Westminster rediscovers the Sovereign Grant and demands to know what we get for our money.

This week it's Lord Foulkes, who will tell the Lords that Britain has the most expensive monarchy in Europe and that the public is being short-changed.

But let us first at least hear him out. Yes, the Sovereign Grant is close to £100 million a year. Nobody at the Palace pretends otherwise, and in a cost-of-living squeeze that affects the majority of us, it's right that it's scrutinised. But it's what the peer leaves out that tells the real story.

The Sovereign Grant is not a cheque written from general taxation. It is a slice of the profits of the Crown Estate, the vast portfolio of property, farmland and seabed that the monarch hands to the Treasury at the start of every reign.

‌



That deal dates back to 1760. The Crown Estate now makes well over a billion pounds in profit, and the lion's share goes straight to the Exchequer to pay for hospitals, schools and, yes, you guessed it, peers' expenses.

View 3 Images King Charles has been at the forefront of creating a slimmed down monarchy fit for the modern age (Image: Getty Images)

The grant is a fraction of what the Crown hands over. Any other business that returned that much to its shareholders would be hailed as a triumph.

Then there's the work. Lord Foulkes sneers at "ribbon-cutting". But ask the thousands of charities with a royal patron what that ribbon is worth.

‌



A royal visit means headlines, donations, volunteers and a morale boost no advertising budget could buy. I have seen it first hand countless times.

The King's Trust began life as the Prince's Trust in 1976, funded by the King's own navy severance pay, and has helped well over a million young people into work, training and education. Few politicians can point to anything they've built that has changed so many lives.

Prince William's Earthshot Prize has become one of the biggest environmental awards in the world, backing practical solutions rather than speeches.

And the Princess of Wales has spent more than a decade championing early childhood, because she understands that the first five years shape everything that follows. It's long-term, unglamorous work, exactly what we usually complain our politicians won't do.

‌



View 3 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales visited Belfast this week (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

As for the jets and the homes, it's a fair question about optics, and the Palace knows it. But many of those properties are held in trust for the nation rather than owned personally, and they are the backdrop for state visits, investitures and diplomacy that bring in trade and goodwill.

Lord Foulkes wants "strict audit and productivity metrics". Splendid. Let's audit the lot: the Crown Estate returns, the millions raised for good causes, the soft power no ambassador can match. And while we're at it, let's have a proper run on what value for money those Lords give us.

I suspect the family would pass with flying colours. The royals don't just cost us. They work for us, and on any honest reckoning, we come out ahead.

News.title: Hurricane Isaias tears through US with horror 120mph winds and three confirmed dead
News.content:
Three people have died and hundreds of thousands left without power as Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the US.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis urged residents to remain indoors and avoid unnecessary travel amid a "hazardous situation" in the state, where high winds, isolated tornadoes and flooding are expected to continue today.

"The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don't be getting out on the roads", he said, as photographs showed homes and businesses battered by the storm and falling debris.

Authorities in the state confirmed that a woman had died after a tree fell on her house amid peak winds of 120mph, with two more casualties confirmed in Alabama on Saturday.

‌



Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after botched execution in major update READ MORE :

View 5 Images Trees crashed into homes in the worst-hit areas across the southeastern US (Image: DAN ANDERSON/EPA/Shutterstock)

Kay Ivey, governor of Alabama, said: "This storm brought in heavy winds throughout Alabama, taking down trees, knocking out power and doing some damage. Unfortunately, we have also learned that two Alabamians have lost their lives. I am praying for their loved ones this morning."

Around 840,000 people remained without power across the southeastern US on Saturday after winds hit substations and downed power lines overnight.

View 5 Images Over 800,000 people have been left without power (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The Gulf Coast Electric Cooperative utility company said they had been temporarily forced to halt efforts to restore power, as conditions had become too dangerous for work to be carried out.

A statement read: "Unfortunately, weather conditions have deteriorated to the point that, for the safety of our crews, we must temporarily suspend outage restoration efforts until conditions improve and it is safe to resume work. We understand how frustrating it is to be without power, and we sincerely appreciate patience and understanding".

View 5 Images The storm will bring more flooding as it heads inland, authorities warned (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Emergency alerts had been sent to phones across Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi ahead of the hurricane warning residents to "take cover now".

‌



The National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned that the remnants of Isaias would continue to produce torrential tropical downpours and strong winds as the storm moves north through Alabama and Georgia.

View 5 Images Huge waves were also witnessed in California as Tropical Storm Rachel approached (Image: Jake Lee Green/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

It marks the beginning of the North American hurricane season, which has begun later than usual due to the effects of the El Nino weather phenomenon.

Large waves began lashing beaches in southern California on Saturday ahead of the impending Tropical Storm Rachel, while Hurricane Simon - expected to become a severe Category 4 storm - will make landfall on the eastern coast of Mexico on Sunday.

News.title: Trump blasts Zelensky and demands Ukraine 'gets leader who can make a deal'
News.content:
Trump blasts Zelensky and demands Ukraine 'gets leader who can make a deal'

Trump was accused of betraying Ukraine after cutting a deal with Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel to America, in a bid to drive down prices ahead of next month's Midterm elections

View Image Trump and Zelensky earlier this month at the United Nations General Assembly (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump has demanded Volodymyr Zelensky be replaced, claiming Ukraine's president failed to "settle" the war.

‌



‌



It comes after the US President was accused of betraying Ukraine yesterday after cutting a deal with Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel to America, in a bid to drive down prices ahead of next month's Midterm elections

‌



Trump made the shocking remarks as he left the White House to travel to Texas for a political rally.

‌



He said "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal,″ adding that "for some reason [Zelensky] never does."

Andy Burnham spoke on the with President Zelensky today, and reiterated the UK's support for Ukraine.

A Downing Street spokesperson said: “The Prime Minister began by recognising the last 24 hours had been difficult for Ukraine and reiterated his complete solidarity.

‌



“The two leaders next discussed the importance of maintaining pressure on Russia: the Prime Minister made it clear that the UK would continue to strengthen its sanctions on Russia and to take further action to constrain the Russian war machine, building on new UK designations against Russian targets announced this week.

“They underlined that Russia should agree to an immediate energy ceasefire, ending its brutal strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure and its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea. This would immediately release more energy and food supplies into the global market.

“The two leaders agreed to meet in person in the coming days to continue their discussion.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Asked if he was concerned his deal with Russia would prolong the war, Trump said: "I see it a little differently. Zelensky could have settled this war many times...and he chooses not to."

Zelensky "settling" the war, as Trump puts it, would involve ceding territory illegally invaded by Russia.

‌



He added: "We said 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries, because that's a world problem that's caused."

In an apparent bid to link Ukraine defending itself against Russia to the midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is expected to suffer heavy losses, Trump went on: "He wants to make problems for the world.

"He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel. Because Russia supplies the diesel fuel throughout the world. And we told him 'do whatever you want, but don't hit the diesel fuel...and what does he do? He goes and hits refineries.

Article continues below

"He'd better damn well stop."

Asked about the daily suffering of the Ukrainian people from Russian rocket attacks, Trump said: "I agree with you. Do you know what I suggest? I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal."

He added: "You've lost 30% of your country and you've had over a million people killed. Between the two of them over 2m people killed. That's a war that should have never started, and I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new President."

News.title: 'Spineless MPs have failed to tackle Royal Family's gravy train as your bills go up'
News.content:
'Spineless MPs have failed to tackle Royal Family's gravy train as your bills go up'

Writing for The Mirror, author and former Lib Dem MP Norman Baker has criticised the government for approving a £100million-a-year Sovereign Grant for the Royal Family

View 2 Images The Sovereign Grant settlement handed to the Royal Family will be £99.7million next year (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

Times are tight. Your bills for heating, for food and for fuel may be soaring, but that won’t worry the royals who have just been given yet another bumper pay rise by the government and will – kerching - now get a handout of £100 million a year.

‌



‌



And that’s after we have spent £359 million on a no-expense-spared upgrade of Buckingham Palace, only for Charles to say he has decided not to live there.

‌



The last year of the Civil List, the predecessor to the current Sovereign Grant, was held in check by Gordon Brown and gave the royals £7.9 million in 2011. Overall our bloated royals are now costing us about HALF A BILLION a year.

‌



Majority of voters want funding for royals slashed after £50m hike in three years READ MORE :

View 2 Images Former Lib Dem MP Norman Baker has criticised the government (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

Successive governments have tried to stop MPs debating royal matters. And MPs are restricted by the rules of parliamentary procedure from criticising the royals.

Just to make sure, each MP when elected has to swear an oath of true allegiance to the monarch, and their heirs and successors, before they can take their seat. These heirs and successors, by the way, include in the top ten the disgraced Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, and the opted-out Prince Harry.

‌



But earlier this month, for the first time in 15 years, MPs were given a chance to scrutinise royal finances. By law the government had to introduce an amendment to push through this big increase, but did their best to smother it as much as possible.

They scheduled the debate at short notice for the first day back after the recess, and as late towards midnight as possible. They needn’t have worried. Very few MPs showed up and almost no questions were asked. With the chancellor scrabbling round to find any spare cash to help deliver the promised “breathing space” for people, you might think MPs would have tried to put a brake on this royal gravy train, even if the chancellor was prepared to wave it on.

You might have thought the Tories, who are so keen to cut benefits for the poorest amongst us, would have had something to say about the huge benefit bill for the royals, but no. Sadly, our MPs have backbones like chocolate eclairs when it comes to the monarchy.

‌



Maybe the culture of institutional deference intimidates them. Or perhaps the lure of rubbing shoulders with our unelected royals at garden parties is just too much of a pull.

And so we look to the Lords, who tend to show rather more independence and who will have their chance to have a say on the matter next week. But wait. The government has decided that the amendment to the law is a “money Bill,” meaning the Lords are unable to vote to reduce the massive increase.

They can only express their views, which the government will then ignore. Meanwhile don’t be surprised if the royals are quietly raising a glass or two of expensive wine to toast out craven MPs.

News.title: Labour peer to launch blistering attack on royals over £100m grant from taxpayers
News.content:
Labour peer to launch blistering attack on royals over £100m grant from taxpayers

EXCLUSIVE: This week former Cabinet minister Lord George Foulkes will tell the House of Lords the royal family do not offer value for money as he criticises the £100m Sovereign Grant

View 2 Images The Sovereign Grant will be set at nearly £100million next year (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

A Labour peer will launch a blistering attack on the Royals this week as he calls for the King's public funding to be slashed.

‌



‌



Former Cabinet member Lord George Foulkes will argue the public is not getting value for the £100million it is set to hand over next year. He told The Mirror he was incensed by the monarch's use of private jets and helicopters and questioned why the family needs so many homes while making public statements on homelessness.

‌



On Wednesday he will tell peers that the UK has by far the most expensive state-funded monarchy in Europe as he argues the Sovereign Grant is too high. The government's Sovereign Grant Bill - which sets the amount the royals receive - will get a second reading in the House of Lords on Wednesday.

‌



The former Scotland Secretary will tell peers: "When we ask the public to fund an institution to the tune of over just under £100 million a year through the Sovereign Grant, at a time when many are facing severe pressure on their household budgets, we have a duty to ask two fundamental questions - are we getting value for money, and do the actions of this institution match the values it preaches?

"I would argue that the answer to both is no."

Blow to Nigel Farage as Reform sheds over 50 newly-elected councillors in five months READ MORE :

View 2 Images Former Cabinet member Lord George Foulkes will hit out this week (Image: FILE)

‌



Lord Foulkes will add: "While European neighbours have streamlined their royal houses, we continue to fund a sprawling network of 'working royals' whose ribbon-cutting duties would, in any other sector, face strict audit and productivity metrics."

The grant is an annual payment to fund the monarch's official duties, such as overseas trips. The payment - based on profits from the Crown Estate - also covers the cost of palace maintenance and employing staff.

King Charles will be given £99.9million by the Treasury in the next financial year. This is down from £137.9million because a decade-long, £369million refurbishment of Buckingham Palace is finished.

‌



But the sum is three times the £31million awarded when the Sovereign Grant was created by Tory austerity Chancellor George Osborne in 2012/13.

Defending the rise, Treasury minister Dan Tomlinson last month said the royals are carrying out more engagements than under the final years of the late Queen. He said they must be adequately funded for their duties.

Lord Foulkes told The Mirror: "They talk a lot about climate change, yet I've seen lots of criticism about the number of private jets and helicopter flights that they use for short journeys.

‌



"That's pretty hypocritical. Then the Prince of Wales has got a major campaign on homelessness, but they've got so many empty and underutilised properties all across the country. Why do they need so many houses? That's a rather embarrassing contrast."

The peer will call for MPs to carry out a full review of royal financial arrangements - and for greater transparency. He will tell peers that Spain’s public grant to its royals is roughly £7million, Sweden’s under £15million, while the Netherlands sits around £45million. "In terms of value for money, our monarchy remains, by a vast margin, the most expensive state-funded royal family in Europe," he will say - suggesting the allocation should be halved.

In July a YouGov poll found 68% of Brits believe King Charles is doing a good job.

‌



In the year to March 31, the royal annual financial report showed £5.1million was spent on travel, £33.7million on payroll and £3.5million on housekeeping and hospitality. Property maintenance totalled £67.5million.

Nearly £127,000 was spent on travel for the King and Queen to make an official visit to Rome last April. Documents show £733,000 was spent on 177 helicopter flights over 12 months. And 60 charter flights cost £837,000 in that time.

In September Mr Tomlinson told MPs: “The new level of the grant will ensure that the Royal Household can continue to deal with property maintenance backlogs following some years of constrained funding during the pandemic.

‌



“It will also allow the Royal Household to replace ageing systems to strengthen cybersecurity and to install energy-efficient heating systems.”

He said the grant must make sure the royals are funded adequately for their duties, stating: “And it is worth pointing out, of course, that those activities have increased significantly in recent years.

“Towards the end of her reign, the late Queen was not carrying out a large number of foreign engagements, and also was hosting a smaller number of state visits.

‌



“The King has increased the engagements that he is carrying out on our behalf as part of his public duties, and that has involved more expenditure in terms of staff costs and making sure that those engagements and the benefits that in terms of the representation of our country and supporting good causes here in the UK can get the funding and the support that they need.”

The grant is set each year by the Royal Trustees - comprising the Prime Minister, the Chancellor, and the Keeper of the Privy Purse.

Under a deal reached during the coalition Government, the grant is calculated based on the profit of the Crown Estate. In the past decade, over £5billion of profits from the Crown Estate have been paid to the Exchequer.

Article continues below

Keeper of the Privy Purse, James Chalmers, said: “This is not a blank cheque. Expenditure is governed by the same standards and disciplines as any publicly funded body, with strict value-for money requirements, detailed planning, multi-year strategies, independent audit, and Treasury oversight.”

News.title: Man dies after tiger attack at wildlife park
News.content:
A man has died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have confirmed.

South Yorkshire Police said it had been called at 13:35 BST to reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster. The tiger then attacked the man and he died at the scene, the force said.

His family had been informed and were being supported by officers, it added.

A park spokesperson said: "We are deeply saddened by today's tragic incident. Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies are with the family and loved ones of the person who has lost their life."

They added: "We are working closely with the police and relevant authorities and would ask that the privacy of those affected is respected at this extremely difficult time. The park will remain closed tomorrow."

Police said the tiger was uninjured, remained in the enclosure following the incident and there had been no wider risk to the public.

The park was evacuated and officers remain at the scene.

The force added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage."

Earlier, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".

News.title: Sara Sharif's grandfather granted guardianship of her siblings in Pakistan
News.content:
Sara Sharif's paternal grandfather has been granted guardianship of her siblings by a court in Pakistan.

The decision comes after years of legal limbo following the murder of 10-year-old Sara by her father and stepmother in 2023.

All five children, who are now aged between 16 and four, have been living in Pakistan since 2023. They were asked to speak to the judge in court, where the eldest said they were comfortable and the siblings were settled.

Sara's grandfather, Muhammed Sharif, told the BBC he was relieved to be granted guardianship after three years of legal battles, saying his hope is that the children "stay healthy" and receive "a good education".

"It is my responsibility to ensure they get the best possible education and care," he said.

When told by the judge that the grandfather would become their guardian, the eldest child responded saying "that's all good".

The five children have been in Pakistan since August 2023, when they were brought to the country by Sara's father, stepmother and uncle after Sara was killed.

The family was in hiding for weeks before the children were discovered by police at the grandfather's house. They were initially put into state childcare.

The adults flew back to the UK and were arrested at the airport. Sara's father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool were found guilty of Sara's murder. Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison and Batool received a minimum of 33 years.

Her uncle, Faisal Malik, was found guilty of causing or allowing her death and given a 16-year sentence.

Sara had been hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in Woking, Surrey.

News.title: King warns malicious online actors are evolving tactics
News.content:
King Charles III has warned of the challenges disinformation and other "hostile online activity" pose to trust and security in the digital age.

The comments, made in a letter to the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to mark its 10th anniversary, spoke of "malicious actors" continuing to "evolve their tactics by using automated technologies".

"From threats to our international order, to the need to balance the risks and opportunities of powerful new technologies, strong cyber security is fundamental to making the online environment safer and more resilient," he wrote.

Last month, the King warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.

In the letter published on Saturday by NCSC, the King praised the government agency. He said its achievements over the past decade have included defending the country against cyber attacks, safeguarding democratic institutions and protecting "the critical infrastructure upon which daily life depends".

"You have built resilience across our public services, businesses and communities, equipping us all to prosper in our ever-evolving digital world," the monarch added.

The King said he was "acutely aware" that much of the work done by the NCSC cannot be praised publicly and that he was filled with "profound gratitude".

The NCSC was established in 2016 as part of the Government Communications Headquarters to protect the UK against cyber threats.

Earlier this week, the NCSC offered assistance to online shopping store Asos after customers received a notification from its app sent by hackers, the BBC understands.

The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people.

Asos said it was investigating "unauthorised activity" involving third-party platforms. The company told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the company's users - including names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth.

It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

The letter from the King to NCSC came after he spoke to AI executives at Dumfries House in Ayrshire last month on how the tech can be used to benefit security.

News.title: Northern Lights stun UK down to England's south coast
News.content:
Residents across the UK were left stunned as the sky was illuminated by the spectacular colours of the Northern Lights on Friday and Saturday evenings.

The natural phenomenon, known as the Aurora Borealis, is the result of increased solar activity.

Such occurrences are mostly visible near the Arctic Circle and northern Scotland, but particularly strong activity levels meant they could be seen as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent on Saturday night.

The Met Office has said sightings could continue to be possible during clear skies until Tuesday.

News.title: Ashe was too scared to cancel her wedding, then her story became a hit song
News.content:
No songwriter is ever off duty. And for the US pop singer Ashe, that included her wedding day.

Last October, she was getting ready to tie the knot at a gorgeous hilltop ceremony in Nashville when inspiration struck.

As she watched her family gather, the musician flashed back to her first wedding, almost a decade earlier. The contrast was stark.

She's called that first marriage "horrifying". Her ex, who she met in college, was, she says, emotionally manipulative and psychologically abusive.

He had insisted on a beachfront wedding, which sounds romantic until you learn that Ashe has a fear of the ocean.

In the run-up, she had been tempted to call it off, but felt powerless to stand up for herself.

On her second wedding day, she realised the opposite was true.

"I'm in a happy, healthy relationship and I have total autonomy over my own life," says the singer, now in her early 30s.

"I thought, if this didn't feel right, I could totally put a halt to the whole thing. I definitely didn't have that first time around."

As she adjusted her veil and prepared to walk down the aisle, she filed that feeling away.

Two months later, and back at work, the idea resurfaced and a song spilled out.

Its name? Stop the Wedding.

It unfolds like a movie scene. Ashe pleads with her younger self to trust her instincts.

"You know how you really feel / You don't have to waste your life," she sings, as the wedding band stutters to an uncertain halt.

"Do I wish I'd had that advice at the time? 1,000 per cent," Ashe says.

"If someone had given me the insight that I was not stuck, and that I could run, I could have changed things sooner. Maybe not at the altar. Maybe weeks before â but it was something I really could have used."

What about the line where she pledges to "burn the wedding dress and run away"?

"I didn't burn my dress," she laughs, "but I did get into a bathtub with it for a photoshoot right after I left my ex-husband, which really ruined it!"

News.title: I couldn't access my family's medical history - not knowing was terrifying
News.content:
When Aaliyah found a lump in her breast, she was anxious to find out if she had inherited an increased risk of cancer.

But because she had been removed from her biological parents at the age of seven months and later adopted, she had no way of accessing her family medical history.

"Not knowing anything about yourself genetically is terrifying," says the 26-year-old, "you can't even begin to imagine it."

The lump turned out to be non-cancerous, but it was one of many occasions when she found herself unable to answer questions about her biological family's health.

Aaliyah, now a trainee solicitor, spent years trying to source information from local authorities and eventually made an official data access request to Bradford Council, which removed her from her biological family as a baby.

She says the whole process took its toll.

"I would say bureaucratic hellscape is an understatement," she admits.

News.title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago, why are they resuming now?
News.content:
They came in their thousands from near and far. Men, women and children lined up on a Kentucky riverfront for the public hanging of a black man convicted of raping and killing an elderly white widow.

It was 14 August 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky, a sweltering Friday in the middle of a legendary heatwave. Some slept overnight near the gallows to preserve their spots. Others held "necktie" parties the previous evening, arriving hungover as teenagers sold popcorn and soda to spectators.

By the execution time of 05:00, the crowd had swelled to an estimated 20,000.

That's when Rainey Bethea, an orphan in his 20s, stepped up to the gallows - sentenced to death after allegedly confessing to robbing, raping and killing Lischia Edwards, 70.

The previous afternoon, he'd eaten a last meal of fried chicken, pork chops, mashed potatoes, pickled cucumbers, cornbread, lemon pie and ice cream.

Many of those gathered - including press from as far away as Chicago and New York - came to see the rumoured "Lady Executioner". The local sheriff had died four months earlier and his widow had become his unlikely replacement.

She declined to pull the trip lever herself, however, and it was a hired hangmen who instead sent Bethea to his death.

That moment marked the last high-profile public hanging in the US. The circus surrounding Bethea's death embarrassed many in Kentucky and the governor outlawed public executions 18 months later.

By then, most states had abolished capital punishment in view of the masses as societal attitudes sought more humane and private methods. Another hanging was attended by a few hundred in Missouri in 1937, but that was lesser known and marked America's final public execution - until now.

News.title: Afrobeats singer Ayra Starr on making history at her NFL half-time show in London
News.content:
Afrobeats singer Ayra Starr has already broken numerous records, and her NFL half-time performance this weekend is set to level up her list again.

The Nigerian star will become the first African artist to headline one of the American football league's international games when the Philadelphia Eagles take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Ahead of the performance at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Starr told BBC Newsbeat her history-making performance "itself is a message".

Earlier this year, Puerto Rican superstar Bad Bunny used his Super Bowl half-time show to celebrate Latin American culture.

The 32-year-old also made history by becoming the first musician to perform entirely in Spanish at the sporting event, normally the most-watched each year on US TV.

Starr said it's "very important" for singers to seize opportunities like this.

"At the end of the day, as artists, we speak for the culture and we speak for the people that listen to us," she added.

"And we have to represent any way that seems fit, that they need."

She didn't want to give away too much about her performance, but confirmed it would feature tracks from her new studio album, Starrgirl, which was released in August.

"Sunday is gonna be amazing," she said.

"I'm still in rehearsals. It's a lot of work we're putting in so I'm really excited."

News.title: Head of Met's volunteer force fired after AI tool found deleted intimate images on work phone
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has fired the head of its Special Constabulary after Palantir's AI monitoring uncovered that he had used his work phone to copy intimate images of a woman.

Special chief officer James Deller, who led the force's volunteer officers, was dismissed following a misconduct hearing on Friday.

The Met said investigators used lawful business monitoring and Palantir's Foundry system, which uses artificial intelligence (AI), to find the misconduct by Deller.

Cdr Pete Stevens said: "SCO Deller failed to meet that bar. His actions were an abuse of the trust put in him and it is right that he is no longer able to serve in policing."
