Investigators found that in July and August 2025, Deller used his police-issued phone to take photos of two intimate images that had been sent to his personal phone.

The pictures had been sent using WhatsApp's "view once" feature, which makes them disappear after they are opened.

He then sent the copied images back to his personal device before deleting them from his work phone.

The misconduct was discovered during a week-long operation called Project Galatasaray, which used the AI technology in a bid to identify corruption and professional misconduct within the Met.

Deller will be added to the College of Policing's barred list, meaning he will not be able to serve in policing again.

Stevens added: "The vast majority of Met officers and staff serve London with dedication and integrity, and they rightly expect robust action against the small minority who abuse their position and undermine public trust.

"That is particularly true of those who serve in the Special Constabulary. They are volunteers who selflessly give up their time to keep London safe.

"They deserve to be led by people who demonstrate the highest standards in all parts of their lives."

News.title: Green Party MP wants to make sure it is 'not vulnerable to extremists'
News.content:
A Green Party MP has said her party needs to make sure it is not "vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists" after members voted for a motion that claimed Zionism was racism.

The motion put forward by activists, which became formal policy after it was approved at the Green's conference earlier this month, has divided senior party figures and been criticised by Jewish groups.

Westminster leader Ellie Chowns told the BBC it was a "significant and damaging policy" and she would work to reform the Green Party.

It comes after ex-leader Caroline Lucas said it was not being protected from entryism - where people sign up to a party to try to change it.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today Programme on Saturday, Chowns said: "I don't know if there are extremists and racists in my party. But I want to make sure that my party isn't vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists."

The MP described Zionism as a "contested concept" and said the motion did not represent the views of the large majority of Green Party members, "nor of people in the country".

Chowns said the motion would be a "distraction from the very important work" the party has been doing campaigning for Palestinian rights.

She added: "I think it is clear that if we have policy, such significant and damaging policy, made by a vote of just 0.4% of our members, that something isn't working in our structures and our policy-making process."

Members of the Green Party of England and Wales endorsed the policy motion by 1,022 votes to 813.

There are 230,000 members of the Green party overall and not everyone attended the conference.

The policy also backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.

It defines Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state".

The Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council, which criticised the motion, said: "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it."

News.title: Drumcree parade ban was in 'best interests of peace', says Bryant
News.content:
The Northern Ireland secretary of state has said his decision to ban the contentious Orange Order Drumcree parade "was in the best interests of peace".

The decision on Friday came after agreement couldn't be reached between the Portadown District Lodge and the Garvaghy Road residents over whether the march would be allowed down the predominantly nationalist road.

Sir Chris Bryant said he received advice from the PSNI chief constable that allowing the procession to go ahead could lead to serious injury, disorder and wider unrest.

On Saturday, a legal challenge by Orangemen against the decision to ban the parade was adjourned until Monday after the judge said it was not an "emergency" case.

The stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland, with stand-offs in the mid-to-late 1990s accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

The Parades Commission was established in 1998 to regulate contentious processions.

Its decisions restricting the Drumcree march have been challenged by the Orange Order for decades.

Earlier this year, a court overturned the commission's original decision to stop the parade, ruling it could go ahead, with restrictions on 27 September.

But Garvaghy Road residents blocked the road that morning, preventing the Orangemen from marching, and a stand-off has continued for almost two weeks.

The Court of Appeal has reserved judgment on a legal challenge brought by Garvaghy Road residents against the decision to allow the march.

Sir Chris said he had spent almost two weeks trying to broker a deal and believed the two sides had come close to an agreement.

He said two outcomes were discussed. One would have allowed the Orangemen to complete one final march along the Garvaghy Road, on the condition it would not apply to march the route again.

The other would have seen the group accept that it had won the right to march, but agree not to exercise that right, but neither proposal secured agreement from both sides.

News.title: Ceremony marks return home of kiwi feather cloak
News.content:
A ceremony has been held to mark the return of a MÄori kiwi feather cloak to New Zealand by a British museum.

The kahu kiwi was one of the farewell gifts presented by MÄori leaders in 1900 to Dr George Cleghorn, a medical doctor who had been working in New Zealand.

It was loaned to the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford by Cleghorn's widow in 1913.

The Homebound Project, a charity which funded the return, said the cloak was "crying to come home".

News.title: Eight men arrested by Greater Manchester Police days after early release from jail
News.content:
Eight men have been arrested by Greater Manchester Police days after leaving prison under the government's early release scheme.

About 700 prisoners from across the country were released early on 1 October in a bid to tackle overcrowding, with about 50 of them being from Greater Manchester.

GMP confirmed that five men had been arrested for breaches of criminal orders, including a domestic abuse prevention order, and others were held on suspicion of robbery, drug offences and domestic violence.

In response, the Ministry of justice (MOJ) said: "We inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse. If we had failed to act, the police would have been forced to halt arrests."

News.title: Rail disruption after overhead line fault
News.content:
Rail passengers are being urged to check before they travel due to overhead line problems on the West Coast Main Line in Staffordshire.

Work was ongoing to fix a fault with the 25,000-volt wires which power trains near Penkridge, causing disruption between Stafford and Wolverhampton.

At 12:00 BST, National Rail confirmed that lines have reopened between Stafford and Birmingham New Street, but residual disruption can still be expected until 16:00 BST on Saturday.

Adam Checkley from Network Rail, said: "Our teams have now cleared the issue allowing the route to reopen, but with trains and their crew out of position, delays and cancellations will continue throughout the day."

Rail replacement buses are in place at Birmingham, Stafford and Wolverhampton.

Checkley added: "We're sorry to passengers impacted by the overhead line problems at Four Ashes near Penkridge.

"With disruption to train services likely throughout the day, I'd urge people to check National Rail Enquiries before they set off on their journey."

Ticket acceptance is in place on alternative routes including the East Coast Main Line, and Midland Main Line via Sheffield.

News.title: Queen reflects on reading 'forbidden' Lady Chatterley's Lover under the pillow
News.content:
Queen Camilla has recalled secretly reading Lady Chatterley's Lover, the passionate and controversial novel by DH Lawrence, as a teenager in the 1960s.

"As teenagers you read a lot of romances. It was the moment of Lady Chatterley, under our pillows, reading that by torchlight. You know the minute something is forbidden, you want to get hold of it," she said about the novel that had been at the centre of an obscenity trial.

The Queen spoke about memorable moments in her own reading for BBC documentary The Book That Changed My Life, and about the life-changing power of literacy and books.

She gave a glimpse of how regular reading is part of her royal marriage: "It's like the best tonic in the world. My husband and I actually read before dinner, just sitting quietly and reading.

"He loves biographies, and PG Wodehouse. I occasionally, when I'm deep in a book, hear him roaring with laughter about something," said the Queen about the King's affection for the author of the Jeeves and Wooster comic novels.

"It's very off-putting, I can't get back into my book, or I'll suddenly start weeping. But it's a lovely, quiet time. I think it would be a complete and utter tragedy if books went forever," she said.

The Queen also revealed more of her own youthful reading, saying she was "mesmerised" by Charles Dickens's Tale of Two Cities and its depiction of those watching the guillotine during the French Revolution.

"Those ghastly women sitting there knitting while everybody had their heads chopped off," she said.

The Queen, who is 79 years old, said she was part of a generation of women who missed out on higher education, which made reading and books even more important.

"I left school quite young. In my day, women didn't go to university, so I think reading has been most of my education," she said.

News.title: Four murder arrests after teenagers attacked
News.content:
Police are continuing to investigate following the arrests of four people after a man died and another suffered life-threatening injuries in Stoke-on-Trent.

A cordon remains in place on Brookhouse Road, Meir, after police were called to reports of violence at 23:45 BST on Friday.

A man in his late teens was confirmed dead at the scene, Staffordshire Police said, and another man, also in his late teens, was taken to hospital, where he remains in a critical but stable condition.

Two 18-year-old men, a 20-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy, all from Stoke-on-Trent, were arrested on suspicion of murder, while the boy was also arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. All remain in police custody.

News.title: Craig Revel Horwood tears up as Strictly Come Dancing celebrity reminds him of ‘dear Len Goodman’
News.content:
Craig Revel Horwood got emotional as a Strictly Come Dancing celebrity reminded him of “dear Len Goodman” in the third week of the show.

In Saturday night’s episode (10 October), Canine expert Graeme Hall and his professional partner Laura Oakley performed a jive to Reet Retite by Jackie Wilson.

While receiving feedback from the judges, Craig held back tears as he said Graeme reminded him of the late Len Goodman which “brought back memories” and made him “a bit emosh”.

Graeme and Laura scored 25 out of a possible 40 points.

News.title: Trump mocks Kamala Harris’ looks as MAGA women guffaw at rambling Tennessee rally
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump mocked Kamala Harris’ appearance during a Tennessee rally, sarcastically calling the former vice president “beautiful” as female MAGA supporters standing behind him laughed along with the derogatory crack.

Trump, as he is known to do, appeared to stray from his prepared remarks Saturday at the midterm rally for Tennessee Republican candidates as he recalled campaign rallies held by Harris and former President Joe Biden during the COVID-19 pandemic.

“Remember that beautiful Kamala? Somebody said she’s so beautiful. Really?” Trump cracked.

Several women behind Trump guffawed at the remark. One gave Harris a thumbs-down, while another vigorously shook her head.

Trump has repeatedly commented on Harris’ appearance, at times calling her “beautiful” while then insisting he is better-looking than his 2024 presidential election opponent.

President Donald Trump sarcastically called former Vice President Kamala Harris 'beautiful' Saturday during a campaign rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, prompting a chuckle from some female supporters ( Reuters )

During a livestreamed conversation with Elon Musk in August 2024, Trump discussed a Time magazine cover featuring an illustration of Harris and scrutinized her appearance.

“She looks like the most beautiful actress ever to live. Actually, she looked very much like a great first lady, Melania. She didn't look like Kamala,” Trump told Musk. “But of course, she's a beautiful woman, so we'll leave it at that, right?”

Less than a week later, Trump returned to the subject during a rally in Pennsylvania.

“Don't ever call a woman beautiful, because that'll be the end of your political career,” Trump told the cheering crowd. “But I say that I am much better looking. I'm a better-looking person than Kamala.”

Elsewhere during Saturday’s rally, Trump aired his grievances with his wife, Melania Trump, claiming she disapproves of his speaking style.

“My wife hates when I do this. She says it’s ‘not at all elegant’ and ‘not presidential.’ I said it may not be presidential, but I won the election in a landslide,” he said.

Trump praised Melania as “a very elegant woman” before discussing her documentary, which he claimed was the No. 1 film of the year.

“And I don’t like that it’s the No. 1 movie. You know why? There’s only room for one star in a family, so I don’t need this movie stuff,” he added.

News.title: Knicks champion Karl-Anthony Towns opens up about grief for World Mental Health Day
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Karl-Anthony Towns has been traded from Minnesota, lost the conference finals and won the NBA title for his childhood team — and still feels he is in the period of grief that began six years ago.

Just 10 days before the New York Knicks' banner-raising celebration, the All-Star big man marked World Mental Health Day by sharing his ongoing emotional journey following the death of his mother to complications from COVID-19.

Entering the first game of this year's NBA Finals, he said he felt “this very big calm” wash over him. He was taken back to amateur youth games with crowds so small he could spot his mom from anywhere.

“I felt like it was kinda just me, her and the game of basketball,” he told the audience gathered Saturday by the nonprofit Project Healthy Minds. “I was able to be like an artist out there. I was able to have my paint brush and have a canvas with the court. And I was able to just paint a beautiful picture for her about the love I have for the game. The love I have to show the world because of her.”

There was a time when he had lost that love for the game. Towns, whose bright smile became a constant image of the Knicks' championship run, said basketball “felt hollow” after his mother's death. “I didn't know if I wanted to do it anymore,” he said.

But Towns found some solace in Arnie Kander, a well-known strength and wellness coach.

“Just to be heard, to be able to talk to someone you can trust, be able to really unload all that pain onto it and allow them to understand your feelings and articulate your feelings the right way, it makes life much lighter," he said. "And I felt myself getting lighter every time we kept talking.”

Athletes embrace mental health

Project Healthy Minds hopes Towns' example will inspire others to seek mental health care. The tech nonprofit runs a free online marketplace for finding therapy, psychiatry, support groups and other services. Its annual World Mental Health Day festival in New York offers an all-day schedule of yoga, art therapy and speakers.

Speaking Saturday with Towns was Boardroom CEO Rich Kleiman, the longtime manager for NBA superstar Kevin Durant and a new member of Project Healthy Minds' board.

Kleiman told The Associated Press that these sorts of conversations are growing more prevalent among athletes. DeMar DeRozan and Kevin Love kick-started the conversation eight years ago when DeRozan tweeted about depression and Love then published a first-person essay about anxiety. Kleiman recalled trading stories about anxiety attacks with Love for several hours one night shortly afterward.

Most players won’t feel that comfortable constantly telling their story, Kleiman said. Mental health isn’t a topic of discussion in the locker room. But he said players are certainly more aware of its impact.

“They just carry so much weight and speak to so many people,” Kleiman told The Associated Press before the panel. “I think it says a lot that Karl Towns is feeling comfortable enough right before the season starts to be able to be so open about it.”

Another panel brought together former NFL wide receiver Brandon Marshall and Gotham FC forward Midge Purce for a conversation about finding purpose outside of performance. Marshall, a six-time Pro Bowl player who publicly shared his borderline personality disorder diagnosis in 2011, said therapy showed him how to “connect with his brain.” He even started taking his therapy sessions in the cafeteria to normalize it for others.

Purce discussed her evolving definition of “tough." Raised by her dad, she said she grew up believing toughness meant “no tears.” But she credited her teammates with teaching her “it's OK to feel sad and upset.”

“I think tough is being able to feel all those things that are touching you and touching your heart, but still finding that resilience to go forward while living all of it," she told the crowd.

Using sports to show emotional strength

Saturday's sports focus offers a glimpse into Project Healthy Minds' future programming.

The nonprofit relies on cultural figures to introduce its platform to their audiences. It partnered this summer with the Broadway play “Every Brilliant Thing,” a one-person show whose narrator — originally played by Daniel Radcliffe, then Mariska Hargitay and, finally, Tracee Ellis Ross — presents his struggling mother with a list of reasons to live.

Soon-to-be-announced initiatives will lean further into sports as the nonprofit tries to inspire more communities to seek mental health care. With interest in women's sports growing and live sports remaining a powerful convener in an otherwise fragmented media landscape, Project Healthy Minds CEO Phil Schermer finds that athletes are well suited to bring their message to the masses.

Athletes, according to Schermer, also shape the American public’s notions of strength. It makes sense to him that they could then model that “it is strong to talk about your emotions.”

“There need to be more men — and more men who are archetypes of strength — being vulnerable," Schermer told AP. “Being willing to talk about these things. And role modeling that it can serve as fuel for your greatest success.”

The Knicks championship run became a rare moment of monoculture, Schermer suggested. The title chase also offered the in-person socialization that young people are demanding, according to Rachel Janfaza, the founder of the Gen Z research firm The Up and Up.

Speaking with “The Anxious Generation” author Jonathan Haidt and The TAG Movement CEO Alexa Arnold, Janfaza said young people used the Knicks and the World Cup to create the in-real-life community they missed during the pandemic.

“We’re seeing this swing," she said, "and it’s really incumbent upon schools and employers and anyone who has a vested interest in helping this generation thrive to actually celebrate this.”

News.title: Man dies after tiger attack at Yorkshire zoo
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A man has been killed in a tiger attack after he entered an enclosure at a zoo in Yorkshire.

Emergency services were called to Yorkshire Wildlife Park shortly after 1.30pm on Saturday after the unnamed victim reportedly climbed into a compound housing two of the big cats.

He sustained serious injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. The man’s family have since been informed, South Yorkshire Police said.

“Regarding rumours surrounding the condition of the tiger, the animal was uninjured and remained in the enclosure following the incident and there is no wider risk to the public,” the force added in a statement.

The wildlife park near Doncaster was evacuated and expected to remained closed for the remainder of the weekend, a spokesperson said.

open image in gallery A man died at Yorkshire Wildlife Park on Saturday after being attacked by a tiger (File) ( PA Archive )

Visitor Karmelle Pelham, from Worksop, told the BBC that she was with her family at the lemur enclosure when the zoo was evacuated.

She told the broadcaster they were told to leave, before being ushered “further and further into the park”. The family heard what sounded like several gunshots before seeing helicopters circling overhead.

Ms Pelham commended the staff for getting visitors out of the park safely without creating panic.

A spokesperson for the park told The Independent that emergency response procedures were activated immediately and that emergency services remained on the scene.

“We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened,” they said, adding: “The safety and wellbeing of our visitors, staff and animals remain our highest priority.”

“The park is now closed and will remain closed tomorrow.”

Did you see what happened? Contact james.reynolds@independent.co.uk

open image in gallery Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with the “Land of the Tigers” attraction opening in 2011

A Yorkshire Ambulance Service spokesperson said that two land ambulances, Yorkshire Air Ambulance and a doctor attended the scene.

Videos circulating online appear to show a man being pawed at and grappled by a tiger in an enclosure at the park. Police said they were aware of the footage and have asked people not to share it.

Park guest Tia Hanson, told the Sheffield Star that she and a friend were at the scene at around 2pm when the walkway between the tiger enclosure and the exit was closed.

“It looks as if someone has jumped into the enclosure. People are saying they heard a gunshot and they say someone either jumped in, or fell in.”

“It wasn’t nice - there were lots of people who looked really upset,” she added.

Becky, from Doncaster, told The Mirror she was at the zoo with her children when they were evacuated.

“We were at the tiger enclosure 10 minutes before the incident happened,” she said.

"We heard four gun shots, but didn't think anything of it until we heard the air ambulance trying to land and then one of the park staff approached us and told us we had to leave the park.”

Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary and MP for Doncaster North, expresses his condolences following the incident in Yorkshire.

“I’m deeply saddened to hear of the incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park,” he writes on Facebook.

“I send my thoughts and deepest condolences to the family of the individual who died. I am very grateful to the emergency services and staff of the park who responded.”

open image in gallery The park was evacuated on Saturday and closed for the remainder of the weekend ( PA )

Doncaster mayor Ros Jones said he was “deeply saddened to hear of the tragic incident that has taken place today at Yorkshire Wildlife Park”.

”My thoughts and prayers are with all those involved at this immensely difficult time,” he added.

Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with the “Land of the Tigers” attraction opening in 2011.

The attraction is on a purpose-built two-acre reserve for endangered Amur tigers, an endangered subspecies with around 500 left in the wild.

Yorkshire Wildlife Park has two Amur tigers, including a 17-stone tigress called Tschuna, who arrived in 2013, and a young male called Altai, who arrived last year.

Photos of the enclosure on the park’s website shows a high walkway for visitors and fencing above the section where the tigers can roam.

News.title: Gunman kills pregnant woman, 2 children and 5 others in massacre of Pennsylvania family
News.content:

A 45-year-old Erie, Pennsylvania, gunman killed eight members of the same family, including a pregnant woman and two children, before turning the gun on himself in what police described as a “devastating” rampage Friday.

The victims ranged in age from 1 year and 10 months to 51, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said Saturday in a news conference.

Two women, aged 51 and 37, were found dead outside the home. Inside, officers found a 5-year-old boy, a girl who was two months shy of 2 years old, and four adults: two women, aged 24 and 44, and two men, aged 19 and 21. One victim was eight months pregnant.

Police found all nine bodies at the Perry Street home after responding around 5 p.m. Friday to reports of a man firing a handgun outside and then storming into the house. A .40-caliber handgun registered to the suspected shooter was found on his body.

“It was horrific. It was the worst scene I have ever experienced,” Lorah said.

open image in gallery A 45-year-old shooter killed eight people, including a pregnant woman and two young kids, then himself Friday at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania ( Getty )

Eight of the nine people who died were related, and the ninth victim was a family friend. Lorah did not reveal a motive for the shootings, but said mental health may be a factor.

“As I said last night, some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes,” Lorah referenced his Friday remarks in which he called the incident “deeply disturbing’

“Out of respect for the victims and the families, I will not discuss the details of what our officers encountered inside that home,” he added Saturday.

Ring doorbell footage from a neighboring home shows the two women arriving in distress and pounding on the door for help, Lorah said.

Audio appears to capture muffled gunshots inside before the suspected shooter came outside and killed the women. Investigators believe he called out to them before they ran toward him.

open image in gallery The victims ranged in age from 1 year and 10 months to 51, police said Saturday ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Two women were found shot dead in the street, while the remaining victims and the suspected gunman were found dead inside the home ( Reuters )

One woman was the sister-in-law of a victim inside the home. The other was a family friend, he said. Police are reviewing their phones and interviewing relatives and witnesses to establish what they knew.

“They must have known that something was going on. They didn’t contact us, though, so we don’t know what that is yet,” Lorah said of the women.

Officers arrived within minutes of a ShotSpotter alert but heard no gunshots or cries for help and saw no movement inside, Lorah said. With the doors locked and windows covered, they couldn’t tell if the gunman was still inside or if anyone was being held hostage.

Police used drones to check the home before SWAT officers forced their way inside and sent in a robot to assess the scene. After discovering the bodies, officers entered the home, he said.

open image in gallery Eight victims were family members, while the ninth was a family friend ( Getty )

All eight victims inside and the suspected shooter died before officers arrived. No gunshots were fired after officers arrived, Lorah said. Sounds mistaken for gunfire during the response came from flashbang devices and chemical munitions used by SWAT officers.

The investigation remains ongoing, and there is no threat to the public.

If you are based in the U.S., and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you

News.title: Nicolas Cage lets slip potential True Detective role at New York Comic Con
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nicolas Cage has seemingly confirmed that he will appear in the next season of True Detective.

It was first reported last year that the 62-year-old National Treasure and Con Air star was in talks to join the show, which is expected to be written by True Detective: Night Country showrunner Issa López.

During an appearance this weekend at New York Comic Con, Cage teased that the rumors are indeed true.

According to The Hollywood Reporter, Cage discussed his future plans on stage and revealed that as he “can only do so many movies back to back” he is “probably going to do another season of television.”

Cage recently made his television debut as the lead in Amazon’s Spider-Noir, but the show was cancelled after just one season.

Nicolas Cage has suggested he might work with showrunner Issa López on the next season of ‘True Detective’ ( Getty )

Cage told the crowd: “I think I might do a season of True Detective. That’s OK that I’m the first to announce that, right? Like Jonathan Turteltaub, he gets a microphone in his hand and he goes to Philadelphia and says, ‘We’re doing National Treasure 3, and Nic’s coming. I’m like, ‘No, I didn’t 

He added: “We’ll see if I want to get together with it.”

Elsewhere in the conversation, Cage also revealed that he refused to sign a waiver approving the use of AI during the making of Spider-Noir.

“How do you survive AI?” he asked. “Amazon is a very AI friendly company to the tune of 50 billion dollars invested to OpenAI. I am not an AI friendly actor. I didn’t sign the waiver to let them use AI on Spider-Noir. It’s kind of like I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again. But that’s OK.”

Little is known about the forthcoming new season of True Detective, which is reportedly set to arrive on screens in 2027.

Series creator Nic Pizzolatto served as showrunner for the first three seasons of True Detective, with Issa López taking over for the polarising fourth season and forthcoming fifth.

True Detective season one focused on detectives Rust Cohle (McConaughey) and Martin Hart (Harrelson) as they investigated a spate of ritualistic murders in Louisiana.

The second season starred Rachel McAdams, Colin Farrell and Vince Vaughn, while the third starred Mahershala Ali and Stephen Dorff.

Jodie Foster and Kali Reis headed up the show’s frosty fourth season, subtitled Night Country, which aired on HBO.

News.title: The signs your child is struggling with returning to school and how to help
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

While the end of the summer holidays often brings welcome structure for parents, the return to the classroom can be a difficult adjustment for pupils. Spotting the signs that a child is struggling is essential, experts say, even if those signs are difficult to identify.

Matt Buttery, CEO of the Triple P UK and Ireland parenting programme, highlighted the contrast between summer freedom and daily structure.

"Many parents will be ready to get back into the routine the school term brings, but for children it can feel like a big adjustment to go from having seemingly endless free time in the sun, to going back into a regular routine," he said. "They may have mixed emotions as they start school again, from excitement to dread – this is normal."

Additional pressures can arise from new subjects, impending examinations, or changing schools. Tiffnie Harris, policy specialist at the teaching union the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), suggests parents contact the school if they feel their child is floundering.

She noted that early half-term tutor meetings or settling-in evenings offer an ideal forum for discussion.

"It’s vital this is done in a constructive way, as this will make the issue much easier to resolve," she explained. "This is a key opportunity for parents to air any concerns and ask questions."

She says it’s useful for parents to be prepared for this by making notes before any meetings.

But how can mums and dads spot their child is not coping well? Here’s what the experts say…

1) Trouble sleeping

open image in gallery

It’s normal for sleep to be a little unsettled when children head back to school, as they adjust to a more structured routine and navigate any worries about the new school year, says Buttery.

“If you notice your child is struggling to get out of bed and regularly complaining about being tired before and after school, a great way to help them adjust is to create a consistent routine,” he advises.

He says it’s best to start by establishing clear and consistent routines around key transition times of the day, such as getting ready for school, after-school activities, homework, meals, downtime, and bedtime.

Bedtime is especially important, he stresses, as many children need time to readjust from more relaxed holiday schedules.

“Supporting good sleep hygiene, such as consistent bedtimes and wake-up times, calm evening activities, and limiting screens before bed can help children feel more settled, rested, and ready to engage with the school day,” he explains.

“As children adjust to a new school year, predictable routines can provide a reassuring sense of predictability during a time of change.”

2) Lack of organisation

Although it’s normal for younger children to be disorganised, as pupils get older, organisation can become an issue that can lead to issues at school, says Harris.

“It helps if parents can work with their children to ensure they check their timetable, pack the night before and have everything they need to be ready for school the next day,” she suggests.

3) School work worries

Signs a child is having issues with school work can include them expressing frustration about it and losing confidence in their abilities, avoiding certain subjects, or saying they find lessons boring or difficult, says Buttery.

open image in gallery

“They might seem anxious or nervous before school days where they have certain lessons, or look like they’re avoiding school work or homework,” he suggests.

It’s important to speak to your child’s teachers as soon as possible if you think they may be struggling with a certain subject, and Harris says: “If a pupil is struggling in a particular class, then having an open dialogue with that teacher can be really beneficial.

“Being receptive to ways parents might be able to help at home is key – for example, where a child is having difficulties with literacy – reading with them and encouraging reading at home can make a real difference, particularly for younger children.

“Remember that schools want to work with parents to provide the best opportunities for their children. This partnership is absolutely vital.”

4) Not bonding with peers

The first few weeks of school can be overwhelming for children, especially if they’re at a new school where they don’t know many of their peers, warns Buttery.

open image in gallery

“If you notice they seem withdrawn, nervous or anxious before or after school, it may mean they’re having a hard time bonding with their new school mates, feeling lonely and unsettled, or having problems with their friendship group,” he says.

One of the most important ways to make friends is by finding common interests, he points out, and children often learn these social skills by watching their parents.

“Talking about what a good friend looks like in your everyday conversations with your child can help,” he says. “Ask them what they think a good friend does – is it letting others join in their games, or listening to ideas from other kids? Notice and praise kids when they do these things, and share what you like about your friends.”

He also advises parents to encourage their child to try the school’s extracurricular clubs, which can be a great way for children to get to know their peers. But he warns parents to make sure children aren’t doing too much, pointing out: “It’s important to encourage designated downtime to avoid your child becoming burnt out or overwhelmed.”

5) Stress about bullying or other issues

Starting a new school year may open up lots of different emotions for your child, and mixing with new kids could spark bullying, or lead to children being left out and feeling stressed or anxious.

Harris says signs of anxiety to watch out for may be a child complaining of stomach problems, not wanting to talk about their school day, or having mood swings.

Buttery says a stressed child may seem quieter than usual, or more withdrawn or irritable, and he suggests that if parents notice any signs of anxiety in a child they should encourage them to express their feelings by asking open-ended questions, such as ‘What was the best thing that happened at school today?’, ‘What lesson did you find the trickiest?’, or ‘What did you and your friends talk about at lunchtime?’.

He adds: “This may help encourage them to share their thoughts with you, rather than the usual one-word answer many parents will hear when they ask their child how their day went.”

But he points out that if stress and anxiety are affecting your child’s ability to enjoy school, parents should seek help through teachers, a GP, or parenting experts.

News.title: Resurgent Verstappen on fire in the Singapore smog
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

News.title: Black British Business Awards 2026 winners revealed
News.content:
The chief executive of Dr. Martens has been named the Black British Business Person of the Year at the 2026 Black British Business Awards (BBBAwards).

Ije Nwokorie, who became chief of Dr. Martens in January last year and is the only black chief executive in the FTSE 250, was awarded in recognition of his role shaping Dr. Martens’ growth strategy.

He is recognised inside Dr. Martens for his strong communication with staff, according to the judges.

Before joining Dr. Martens, Mr Nwokorie spent more than 11 years at Wolff Olins, the marketing giant, before working as a senior director at Apple.

Born in the US but brought up from age six against the backdrop of post-civil-war Nigeria, Mr Nwokorie has described how he and his family went from the lifestyle trappings of 1960s America to a small Nigerian village and a home with no running water.

On winning the award, Mr Nwokorie said: “This recognition means a lot to me. While this award bears my name, it reflects the talent, dedication and generosity of the incredible teammates, mentors and leaders who have shaped me as a person and a professional.

“It is a powerful reminder that there is nothing more important in our leadership journeys than the time we invest to help others thrive.”

Alongside his executive career, he has served as a trustee at Charity: water for nearly a decade and held board roles at cultural and humanitarian organisations including the Institute of International Visual Arts and Malaria No More UK.

He also served as chairman of trustees for the Chineke! Orchestra, a British orchestra championing change and the first in Europe to feature a majority of black and ethnically diverse musicians.

The Black British Business Awards started in 2014 to celebrate the achievements of black people in British business. The Telegraph is the national media partner for the awards.

Mr Nwokorie was presented with the award at an exclusive ceremony sponsored by JPMorgan Chase at London’s Hilton Park Lane hotel.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sophie Chandauka, the executive founder of the awards, said: “You lend the BBBAwards credibility not simply to celebrate excellence, but to ensure the best and brightest from all communities get a fair shot. That commitment has made the BBBAwards the UK’s premium awards programme for black business achievement.”

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said: “We couldn’t be prouder to support and celebrate such an outstanding breadth of black British talent.

“Their accomplishments continue to inspire future generations and demonstrate the exceptional value they bring to businesses, communities and the wider UK economy.”

This year’s winners are as follows:

Black British Business Person of the Year: Ije Nwokorie, chief executive of Dr Martens

Arts and Media Rising Star: Sheniece Charway, artist partnership manager [EMEA], YouTube/Google

Arts and Media Senior Leader: Amie Parker-Williams, director, digital commissioning and production, Paramount

Fashion, Beauty and Consumer Senior Leader: Andrea Thompson, journalist, brand consultant and former editor-in-chief, Marie Claire UK

Fashion, Beauty and Consumer Rising Star: Yasmin O’Neal, senior director for global brand and impact, DECIEM

Entrepreneur Rising Star: Dr Elsa Zekeng, founder and chief executive, SökerData

Entrepreneur Senior Leader: Antonia Okonma Shittu, founder and chief executive, A-List Lace Hair

Financial Services Rising Star: Nana Agyemang, proposition delivery manager, Barclays

Financial Services Senior Leader: Melissa Max-Macarthy, formerly managing director, head of strategy and innovation, retail banking, NatWest Group

Professional Services Rising Star: Jack Van Cooten, senior manager – external vendors and data, Oliver Wyman

Professional Services Senior Leader: Laurie-Anne Power KC, barrister, 25 Bedford Row

Retail and Hospitality Senior Leader: Leona De Graft, vice-president of global ecommerce, Levi Strauss and Co

Retail and Hospitality Rising Star: Rickey Devonish, head of apprenticeships and emerging talent, JD Group

STEM Senior Leader: Eustace Xavier, finance director, technical services, Mitie PLC

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

Sports.title: Jordan Pickford faces England fight as David Seaman fires warning despite Everton’s hunt for fourth-straight clean sheet
Sports.content:
Next

JORDAN PICKFORD is facing the fight of his career to keep his England shirt.

The Everton stopper, 32, heads into Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Hull City aiming for a fourth-straight clean sheet in all competitions for the Blues.



Throw in another two for the Three Lions over the international break and you could be forgiven for thinking his spot as the country’s No1 was assured.

But the 93-capped star’s international place is under threat for the first time in almost a decade after he was benched twice for his country in favour of James Trafford over the past three weeks.



With England boss Thomas Tuchel watching his every move — and Leeds’ Trafford breathing down his neck — Pickford cannot afford any slip-ups at the MKM Stadium.

And legendary Three Lions ‘keeper David Seaman says the Everton stalwart MUST perform under the intense heat of competition if he wants to be Tuchel’s first-choice come Euro 2028.



Speaking via Betway, Seaman said: “That’s going to be close. When you look at Jordan and what he’s done for England, you’re not really expecting him to be left out.

“But James is going to be pushing him now, and this is what he needs.

“Now Trafford’s playing for Leeds regularly, and he’s been given the nod by Tuchel to show that he trusts him against the world champions Spain.

“That was a massive boost of confidence for James Trafford. We saw a goalkeeper that’s very capable of performing at that level.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I’m 50/50, if I’m honest, and that’s because of how highly I rate James Trafford.

“Jordan’s level is up there because of what he’s doing for England, and he’s now doing it more regularly for Everton as well.

“It wasn’t his best World Cup, he knows that, but he’s still got all that experience. Now it’s about seeing how he can perform when there’s a real contender.”

Sports.title: Under-pressure Burnham urged to come clean about ALL his dealings with Man City & their UAE owners
Sports.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham has been urged to come clean about all his dealings with Manchester City and their UAE owners.

The PM is facing pressure to publish all correspondence and financial links to the club, found guilty of widespread cheating.



It comes after the ex-Manchester mayor was accused of “political interference” by saying he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners.

He later clarified, saying: “It’s important to separate the football issues from wider investment.”



The Tories have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy demanding the Government is “open and honest” about its involvement in the case.

This includes disclosing all contact with Man City and its owners and any relevant correspondence with the Independent Football Regulator.



It comes after The Sun revealed Labour politicians received nearly £300,000 of freebies from the UAE and City.

Deputy leader Lucy Powell, whose constituency covers City’s Etihad Stadium, got tickets to five matches worth £2,360.

Louie French, shadow sports minister, wants to know all financial links with ministers or advisers.

He also called for all details published about a meeting between City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at No10 last month.



The PM’s City links go back to 2018 when he attended the opening of a club office in China.

City deny breaking Prem financial rules and have launched an appeal.

Mr French said they had “sincere concerns” about perceived Government interference in the process, calling the PM’s comments “highly inappropriate”.

Sports.title: Burnham must come clean about EVERY government contract with Man City – then stay out of football
Sports.content:
Next

KEEPING politics and Government out of sport is a belief that unites the vast majority of the public, regardless of football or political allegiances.

When news first broke that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges and were likely to appeal via their small army of lawyers, my first instinct was, “This is going to get very messy for English football so do not make it worse by providing a quote to a journalist.”



The vast majority of MPs were of the same opinion, no doubt because we are also warned to avoid commenting on live legal cases.

So why was the Prime Minister so keen to get involved and defend City?



Within a day of the verdict, he was on the BBC saying how worried he would be to lose City’s owners — ignoring the widespread concerns and the millions of fans who believe in fair play and healthy competition.

He appeared to find a new spirit of the blues, but why?

The Premier League says the independent commission found City inflated their accounts by more than £900million over nine seasons.

City deny it, and that is for the appeal process to settle.

For decades, the global success of the Premier League and EFL has seen vast sums flood into English football, attracting the best players and a new generation of international owners.

But this success has also attracted a renewed focus on the long-term sustainability of club finances, with the leagues implementing new spending rules to try to ensure fairness and healthy competition on the pitch.



It is no surprise, then, that other Premier League clubs were astonished by the Prime Minister’s remarks and fear political interference in the appeal.

Days before news of the verdict broke, City’s chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak reportedly held a private meeting with the Business Secretary in Downing Street, wearing his other hat as boss of Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth fund.

In recent years, investment from Abu Dhabi has helped transform great swathes of Manchester while Mr Burnham was Mayor.



Then there is the regulator, which may yet have to decide whether City’s owners are fit and proper people to run the club.

Its chairman, David Kogan, is a Labour donor who backed both Lisa Nandy and Keir Starmer — a link ministers later had to apologise for failing to declare.

I want to be clear that none of this proves anyone has done anything wrong.

But taken together, it raises questions that any fair-minded fan would want answered.

That is why I have written to Lisa Nandy, who has served as Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport since 2024, demanding that her department publish every financial link or exchange it has had regarding Manchester City and its owners, across Whitehall and with the regulator.



I have also asked whether the Government has taken legal advice on the regulator’s ability to judge this case fairly, if required, given the impact of its political links and Andy Burnham’s inappropriate comments on perceptions of natural justice.

Put in footballing terms, this is a VAR review to help improve transparency and ensure the Government is not involved in any foul play, which would make this difficult situation for football even worse.

The Prime Minister promised to do politics differently, and the first test of that promise is honesty.

Mr Burnham was never elected Prime Minister by the country, but he answers to it all the same.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If everything is above board, publishing the paperwork costs him nothing, yet every day he dodges the questions, the smell grows stronger and football’s reputation suffers.



The Prime Minister must now come clean and stay out of football.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hurt by Man Utd fans’ BOOING team during 1-1 draw with Tottenham but says: ‘I’m not hiding’
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK admits he is “hurt” by Manchester United supporters’ booing during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham.

United matchgoers booed midway through the first half amid Tottenham’s dominance and again at half-time with the game goalless.



There were more boos at full-time in response to Dominic Solanke’s 92nd-minute equaliser that leaves United with one win from their first six Premier League games – their worst start in 40 years.

United’a away-dayers also booed Carrick’s decision to substitute Kobbie Mainoo in their 1-1 draw at Fulham three weeks ago.



Carrick conceded: “When things aren’t quite going to plan, I understand the reaction at times. Obviously, it hurts. It hurts a lot.

“It’s not nice to go through, but sometimes you have to go through it, that’s how it is.

“I care as much as anybody about this place, so sometimes you could say too much because then it overspills. But it’s coming from a good place, really, and so I understand it.

“But yeah, of course, it’s not nice to have to go through that. I thought the players dealt with it well, to be honest, and used it coming out especially in the second half.

“Even before the changes, I thought there was, you could see that we were starting to look more like ourselves.

“We just had to make changes to try and freshen up that little bit more, which we got the benefit of, and made a difference.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

United have now conceded to ten men in two home games running, having lost to Manchester City last month.

Tottenham and Everton both claimed added-time equalisers against United, who have failed to win from a winning position in three of their eight games this term.

Carrick added: “I’m not happy with the amount of points that we’ve had so far, for sure. I’m not hiding [and] there’s no hiding from that.

“I think it could have been different for a couple of little things here or there, but the reality is the reality, we’ve got to accept it, you know.

“We need to put things in a direction, in a positive direction quite quickly, that’s pretty plain.



“We can do, we can do, of course we can, we’re more than capable of doing that. Just got to be a little bit more streetwise in the moments and a little bit more stubborn and a little bit more stronger in seeing out certain things.

“But we’ve been in good positions at times, other times we haven’t done well enough, but sometimes you have a real patch when it is going against you and things don’t work out as you’d want them to work out.”

Sports.title: Mark Chapman & MOTD co-star Kelly Cates enjoyed secret date in New York during World Cup months before romance revealed
Sports.content:
Next

MATCH Of The Day host Mark Chapman extended his World Cup for a secret date with co-presenter Kelly Cates in New York.

Their Big Apple tryst comes after we revealed last week the pair have been seeing other romantically.



Chapman, 52, claimed on a podcast he was leaving the US after hosting BBC1’s coverage of the England and Argentina semi in Atlanta on July 15.

But instead of flying directly back to the UK, he travelled to New York to meet Kelly, who was there for BBC Radio Five Live’s coverage of the final on July 19.



An industry source said last night: “Mark said he had a business meeting in New York so went there before returning back to the UK, but also met with Kelly one evening for a date. It was the perfect place to conduct their budding romance.”

Kelly, 51, daughter of Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish, had also been in Atlanta for the England semi-final.



Chapman told Gabby Logan on the Sports Agents podcast that he was not working for the final and was returning to the UK for The Open golf at Royal Birkdale.

He said: “Then I will drive back from The Open golf listening to Kelly and the build-up on the radio and then I’ll catch some of you on the telly.”



Sources said the broadcaster, nicknamed “Chappers”, did not arrive in the UK before July 18, and attended the golf for the climax the following day.

He also always planned to fly back to the UK via New York and did not create further BBC costs.

Last week we revealed how Chapman and Kelly, 51, had been dating since May after growing close on Match Of The Day – where they share presenting duties with Gabby, 53.



Chapman was seeing Dubai-based mum-of-two Clere Collier for three years before abruptly ending the romance in April.

He and Kelly appeared flirty on TV’s Celebrity Gogglebox this summer.

Kelly split from TV producer husband Tom in 2021. They have two kids.

Chapman lost his wife of 19 years, Sara, to cancer when she was aged just 44 in 2020. They had three children together.

The BBC declined to comment. Representatives for Kelly and Mark were asked for comment.

Sports.title: Man City on high alert over bus arrival at Anfield as police on standby for hostile Liverpool reception after verdict
Sports.content:
Next

IT WAS always going to be a bearpit when Manchester City walked out at Anfield on Sunday.

A cauldron of ear-splitting noise and intensity, febrile and furious.



But now, after two weeks when City’s off-field conduct has been under the microscope like never before, it is likely to be even more brutal.

A test of nerve for both teams once the actual football kicks off at 4.30pm.



That the home supporters, never shy of an opinion, will want to make things tough for City is inevitable. That is how it is supposed to be.

Football is a tribal sport. It runs in the blood, through the generations.



Few, if any, grounds reverberate with more passion and fervour than the one that stands proudly behind the Shankly Gates.

Get ready for a ­decibel count that is off the scale, especially with the Kopites believing they have official vindication for all their long-held suspicions.

Both teams will face an examination on the field of play, with Andoni Iraola getting his first real taste of what Anfield can be with everything on the line.

And while City chief Enzo Maresca has walked out alongside Pep Guardiola in the past, this time he will be front and centre.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

There must be worries about how the heightened furies of the past few days will play out.

After all, on previous City visits to Anfield, it has too frequently boiled over — and not in any way to the credit of the home side.

For decades, Liverpool’s rivalry with teams from the other end of the East Lancs Road was squarely aimed at those wearing red rather than blue.

Supporters of both teams were guilty of what is now known as ‘tragedy chanting’, making fun of disasters.



Comments by club bosses often fuelled the atmosphere.

Sir Alex Ferguson wanted to “knock Liverpool off their f***ing perch”, Kenny Dalglish and Rafa Benitez refused to sit back and be verbally bullied, and England squad harmony was frequently disrupted by club loyalties.

Yet it was never about City — until City, under the Abu Dhabi ownership whose conduct is at the heart of the Premier League charges, started being good.

Locked in a title race in 2014 — one that ­Liverpool were to throw away in the space of a few days against Chelsea and Crystal Palace — a City fans’ bus was attacked on the way to one game.

And when City enticed Kop star Raheem Sterling to join them the following year, with the appointment of Guardiola to lock horns with Jurgen Klopp adding extra spice, it degenerated.



In 2018, Pep and his team bus were ‘welcomed’ to their Champions League quarter-final by a fusillade of cans, bricks and other missiles that brought a fine of £17,500 from Uefa.

As the rivalry cranked up on the pitch in a series of compelling clashes, so the temperature off it rose.

City rightly complained after a home fan spat in the direction of Guardiola during the 2-2 Prem draw in October 2021.

Then 12 months later, with City furious after coins were hurled at their boss during a 1-0 Liverpool win, the team bus was attacked again as it left the ground, with the windscreen smashed.

And that was when it was all about a football rivalry. Not with the heightened and inflamed tensions of City’s allegedly dirty laundry being washed in public.



The fact that Merseyside Police are on standby for incidents before kick-off, following social media appeals for home fans to gather from two hours before kick-off with their “flags, banners, pyros, flares and Kopparbergs” is a clear signal of concerns.

The hope is that we are left talking about the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

About how City responded to everything that has transpired, how the home supporters walked the right side of the delicate line between acceptable hostility and unacceptable physical intimidation.

That, though, may not be quite what transpires on the day.

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba made Man Utd more attacking on his debut… but his biggest challenge will be to shield porous defence
Sports.content:
Next

THE introduction of a defensive player made Manchester United more attacking.

Carlos Baleba’s overdue debut threatened to be the turning point in United’s unconvincing draw with Tottenham. He should not have had to wait until the 59th minute.



This was not the welterweight midfield match-up either set of supporters had hoped for. Tottenham blew United out of the water to recruit Mateus Fernandes, yet he only crossed the white line in the 89th minute.

Sandro Tonali, so often United’s scourge during his three years with Newcastle, was in majestic form against them again.



This was a must-win match for United yet Michael Carrick continued to hold Baleba back. Throwing him in from the start into the bear pits of Atletico Madrid or Elland Road next week is more sink-or-swim.

Baleba will have at least benefited from this bright bow. He was eventually summoned as the hour loomed and immediately showcased his athleticism with a pirouette and pass that sparked an attack and lit a spark in the stands.



The 22-year-old, sidelined since late July with an ankle injury, looked eager to make up for lost time. Baleba was urgent and alert, qualities the United midfield was totally lacking before his name was announced.

Baleba’s impact was so swift he forced his old coach Roberto de Zerbi into a counter change in Tottenham’s midfield. It was not Fernandes.

With a headline midfield signing and a focal point in the handy Joshua Zirkzee, United breached a toothless Tottenham. Baleba had no major role in Bryan Mbeumo’s goal but he had lifted the mood and his teammates.

There were boos from United supporters during the first half, more at half-time and again at full-time.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A Senne Lammens punt into touch sparked the first chorus. In successive games, United matchgoers have booed Carrick’s substitution and style.

Carrick’s game management has deserted him for much of this season and sending Baleba on does not suggest he has the Midas touch again. Baleba had to come on at half-time.

Carrick is developing a blind spot with Youri Tielemans, the only United player who has started every game this season. Ironically, the Belgium captain admitted in pre-season his body “switched off” during the World Cup amid the workload.

Tielemans was robbed of the ball in the opening minutes and Kobbie Mainoo was on his heels when Bergvall was on his toes to pounce on Senne Lammens’ lax clearance that Dominic Solanke squandered.

Almost every United manager ends up depending on the counter-attack and Carrick has also reached that point of desperation. Tonali gave a glimpse of the controlling style he would have offered and his craft made Solanke’s late equaliser possible.



Tonali is a £100million player. United have never stumped up that fee for a signing.

Elliot Anderson, another nine-figure transfer, was man of the match at Old Trafford in last month’s Manchester derby. United’s refusal to shop in the same boutiques as their rivals is costing them points.

Only when Baleba emerged did it feel that the playing field was levelled in the middle of the field. Before that, the panic was palpable.



Carrick is usually a static presence on the touchline yet he was uncharacteristically animated during a forlorn first half.

If Gary Neville had remarked that it was the worst 15 minutes he had seen from a United team in his lifetime, he would have had a point.

With Tonali at the base of Tottenham’s midfield triangle, United were pressed into going long to a non-existent target man.

Spurs had a conductor in Tonali to engineer attacks.

United were offered Connor Gallagher by Atletico last year. Gallagher lacks the ability of Mainoo and Tielemans but has a superior engine. So does Bergvall.



Baleba, seven years Tielemans’ junior, has been training for at least three weeks and turned out in a behind-closed-doors friendly last week.

As a specialist defensive midfielder, he is a more suitable foil for Mainoo and has been bought to strengthen the starting XI.

Mainoo belatedly grabbed the first half by the lapels, holding off Solanke to charge into the Tottenham third.

Those shots of adrenaline from United were rare and Tielemans was a sedate passenger.

Predictably, Carrick hooked Tielemans for Baleba. Mainoo, who withdrew from the England squad, produced possibly his weakest performance of the campaign.



Baleba was overzealous with the odd challenge and stray punt at goal. But Tielemans’ starting stint must end next week, either in Madrid or Leeds.

The bigger challenge for Baleba is to shield this porous United defence.

Their sole clean sheet this term remains in the Champions League against debutants Sabbah and they have now conceded to ten men twice.

Sports.title: Van Gerwen dumped out of Swiss Darts Trophy as nightmare year goes on
Sports.content:
Michael van Gerwen's nightmare year went from bad to worse as he was dumped out of the Swiss Darts Trophy in his opening match by Mensur Suljovic 6-4 on Saturday night.

Suljovic led 5-2 before Van Gerwen threatened a comeback but three missed darts to force a decider allowed Suljovic to take advantage.

It was Suljovic's fourth straight win over Van Gerwen and the fifth time in six tournaments that the Dutchman has exited after one match.

Van Gerwen's woes continue

Defeat in Basel marks the first time Michael van Gerwen has lost his opening match in FOUR European Tour events in the same season since its inception in 2012



European Darts Trophy ❌



German Darts Grand Prix ❌



Flanders Darts Trophy ❌



Swiss Darts Trophy ❌



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Colin Lloyd discusses Van Gerwen's ongoing struggles

Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen and Jonny Clayton all advanced to Finals Day as ten seeds crashed out on a remarkable day of action in Basel.

Newly crowned World Grand Prix champion Humphries was among the headline acts on Day Two at the St. Jakobshalle, where he prevailed against Kevin Doets.

Despite racing 3-0 ahead with 122 and 121 checkouts, Humphries was forced to survive a furious fightback from Doets, defying the Dutchman's 105.64 average to triumph in a breathless decider.

"I was really pleased with that performance," reflected Humphries, who averaged almost 103 and pinned 67% of his attempts at double.

"I felt like I was the better player for most of the game, but Kevin was really strong at the end there, so I had to really work my socks off."

European Champion Van Veen also impressed on Swiss soil, producing a hat-trick of ton-plus checkouts to whitewash a shell-shocked Niko Springer in just under ten minutes.

Clayton, meanwhile, stole the show with an irrepressible display against Maik Kuivenhoven, averaging 108.81 and landing two bullseye finishes to kick off his title bid in style.

The Welshman will take on Rob Cross for a place in the quarter-finals, after the former world champion halted Luke Woodhouse's mid-match fightback to close out a battling 6-4 victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Stephen Bunting looks back on that viral interview with Raymond van Barneveld at Ally Pally

There will be a new champion crowned at the St Jakobshalle on Sunday evening, as former champions Stephen Bunting and Martin Schindler crashed out on a day of upsets in Basel.

Swedish star Jeffrey de Graaf put in a clinical display of doubling to account for reigning champion Bunting, while Schindler was swept aside by Tom Bissell, who will feature at Finals Day for the first time in his European Tour career.

Dirk van Duijvenbode recorded a fifth straight win against James Wade to end the left-hander's bid for back-to-back European Tour titles, and a resurgent Michael Smith now awaits the Dutchman in the last 16.

The 2023 world champion delivered one of his best performances of the year to seal a 6-4 against Jermaine Wattimena, converting consecutive 116, 124 and 144 checkouts in the process.

Smith averaged just shy of 103 to cap off a quality display, which also preserves his hopes of qualifying for the Machineseeker European Championship later this month.
