Solanke, later to be the hero, was the most obvious culprit of the first half. In just the third minute, United goalkeeper Senne Lammens passed the ball straight to Lucas Bergvall and when he played Solanke through, he allowed Lammens to save when he should have been given no chance.

That set the tone for the half. Spurs – with key players on the bench for a variety of reasons – were organised and purposeful and energetic. Gallagher was excellent while Savio and Mohammed Kudus carried threat if not always the right end product.

United, by contrast, were lame. They seemed content to let Spurs come on to them and only started to muster some kind of momentum on the break in the final ten minutes of the half.

Spurs were particularly progressive down their left where United’s emergency right-back Leny Yoro had a difficult time. A goal should have come from there in the 21st minute when a nice combination allowed Savio to feed Kudus only for the shot on the turn to fly by the post.

Bryan Mbeumo's clever strike had given the hosts the lead

There was also a shot over the bar from Bergvall and a break into the box by Gallagher that was halted by a desperate but timely toe-poke from the retreating Youri Tielemans.

On the touchline De Zerbi looked grimly frustrated and no wonder.

Early in the second half Savio was again away down the left and once again his low cross almost led to something for his team but didn’t. Then, a minute later, the Brazilian did find Solanke in the middle only for another good chance to go begging, this time over the bar.

Later on a misdirected Harry Maguire interception allowed Savio in only for Kobbie Mainoo to divert the shot over. In between all that United had shown some belated promise.

New signing Carlos Baleba was rapturously welcomed when he emerged as a substitute and his first contribution was to control the ball beautifully and send Fernandes away down the left.

But it was another substitute, Joshua Zirkzee, who impacted the game more significantly. The Dutch forward started to link play better and hold up the ball. It enabled United to get up the pitch more regularly and, with eighteen minutes left, they somehow took the lead.

Mbeumo is a reliable finisher and he took this one well. Turning on to his left foot in the penalty area, he shot low across Antonin Kinsky and into the far corner after taking a pass from Matheus Cunha. But with at least five Spurs players in the vicinity, he simply should not have been given that amount of time.

For Spurs, another disaster loomed. And things soon got an awful lot harder.

Bentancur’s lunging tackle at Fernandes was not clever but the headbutt he planted on Shaw after the United player arrived to shove him in the chest was just stupid. Briefly chaos reigned by the near touchline. Players, coaches. They were all in. When it settled down, Spurs were a man down and a goal down.

Now United boss Michael Carrick faces a huge week which may define his future

United just had to manage the game now. Given what we have seen from them this season, it was far from a given that they would. And, perhaps quite predictably, they didn’t.

Two minutes into eight minutes of time added, Sandro Tonali – by now playing at left-back – crossed to the far post for Solanke to head in.

It was a marvellous effort by a striker with something to prove. Why United defender Lisandro Martinez attempted to wrestle him instead of looking at the ball, maybe only he will know.

As his team celebrated in the corner, De Zerbi clutched a spare ball and appeared to try and eat it. The Italian may feel his luck is about to change. It should do. His team looked well coached here. By contrast, United continue to exist on a mixture of vague hope and sense of history. Neither will be good enough in the long term.

Sports.title: 'Hurt' Michael Carrick rues Man United's failure to kill game against 10-man Spurs - as Roberto De Zerbi reveals Rodrigo Bentancur's red card inspired his side
Sports.content:
'Hurt' Michael Carrick rues Man United's failure to kill game against 10-man Spurs - as Roberto De Zerbi reveals Rodrigo Bentancur's red card inspired his side

Michael Carrick was left to rue Manchester United's failure to kill off 10-man Tottenham after Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for headbutting Luke Shaw at Old Trafford.

Carrick admitted it 'hurt' to be booed by fans after Dominic Solanke struck in injury-time to give Spurs a 1-1 draw and leave United with six points from six league games – their worst start in 40 years since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson in November 1986.

It was the second Premier League game in a row at home that United – who also conceded a late equaliser at Everton last month – couldn't beat 10 men after losing the Old Trafford derby to Manchester City.

'When things aren't quite going to plan, I understand the reaction at times,' said Carrick of the boos at the end of both halves. 'Obviously, it hurts, you know. It hurts a lot. It's not nice to go through, but sometimes you have to go through it.

'I care as much as anybody about this club. But it's coming from a good place really, and so I understand it.

'I'm not happy with the amount of points we've had so far. There's no hiding from that. I'm not hiding. That's the reality and we've got to accept it. We need to put things in a positive direction quite quickly, that's pretty plain.

Michael Carrick was left frustrated at his Man United side's 1-1 draw with Spurs on Saturday

'That's two late, late goals against us to throw away two wins. So that changes a lot of things. It changes the feelings among ourselves and it changes the points.

'We need to do better with seeing out games once we get ourselves in a good position, that's for sure. We're more than capable of doing that. We've just got to be a little bit more streetwise in the moments and a little bit more stubborn and strong.

'It's definitely something where, 10 men or not 10 men, if we're ahead in games, we've got to see them out.'

Tottenham are still without a win in their six Premier League games this season, but the manner of their performance and fightback gave Roberto De Zerbi plenty of reason to feel positive.

The Italian admitted that Bentancur's reaction to being pushed by Shaw was the wrong one, but bizarrely revealed that he kissed the player in the dressing-room afterwards because he showed some fighting spirit.

'I kissed Rodrigo and say thanks,' revealed De Zerbi. 'It is clearly a mistake from Rodrigo, it is not the right reaction in football.

'But now Tottenham needs to react. Sometimes the reaction is not nice, not positive for the team, but in that moment maybe with 10 players we played with more courage more energy.

'For a long time Tottenham played without this blood and this character. Now I am the coach and I want to see this character every game. With the qualities and the character and the right energy, we are going to win many games and score many goals.'

Sports.title: 'Stupid' Rodrigo Bentancur sparks mass brawl after HEADBUTTING Luke Shaw as Spurs star is sent off in clash with Man United
Sports.content:
Tottenham midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur was branded 'stupid' by Gary Neville after headbutting Luke Shaw and seeing red against Manchester United.

Bentancur had only been on the pitch for 12 minutes as a second-half substitute, but lost his cool in the 78th minute when he lashed out at Shaw and was given his marching orders.

He appeared to put a high tackle in on the left back, who was left fuming and chased his opponent down before pushing him to the ground.

Bentancur responded by rushing to his feet and headbutting Shaw, resulting in a brawl between the players.

'Madness from Bentancur,' Neville said on Sky Sports. 'Lack of discipline is not what he (Roberto De Zerbi) needs.

'It's stupidity. It really is.'

Rodrigo Bentancur is sent off... and here's why ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/3ahzz5iUbg — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) October 10, 2026

Rodrigo Bentancur (left) was sent off for Tottenham against Manchester United after headbutting Luke Shaw

The Uruguay international had to be pulled away from Shaw, who was booked, by United defender Lisandro Martinez.

A member of Tottenham's coaching staff had to eventually escort him down the Old Trafford tunnel.

Tottenham were already 1-0 down at the time, after dominating the first-half but failing to find the back of the net – a problem they have had regularly this season.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi, meanwhile, said after the game: 'I kissed Bentancur in the dressing room. We need this type of character. Football is character.'

United got their act together in the second period and went 1-0 up through Bryan Mbeumo, and Bentancur's actions made it a near-impossible task for Roberto De Zerbi's side to come back.

They did, though, manage to do just that in stoppage time when Dominic Solanke converted a cross to leave Old Trafford stunned.

Spurs are, though, still without a win this season. They did, however, move from bottom to 18th in the table.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Man United 1-1 Tottenham PLAYER RATINGS: Who has lacked composure all season? And which summer signing put in his best display in a Spurs shirt? Now have YOUR say
Sports.content:
Man United 1-1 Tottenham PLAYER RATINGS: Who has lacked composure all season? And which summer signing put in his best display in a Spurs shirt? Now have YOUR say

In a game neither side could afford to lose, Manchester United and Tottenham played out a 1-1 draw – though the match was short of anything but drama.

Spurs dominated the first-half at Old Trafford but, as has been the case for them so often this season, failed to find the back of the net.

United regrouped after the break and took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo, and it looked as though it would be tough for Spurs to come back when they were reduced to ten men.

Rodrigo Bentancur saw red when he headbutted Luke Shaw in the 78th minute but that didn't deter the away side.

Dominic Solanke got in front of Lisandro Martinez to head in an equaliser, and it was enough for Spurs to take a point back to north London.

Daily Mail Sport's CHRIS WHEELER and MATT BARLOW were at Old Trafford to rate the players.

Manchester United conceded a late equaliser to throw away three points against Tottenham

Man United (4-2-3-1)

SENNE LAMMENS – 5

Has lacked the same composure since his mistake for Belgium at the World Cup. Poor pass out to Mainoo almost cost United early on but at least he made amends with a smart save from Solanke.

LENY YORO – 5

Played out of position again at right back and Spurs focussed on that side of United’s defence but produced two fine interception tackles on Van Hecke and Udogie.

HARRY MAGUIRE – 6

It said much about United’s lack of creativity that the big defender decided to try his luck from 30 yards towards the end. Otherwise looked solid up against the physical challenge from Solanke.

LISANDRO MARTINEZ – 4

Put just enough pressure on Solanke to force him to fire over in front of goal early in the second-half but was outmuscled by the Spurs striker when he equalised to such an extent that Martinez’s back was facing the ball as it came over.

LUKE SHAW – 6

Kept Kudus in check on United’s left and was involved in the main flashpoint of the game towards the end when he reacted angrily to a wild challenge from Bentancur who was sent off for aiming a headbutt at him.

YOURI TIELEMANS – 4

Struggled against the energy of Bergvall and Tonali in midfield. Did well to track back and get a vital touch to deny Gallagher a one-on-one chance before half-time.

KOBBIE MAINOO – 5

Carrick said the England midfielder had done a little bit of training since pulling out of international duty but not enough on this evidence. Vital block to divert Savio’s close-range shot over in the second half.

AMAD DIALLO – 6

Available for the first time this season and went straight into the starting line-up. Probably United’s most dangerous player during his hour on the pitch, but fired tamely at Kinsky with their only chance of the first half and skied another effort into the Stretford End.

Amad Diallo was available for the first time this season for United and was United's most dangerous player while he was on the pitch

BRUNO FERNANDES – 5

Carried a knock playing for Portugal in the international break and looked like it was still affecting him. Very subdued performance by his standards.

MATHEUS CUNHA – 5

The Brazilian has been more effective off the left than as a false nine, and had a hand in the goal. But struggled for much of the game and spent too much time on the floor moaning at the officials.

BRYAN MBEUMO – 7

Amad’s return allowed him to play through the middle, as he did in pre-season, but came to life after reverting to the right before the hour mark as he scored a goal and went close to a second.

Subs

DIOGO DALOT (for Yoro 59) – 6

Booked late on and part of a treble change that was dearly needed.

CARLOS BALEBA (for Tielemans 59) – 6

What a boost it is for United to have him available. United were better with him on the field.

JOSHUA ZIRKZEE (for Diallo 59) – 7

Provided a different option for his side and may find himself being used more than expected depending on Benjamin Sesko's injury status.

MARCUS RASHFORD (for Cunha 90+5)

Manager

MICHAEL CARRICK – 6

A big game for him. Always stone-faced, but will surely be feeling the pressure. Had to cop a lot of stick at various times during the game, and will be livid with how his side finished proceedings. Still under the cosh.

Bryan Mbeumo, meanwhile, scored United's goal but was best when he moved to the right

Tottenham (4-2-3-1)

ANTONIN KINSKY – 6

A complete bystander for the first half hour and very little to do overall. Not a lot he could do when beaten by Mbeumo. Save to deny the United goalscorer a second priceless when Solanke levelled in stoppage time.

ARCHIE GRAY – 6

Solid and determined. Does not always look entirely comfortable at right back but his greatest asset is that he keeps going and refuses to buckle. Kept Cunha quiet for most of the first half forcing Carrick to switch him and Fernandes. Booked.

JAN PAUL VAN HECKE – 5

Sometimes erratic on the ball. Won headers albeit against an attack with little aerial threat. Made tackles on the edge of the penalty box but easily turned by Mbeumo for the United goal. Booked.

MARCOS SENESI – 7

Exuded calm, read the game and used the ball well. Forged a good understanding with Van Hecke. Replaced in the closing stages when De Zerbi wanted Fernandes on.

DESTINY UDOGIE – 7

Kept Amad quiet and drove forward to dovetail well with Savio in the first half. Alert on the cover to make a couple of vital clearances in the second half.

Jan Paul van Hecke (right) was erratic on the ball and found himself spun for United's goal

LUCAS BERGVALL – 6

Terrific energy in opening phase when Spurs took control. Won the ball for early Solanke chance. More vertical drive than Bentancur and fewer mistakes in possession. Faded and replaced.

SANDRO TONALI – 6

Perhaps his best display in a Spurs shirt. Read the game, shielded his centre halves and covered the ground effectively. Still expect more quality on the ball and eventually it came. He was operating as a left back when he produced the cross for Solanke’s goal.

MOHAMMED KUDUS – 5

Bright opening on his first start since January. Got on the ball and tried to create. Good chance squandered in the first half when he fired wide. Faded and withdrawn on 66 minutes.

CONOR GALLAGHER – 7

Exceptional work-rate and effective in the first half. Glimpse of goal denied by an excellent recovery by Tielemans just before half-time. Less influential after half time but still industrious. Booked.

SAVIO – 6

Playing on the left, where his pace off the mark brought early successes one-v-one against Yoro. Quick on the break, good chance created for Solanke second half. Switched to the right when Marmoush came on.

DOMINIC SOLANKE – 6

Surprise captain, showed strength to lead the line and occupied United’s centre halves. Wasted glorious chances at the start of each half but kept going and equalised with a glancing header in stoppage time.

Dominic Solanke (right) was Tottenham's surprise captian for the day and did well tohead a late equaliser for his side

SUBS

OMAR MARMOUSH (on for Kudus 66 mins) – 4

Made little impact as the game slipped away from Spurs.

RODRIGO BENTANCUR (on for Bergvall 66 mins) – 3

Ruined any hopes of a real fightback. First, a reckless tackle and then up to headbutt Shaw sparking a mass skirmish and leaving Spurs to finish the game with ten men.

JAMES MADDISON – (on for Gallagher 74 mins) – 5

United scored as he was waiting to come on and the game changed again with the red card soon after. Tried to get on the ball and make things happen.

MICKY VAN DE VEN (on for Udogie 74 mins) – 5

Came on at left back and ended up back in the middle after Senesi’s late exit.

MATEUS FERNANDES (on for Senesi 90 mins)

MANAGER

ROBERTO DE ZERBI – 6

Rewarded for his faith in the front four he has been working with over the international break. They started at an impressive tempo but could not capitalise. Subs backfired when Bentancur was sent off but will love the spirit shown to fight back.

Sports.title: Pressure mounting on Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa after eight minutes of madness lead to defeat at Ipswich
Sports.content:
Pressure mounting on Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa after eight minutes of madness lead to defeat at Ipswich

Alvaro Arbeloa insists he does not ‘fear’ for his job despite Fulham extending their winless run to six matches after an eight-minute implosion against Ipswich Town.

That said, deep down he must feel the pressure. It is not just the record but the manner of the defeats, consistently dropping points at the death.

In four of their last five matches, they have conceded decisive goals in the last 15 minutes - crumbling when results are decided.

That lack of tenacity to see a game out is a major concern and should leave Arbeloa in a perilous position.

‘I never worry about my position,’ Arbeloa said. I don’t feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it. You have to work, take the decision and you need to show confidence to your players.

‘I am so happy with many things that they are doing. I know it is not easy for them. It’s not about my position, it is about Fulham’s position. That is the most important thing. Obviously it is just six games, but it is true we need points.’

Alvaro Arbeloa may struggle to survive as Fulham manager despite playing some good football

In his maiden press conference, the Portuguese coach requested patience because of Fulham’s tough run of fixtures at the start of the season.

But a manager can only be given so much time. After five games without a win, the fortnight after the international break looked critical on paper, with games against all three promoted sides.

Looking at the run, these fixtures were poised to reveal whether Fulham are genuinely in a relegation battle or have simply been victims of a difficult run of games.

For 87 minutes, there was reason to believe the latter. Fulham moved the ball well, created good chances and got their goal when Ryan Sessegnon picked up Issa Diop’s headed clearance on the edge of the penalty area and drilled into the bottom corner.

But the collapse was catastrophic. Abdoul Ouattara stunned Portman Road with a thunderous left-footed strike on 88 minutes before Dara O'Shea completed the turnaround in stoppage time.

Just four minutes separated the two goals as Fulham folded, lending legitimacy to fears that Arbeloa is the wrong man for the job. His team tired and fatigue kicked in as their belief faded.

Fulham took a risk appointing the inexperienced coach, whose only stint as a senior boss was a brief interim role at Real Madrid.

But by the day, it appears more of a gamble than a calculated decision. With two crucial games to come against teams likely to be in a relegation battle, Arbeloa's position must be evaluated.

If he is afforded more time and the wait for a win extends beyond their matches against Hull and Coventry, Fulham could have major regrets come the end of the season.

Sports.title: Gritty rather than pretty but there's no stopping Brighton - even if Fabian Hurzeler refuses to entertain talk of a title push, writes ROSS HEPPENSTALL
Sports.content:
Nothing, it seems, can stop Brighton right now.

Not Manchester United. Not Arsenal. And not Sunderland, who never looked like breaching a visiting rearguard which comfortably held firm after Pascal Struijk's controversial 57th-minute red card.

Fabian Hurzeler's men, who had opened the scoring moments earlier through Maxim De Cuyper, conjured a delightful late second through Jaouen Hadjam to seal another outstanding win.

SEAGULLS CONTINUE TO SOAR

This was Brighton's fourth straight victory in all competitions and lifted them to within two points of the Premier League summit.

Before the international break, they won 5-0 at Coventry and beat Arsenal 3-0, either side of an impressive 3-2 Carabao Cup victory at Old Trafford.

This latest success was not pretty at times but Hurzeler's men gradually made their superiority pay.

Maxim De Cuyper was on the scoresheet for Brighton as they moved to within two points of the top of the Premier League

No one can stop Fabian Hurzeler's side right now, and Sunderland never really got close

In the 53rd minute, effervescent captain Pascal Gross's intelligent pass found De Cuyper and he drove an excellent, first-time shot past Robin Roefs.

Gross, 35, was named the Premier League Player of the Month for September and Hurzeler smiled: 'I compare Pascal to a good wine – the older the better. Let's see how good the wine gets.'

Struijk then saw red after being adjudged to have hauled down Wilson Isidor as he threatened to break clear.

Neither referee Thomas Bramall nor his assistant gave a foul initially, but video assistant referee (VAR) Neil Davies intervened and Struijk was dismissed.

Brighton defended superbly and then hit their hosts on the counter-attack late on when Georginio Rutter's clever pass found fellow substitute Hadjam and he rifled home a brilliant left-foot finish.

Much is made of Brighton's ability to cut teams apart with pretty passing but this was a win chiselled on obstinate defending.

Hurzeler said: 'I sound a bit old school now but there's a saying 'defence wins championships'… although I'm not speaking about championships!

'Defence wins games and we're known for playing nice football but we don't want to be this nice club anymore.

'We want to be a team who plays effective football and this was a good start.'

Pascal Gross (centre) won the Player of the Month award for the league last season and picked up another assist here

Regis Le Bris' side struggled to make an impact in attacking areas with Brian Brobbey missing

BLACK CATS LACK BITE

With striker Brian Brobbey missing through injury, Wilson Isidor was tasked with leading the line but struggled to make any real impact.

Veteran captain Granit Xhaka also misfired in midfield and next up for Sunderland is a trip to Portuguese outfit Torreense in the Europa League.

Brighton, meanwhile, host Lithuanian side Kauno Zalgiris in the Conference League.

Sports.title: Dapper Laughs DRAWS boxing fight with Joey Essex in controversial decision
Sports.content:
Dapper Laughs DRAWS boxing fight with Joey Essex in controversial decision

Reality TV star Joey Essex took on comedian Dapper Laughs as Misfits Boxing returned to London on Saturday night

View 2 Images Joey Essex punches Dapper Laughs

Dapper Laughs was denied victory over Joey Essex as their boxing fight was controversially scored a draw.

‌



‌



Dapper - real name Daniel O'Reilly - has attempted to rehabilitate his image having been cancelled 16 years ago. He now tours the country doing stand-up comedy under his real name and accepted this fight with Essex on two weeks' notice - primarily to promote his upcoming film.

‌



Both Dapper and Essex had one fight to their name ahead of meeting in the ring with the former stopping Simple Simon three years ago before retreating from the influencer boxing scene.

‌



Misfits Boxing results including Big Stacks and Joey Essex vs Dapper Laughs READ MORE :

Essex, meanwhile, made his Misfits Boxing debut last year, outpointing Numeiro in a slug-fest. The reality TV star, who has appeared on TOWIE and Love Island, is the nephew of renowned boxing trainer Tony Sims and promised a more measured approach on his return to the ring.

And while he was not as gung-ho as he was 12 months ago, Essex struggled to impose himself in the opening round. Dapper, perhaps accepting his fitness would ultimately let him down, looked determined to take the fight to the favourite and landed the bigger shots. Essex laughed off his attacks but was on the end of another right hand in the second session as Dapper looked to take control.

‌



Dapper landed another right hand in the third round as he looked to turn the fight into a brawl. Essex responded with the same shot. But Dapper pushed the younger man back towards the ropes with a right-left combination. Dapper appeared to be tiring as the round drew to a close as Essex marched forwards.

View 2 Images Dapper Laughs punches Joey Essex

Both men began the final session as if they knew they needed to impress the judges. But it was Dapper who had more success with his right hand as he looked to defy the odds. Essex attempted to respond but it was he who was forced backwards under a final assault as the seconds ticked away.

Article continues below

Dapper and his team were the more expectant at the final bell but both men had to settle for a share of the spoils with the judges scoring the fight 37-39, 40-36 and 38-38.

Earlier in the night, Big Stacks, who calls himself the UK's Hardest Man, outpointed former West Ham defender James Collins. The Welshman had stepped in to replace bed salesman Thomas Skinner and did not look out of place.

But Stacks dropped Collins in the third of four rounds with the ex-footballer doing well to get back to his feet. Ultimately, two of the three judges gave Stacks the nod.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick disagrees with Sky Sports pundit's Man Utd claim after blowing win vs Tottenham
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick disagrees with Sky Sports pundit's Man Utd claim after blowing win vs Tottenham

Manchester United could only manage a draw against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford with the Red Devils now said to be lacking confidence

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has questions to answer (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was left to bat away suggestions that Manchester United's slow start against Tottenham was due to a lack of confidence, as they drew at Old Trafford. The Red Devils gave up a 1-0 lead against the Lilywhites as the match ended all square, with accusations that Carrick's team are without self-belief.

‌



‌



The United boss witnessed boos at both the half-time and full-time whistle as his team continued their disappointing start to the season. The club picked up their sixth Premier League point of the season as they failed to hold on against their 10-man opponents, their lowest tally after four matches for 40 years.

‌



With the hosts leading 1-0, Rodrigo Bentancur received his marching orders after headbutting Luke Shaw, yet United couldn't see out the victory as Dominic Solanke struck a late leveller. That saw some fierce criticism after the match.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp delivered a damning verdict on the Premier League's 12th-placed side, slamming the team's organisation. He added that the team's lack of confidence is an issue that Carrick does not have the required squad to deliver the results expected of the club.

"Brighton in the Carabao Cup, 2-0 up and lose 3-2, that is unprecedented and does not happen at Old Trafford, except it does with this team," Redknapp vented.

‌



"I do not see enough connections in that midfield and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back and Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is just a theme this season.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick does not believe confidence was an issue in United's slow start (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"Their energy levels are not good enough and they look loose going forward, there was no real structure. The squad is not good or strong enough and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect."

While Carrick was frustrated with the result, he did not think confidence caused United to start the game slowly. "I don't think it is lack of confidence," he said after the match.

"But a game can get away from you very quickly. We found a way right back into the game, and got ourselves in a great position - that is one of the most disappointing things."

Article continues below

When questioned about the boos directed at his team, he said: "It's not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment. The reality is what it is; we need to get back to winning games."

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Settlement talks with Premier League before punishments agreed
Sports.content:
Man City are in the centre of a major Premier League charges storm

Manchester City are back in Premier League action for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to The Mirror's live blog on Saturday, October 10, as Premier League action returns following the extended international break.

Manchester City are set to return to the pitch for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The club have already launched an appeal after an Independent Commission found them guilty of 114 out of 115 charges relating to the period between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

The allegations include claims that more than £830million in owner funding was used to inflate the club’s revenues through so-called 'sham' agreements. Speculation continues to mount over the potential sanctions City could face, with possible punishments ranging from a substantial fine and points deduction to the prospect of expulsion from the Premier League.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Manager Enzo Maresca has since addressed the media for the first time following the verdict, insisting he has 'complete trust' in the club as attention turns to their return to competitive action.

"Personally, I'm very calm to be honest," said Maresca. "The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club.

"We understand the noise, but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side."

City will face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday with a scheduled kick-off for 4:30pm.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho embarrassed and Vinicius Jr sent off in incredible Real Madrid hair pull drama
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho embarrassed and Vinicius Jr sent off in incredible Real Madrid hair pull drama

Real Madrid ace Vinicius Junior went mad after being shown a red card for pulling their hair of his opponent and seeing his goal cancelled out against Villarreal

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr saw his goal ruled out and he was sent off for a hair pull (Image: La Liga live)

Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior was shown a red card for an audacious hair pull and had a goal ruled out in the process. The Brazilian winger looked to have silenced his haters after getting on the scoresheet, having been booed onto the pitch by Villarreal supporters.

‌



‌



Vinicius entered the fray early in the second half before getting on the scoresheet after 72 minutes. Jubilant scenes followed as the Brazilian enthusiastically celebrated with Jude Bellingham and boss Jose Mourinho.

‌



The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager had even gone racing down the sideline, such was his joy. Both his and Vinicius' moods soon changed as VAR intervened and fury emerged.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The video assistant referee spotted the 26-year-old pulling the hair of Villarreal ace Nathan Saliba as he raced into the opposition half, while Bellingham was in possession of the ball out wide. The England international ultimately provided his team-mate with the ball to double Los Blancos' lead but it was all for nought.

Instead of adding to his goal tally, Vinicius was eventually given his marching orders, provoking a furious reaction as he practically chased referee Isidro Díaz de Mer before leaving the field. It marked the first time VAR had overturned a goal and provided a red card simultaneously

‌



The decision meant that Real were required to defend a one-goal lead with 10 men, which they managed successfully. Yann Diomande made the important contribution after the summer signing started ahead of Vinicius.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr celebrated with Jose Mourinho following his disallowed goal (Image: Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr was furious to be shown red (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

‌



Real Madrid TV has already broadcast their frustration with the referee's performance. "You can call it a foul by Vinicius, but the problem arises when this VAR referee hasn't called for the red card shown to Carlos Romero in the match against Espanyol for two seasons," says Real Madrid TV.

Referee Pablo González Fuertes revealed that his colleague made the right decision to send off the Real Madrid star, however. Speaking on Radio Marca, He said: ""A correct sending-off because it was a very blatant hair-pull on Saliba.

"It was violent conduct on the part of the Real Madrid forward. And, logically, the goal was correctly disallowed."

Article continues below

Depending on the referee's report, Vinicius could now miss the Clasico against Barcelona in two weeks.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick addresses Man Utd boos amid fan backlash and addresses new 'reality'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick addresses Man Utd boos amid fan backlash and addresses new 'reality'

Michael Carrick saw Manchester United underwhelm once again as they were held by Tottenham, which saw the Old Trafford crowd boo on multiple occasions

View 2 Images Michael Carrick had to face several boos from the Old Trafford crowd

Michael Carrick concedes he understands the boos from the Old Trafford crowd, but they still hurt after seeing his Manchester United side drop more points.

‌



‌



The Red Devils conceded in stoppage time to Tottenham, who had dominated for the majority of the game. Bryan Mbeumo scored the game's opening goal on 70 minutes, but only after the north Londoners, without a win in the Premier League, had outclassed the hosts.

‌



They missed chance after chance, but finally found the net on 92 minutes courtesy of a Dominic Solanke header. United were booed off at half-time, and again at the final whistle.

‌



That frustration is not lost on Carrick, who is already feeling the pressure in what is his first season at the helm. The ex-player had an impressive interim spell last term and landed the job permanently, but has presided over United's worst start to a season since 1986.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Addressing the boos he told BBC's Match of the Day: "It's not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games."

‌



United have continued to let leads slip during games, Saturday being yet another example, with Carrick's poor run of results coming despite a generous fixture list.

The Red Devils boss said on another lacklustre showing: "I don't think it is lack of confidence, but a game can get away from you very quickly. We found a way right back into the game, and got ourselves in a great position - that is one of the most disappointing things.

View 2 Images Man Utd have won just one of their opening six games

‌



"It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

"But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That's two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That's the reality."

United have only won the once this season, against newly promoted Ipswich, as they remain in the bottom half of the table. Their next assignment sees them head to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League before returning to domestic action against rivals Leeds at Elland Road.

Sports.title: Five Liverpool players facing tough chats as Andoni Iraola reveals his golden rule
Sports.content:
Five Liverpool players facing tough chats as Andoni Iraola reveals his golden rule

Andoni Iraola has opened up on the honest approach he takes to selection and managing his squad - with several Liverpool stars likely having those conversations with the Reds' boss

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola is prepared to be honest with his Liverpool players regarding their standing in the squad (Image: Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola insists he's more than happy to be honest with his Liverpool players when it comes to their standing within the squad.

‌



‌



The Spaniard, still adapting to his new role having been appointed in the summer, has inherited a group built by Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot. Despite some holes, it is not without quality, which has left plenty of competition for places.

‌



The former Bournemouth boss, chasing his first Anfield win in the Premier League this weekend, admits he's no interest in stringing on members of his squad when it comes to where they sit in his pecking order.

‌



Iraola has opened up on the approach he takes with his players - some of whom will be regular starters, others may be fighting for their position and some may have to accept that several individuals are preferred to them at any one time.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He told the club's website: “You cannot tell a player if he comes here to talk to you, ‘Don’t worry, you will have your chances’ and maybe he doesn’t have the chances.

‌



“I prefer to tell him, ‘Hey, you have to fight for your position. You are in a difficult place because I’m preferring this one in front.’ So it’s more a challenge.

“And even if you are thinking that he will have minutes, I don’t like to tell him, ‘Don’t worry, you will play.’ Because that’s a mistake when you promise, ‘Don’t worry, you will play a lot, you will have your minutes.’ Maybe he’s not playing well or he’s not deserving the minutes and then you cannot give him those minutes and you have a problem there."

View 5 Images Bradley Barcola's arrival has changed the dynamics in the frontline

‌



Iraola ultimately concludes: “It's impossible to be fair with everyone, but I prefer to say every decision has to be putting the team first. Even if it’s difficult for me, the decision, if it is for the benefit of the team you have to take it.”

Despite their being calls for Liverpool to bolster areas of their squad sooner rather than later, other positions are well stocked, which is leaving certain players to miss out or remain patient. It means their manager's honest conversations will take on even more importance as several players question where they stand, we take a look at a few who might be having those chats.

Alexis Mac Allister

The Argentine was happy to go public recently as he lamented his contract situation, seeing some of his midfield colleagues sign new long-term deals. Mac Allister has started in three of Liverpool's five games in the league, but with Florian Wirtz acting as the team's 10, it has left only two midfield spots available.

‌



View 5 Images Alexis Mac Allister has publicly aired his frustration

Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch are both very much in favour, so Iraola will have to be managing a player who must, internally, be questioning whether those at Anfield see him as a long-term asset.

Victor Munoz

The Spaniard was convinced to move to Liverpool ahead of Newcastle in the summer, but that was before more than £100million was spent on Bradley Barcola. Such a mammoth investment makes the Frenchman hard to leave out. And that effectively leaves only one wing spot still up for grabs.

‌



Munoz came off the bench to rescue a point against Nottingham Forest, showing what he can do, but that hasn't meant he's been promoted to a weekly starter. He has started in three of the five games so far, which will give him confidence, but there is certainly a rotation game to be played in the final third.

View 5 Images Liverpool have high hopes for Rio Ngumoha (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Rio Ngumoha

The hype is notable, so much so that the teenager will do well to not notice it. Slot was under pressure to give him more minutes before he was axed, but Ngumoha hasn't started since the opening game of the season. He's already had to digest being an unused substitute.

‌



When you're 18 it is easy to want to be in a hurry. And there's a balance to strike between letting youth just flourish, which requires minutes, but equally managing expectations and protecting such talents. Iraola has a tough task on his hands there.

Cody Gakpo

Before the summer transfer window shut he was heavily linked with a move to Manchester City, which seemed like a natural move with Barcola coming in as the blockbuster recruit. Ironically it seems to have spurred on the Dutchman, who has been perhaps the best performing attacker at Anfield to start the campaign

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo had looked set to leave Liverpool in the summer (Image: Richard Lee/Shutterstock)

‌



That has made managing him and his expectations all the more challenging for Iraola, who on form would perhaps have Gakpo as the first name on the team sheet. But there's a determination to get the best from Alexander Isak, Wirtz and now Barcola. All of which leaves Gakpo with games that will have to see him on the bench.

Joe Gomez

It feels mental that he's not even 30 yet given how long he's been at the club. Gomez played under Brendan Rodgers, underlining the extent of his spell at Anfield. Gomez though has been constantly struck down by injuries, and that continued in pre-season, which has put him on the back foot.

He returned for the bench recently and his first appearance came in the Carabao Cup, but with Ronald Araujo coming in from Barcelona to aid Virgil van Dijk, the battle to be a first choice centre-half has ramped up. Gomez is known for his versatility, but Iraola is persevering with the team's full-backs at present.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Tottenham descends into chaos as red card sparks huge clash
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Tottenham descends into chaos as red card sparks huge clash

Tottenham went down to 10 men when players from both teams clashed late in the match at Old Trafford with Spurs already a goal down against Manchester United

View 2 Images Rodrigo Bentancur clashes with Luke Shaw (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off after clashing heads with Luke Shaw as Manchester United vs Tottenham threatened to descend into chaos. With United 1-0 up, Bentancur reacted rashly after being shoved to the ground.

‌



‌



Shaw pushed over his rival after Bentancur had launched the ball away following some flying tackles. The Uruguay international quickly got back to his feet and moved his head towards the United defender.

‌



The full-back hit the floor, dramatically clutching his face as bodies from both teams quickly came together. A melee ensued as Shaw and Jan Paul van Hecke came away with yellow cards in addition to Bentancur's red.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The offence means Tottenham have received five red cards since the start of last season, with London rivals Chelsea the only side to have earned more, having racked up eight.

On commentary, Gary Neville was in disbelief over Bentancur's actions. "It's madness from Bentancur to get involved," he said.

‌



"Lack of discipline is not what he needs. The scissors tackle, that's a yellow, Shaw pushes him and he comes up... He just gets up and leads towards him doesn't he? It'll always result in a red, especially after the challenge, it's just stupidity."

View 2 Images Tempers flared at Old Trafford (Image: Sky Sports)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Former Tottenham star Chris Waddle believes that Shaw also should have been given his marching orders. Waddle said: "Luke Shaw has stepped out of line there and has sort of held his head as though he's been headbutted.

"If Rodrigo Bentancur's got a red for it, Luke Shaw should have a red too. You can't raise your hands. Where's VAR?"

Sutart Atwell's decision to send off Bentancur for a headbutt was checked by the video assistant referee. “I’ve got a red card for Bentancur for a headbutt," said Atwell.

‌



VAR, Jarred Gillett, responded: “He puts his head into Shaw with some force – that’s violent conduct. He stands up and into Shaw and there’s a movement of the head”.

Spurs were able to come back from behind despite being down a man against United. They were trailing thanks to Bryan Mbeumo's strike when the melee ensued.

Dominic Solanke was able to hold off Lisandro Martinez to gently glance the ball past Lammens to earn Spurs a point away from home.
