Israeli attack destroys building in Gaza one year into ‘ceasefire’

NewsFeed Israeli attack destroys building in Gaza one year into ‘ceasefire’

An Israeli strike destroyed a residential building in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood in Gaza City, sending flames and smoke into the air. The attack comes one year into a US-brokered ceasefire, yet Palestinians continue to face Israeli bombardment.

World.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.

"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".

Global fuel supplies, including diesel, have been severely limited by the war against Iran launched by the US and Israel, which led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil products usually flows.

Russia - a major producer - and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes on each other's energy infrastructure and transport facilities, further straining energy markets.

"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," Trump continued.

"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."

Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace".

The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.

Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.

He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

World.title: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 20 people
World.content:
Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 20 people including four children, local officials said.

The glide bombs hit residential buildings in the southern city on Saturday morning. At least 32 others were injured in the attack, with more still missing and believed to be under the rubble.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing "its thanks" for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump last night easing sanctions on Moscow to import Russian diesel.

He added that 13 other regions had come under attack overnight, arguing this demonstrated Russia took "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting".

Photos and videos from the site of one of the strikes in Zaporizhzhia show an apartment block mostly destroyed.

"The ground floor was hit, and the floors above just collapsed," acting Mayor Regina Harchenko told Ukrainian television from the scene.

She said more than 80 workers were involved in ongoing search and rescue operations which are expected to continue throughout the day.

The rescuers regularly stop to listen for any noises made by survivors who could be under the rubble.

Harchenko said Russia had struck at "our very heart" and "our littlest ones" were among those killed, adding that their deaths were "awful grief for their families. For the city."

Zaporizhzhia is a major regional centre with more than 700,000 residents. It is located less than 10 miles (16km) from the front line and is frequently attacked by Russian drones and missiles.

World.title: Several injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
World.content:
Several people have been injured in another attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have carried out similar strikes on the hub.

Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were suspended on Saturday after the attack, the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said in a statement.

More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness.

The US embassy said it was "aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport" and urged American citizens to avoid the airport and surrounding areas.

A projectile also fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition which is fighting the Houthis said.

The attack comes a day after authorities said three Saudis including a pilot were killed in two attacks on the airport by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.

A source at a local hospital told AFP that dozens of people had been wounded in Saturday's attack.

An eyewitness who said they had been in the domestic terminal told the news agency that they had seen gate 401 hit and "injured [people] in front of my eyes", adding: "Everyone was running."

Western embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens away from the airport, while the UK Foreign Office told British nationals to stay away "until the airport is secure and to monitor the advice of the Saudi authorities".

Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there.

All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows.

Doctors had been asked to report to hospitals to address the situation, a medical source told AFP.

"We were told we are dealing with a 'serious emergency situation'," the medical source told the agency.

The suspected attack comes during a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west.

The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war.

The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.

That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.

A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government.

A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

But the informal truce began to unravel in July.

The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport.

World.title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
World.content:
US death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital following her botched execution at the end of last month, her lawyers have said.

Pike, 50, has been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years and is continuing to receive medical care, according to a statement from her lawyers on Saturday.

She survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September, which left her in a critical condition.

Pike regained consciousness earlier this week and began speaking - stunning experts, medical staff and her lawyers.

Her case is now in uncharted territory as she is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

World.title: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
World.content:
Four people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain.

Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses.

At least 600,000 people were without power in several states as of Saturday afternoon, according to tracker PowerOutage.

Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone.

The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people.

Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon is bearing down on Mexico's Pacific coast and has strengthened to category four. It is expected to make landfall sometime overnight.

And Tropical Storm Rachel, also in the Pacific Ocean, is edging towards land and is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday.

World.title: Expedition hopes to find aviator Amelia Earhart's plane on remote island
World.content:
A team of researchers are on their way to a remote island to inspect what they think could be the wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart's plane.

The group, from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University, are expected to arrive at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean by Monday in the hopes of solving the mystery of her disappearance.

The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation on her fate.

The team are aiming to find what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020.

Purdue University said the object had since been confirmed to have been visible in aerial photography of the area dating back to 1938.

The researchers are currently roughly halfway through their journey to the remote atoll aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel.

They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country.

When they eventually arrive, they will have to navigate through a narrow gap created in the atoll's reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.

"Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the ALI and the expedition lead, said.

World.title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
World.content:
A woman has been arrested after injuring three people in a third knife attack recorded at schools in Poland this week.

The 21-year-old used a "dangerous object" to attack a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital, Warsaw, police told news agencies PAP and AP.

It comes a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland, following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which led to the killing of a female caretaker.

A Warsaw police spokesperson said they could not confirm whether the latest incident was related to the two previous attacks.

Authorities told local media that the 17-year-old injured on Saturday had been taken to hospital, but her condition was not life-threatening.

Two other women aged 17 and 24, who had gone in to submit enrolment documents, were also injured, Poland's state news agency reported.

Police told local media that the suspected attacker was a student at the school and initial findings suggested that she did not know the three victims.

Schools in Poland had been stepping up security following knife attacks at schools across the country on 7 and 8 October. Polish police said they had detained 76 people after deploying to schools across the country.

"When it comes to the safety of Polish children and peace in our schools, there is no room for compromise," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said ahead of the operation.

Local media, citing a police spokesperson, reported authorities had information to suggest incidents this past week could be related to an internet challenge.

On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian.

A day later, a 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in LeszczydÃ³Å-Nowiny, north of Warsaw.

Interior Minister Marcin KierwiÅski also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone".

World.title: Nobel peace laureate says US sanctions on ICC 'unacceptable'
World.content:
Navi Pillay, the winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize, has called US sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) "unheard of" and "unacceptable".

The South African former ICC judge was awarded the prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", which paved the way for a "more comprehensive global legal order", the Nobel committee said.

US President Donald Trump expressed his disatisfaction with the pick and hours later the US unveiled sweeping sanctions in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it described as a "rogue" institution.

The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.

Pillay, speaking via video link during an event at the Nobel Peace Center in Oslo on Saturday, said: "There is so much tension and anxiety over the continued existence of international courts, mainly the International Criminal Court in The Hague.

"Most importantly, sanctions have been announced by one country against the judges, just for the judicial orders they issue. This is unheard of, unacceptable."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier said the sanctions - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans.

The US has already sanctioned 17 ICC judges and officials, but this move sanctions the court itself as an institution and is intended to inhibit its ability to operate financially.

However, the US has provided a six-month grace period before some of these latest sanctions kick in, meaning member states can keep paying for its operations - a move Washington says is to allow countries time to negotiate a "solution to address" US concerns.

The Trump administration claims that the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty.

It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar".

The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in saying they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions.

World.title: Benue: Suspected herdsmen kill nine in fresh Ukum attacks
World.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

At least nine persons have reportedly been killed in fresh attacks by suspected armed herdsmen on Tse-Nyaku, Tse-Biliji and adjoining communities in Mbatian Council Ward of Ngenev, Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.

Several others were reportedly injured, while an unspecified number of residents were said to be missing following the attacks, which began at about 11pm on Friday.

A local source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the assailants invaded the communities in large numbers, shooting sporadically and forcing residents to flee their homes.

According to the source, nine bodies had so far been recovered from the affected communities.

“The attackers came in large numbers and started shooting in the communities. Luckily, many people managed to escape, except for the nine who have been confirmed dead for now because their corpses have been recovered.

“However, it is very likely that the number could increase because many people have not been seen, and no one knows whether they were killed or escaped to other communities.

“Our people discovered that one of armed herdsmen is in possession of the phones of one of the victims and he has been using it to make and receive calls.

“The attacked communities have also already been deserted. It is a very sad day for our people. The Sankera axis of Benue has become a shadow of itself due to the level of insecurity,” he said.

Reacting to the incident, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate for Ukum I (Ngenev) State Constituency in the Benue State House of Assembly, Livinus Tyodoo, described the invasion as “one attack too many.”

In a statement he personally signed, Tyodoo said he received disturbing reports of the deadly attacks on the communities on Friday night and in the early hours of Saturday.

He said the attacks, allegedly carried out by suspected herdsmen militia, had reportedly claimed more than nine lives, adding that several bodies had been recovered while other residents remained missing and some survivors sustained varying degrees of injuries.

“This is one attack too many. I unequivocally condemn the senseless killing, displacement and continued persecution of innocent citizens in their ancestral homes.

“The people of Ukum I (Ngenev) deserve to live in peace, cultivate their farmlands and pursue their legitimate means of livelihood without the constant fear of violence.

“Human civilisation has evolved beyond the Hobbesian state of nature, where life was characterised by insecurity and the constant fear of violent death. In the 21st century, the sanctity of human life must remain paramount, and no community should be abandoned to the mercy of armed assailants,” he said.

Tyodoo stressed that the incident should not be politicised, urging the authorities to take urgent and decisive action to prevent further bloodshed.

“This is not the time for politics or the exchange of blame. It is a time for urgent, coordinated and decisive action,” he said.

He called on the Benue State Government, Ukum Local Government Council and relevant security agencies to strengthen security operations in the affected communities and other vulnerable areas of the local government.

According to him, beyond issuing statements and ordering investigations, the government must ensure effective intelligence gathering, proactive security deployments, the arrest and prosecution of those responsible, and concrete measures to prevent further attacks.

“Our people must be able to return to their ancestral homes, reclaim their farmlands and carry on with their daily activities without fear. The protection of lives and property is a fundamental responsibility of government, and the people of Ukum deserve nothing less,” he added.

The PDP candidate also expressed condolences to the families of those reportedly killed, while praying for the safe return of missing persons and the speedy recovery of the injured.

“I pray for the peaceful repose of the souls of the departed, comfort for the bereaved families, the safe return of anyone still missing, and a speedy recovery for those who sustained injuries.

“May God comfort our grieving communities, protect our people and restore lasting peace to Ngenev, Ukum and Benue State at large. The time for urgent action is now. Our people deserve security, justice and lasting peace,” he said.

When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, said he was yet to receive a report on the incident.

World.title: PSG ease to Ligue 1 win before Manchester City test
World.content:
PSG’s Georgian forward #07 Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (C) celebrates Paris Saint-Germain’s victory with teammates at the end of the French L1 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and Le Mans FC at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 10, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

Paris Saint-Germain were comfortable 3-1 winners against Le Mans on Saturday before they look ahead to a tougher test away to Manchester City in the Champions League next week.

Their third win in a row after a slow start to the season came despite resting a host of players.

PSG went ahead through a first-half spot kick from centre-back Lucas Beraldo but Louis Mafouta brought Le Mans level at the Parc des Princes nine minutes after half-time.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia spent the first half on the bench but he put PSG ahead on 61 minutes, just two minutes after he was brought on, before Maghnes Akliouche wrapped up the win seven minutes later.

PSG move up to fifth before the back-to-back European champions travel to City, who are reeling after being found guilty of dozens of Premier League spending infractions, on Wednesday.

Monaco missed a chance to open up a two-point lead at the top as they were held to a 2-2 home draw by Toulouse.

They lead Lille by a single point after the northern side beat Le Havre 1-0 at home.

World.title: Ogun PDP urges calm over Adebutu’s omission from INEC list
World.content:
Adebutu

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has called on its members and supporters to remain calm following the omission of its governorship candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, from a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), expressing confidence that the issue would be resolved ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The opposition party alleged that the development was the result of pressure from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which it accused of being apprehensive about the PDP’s chances in the forthcoming election.

The party, however, maintained that Adebutu remained a bona fide member of the PDP, insisting that he had fulfilled the party’s membership registration requirements within the stipulated period.

In a statement issued by its Publicity Secretary, Arc. Kayode Adebayo, the PDP said, participated in the party’s digital membership registration exercise, during which his membership card was printed and verified before being submitted to INEC within the prescribed timeframe.

“We state emphatically that our candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has never left the Peoples Democratic Party at any time. He duly registered as a member of the party within the designated period of the digital registration exercise, and his membership card was printed, verified and submitted to INEC at the stipulated time,” the statement said.

The party attributed the omission to what it described as political interference, alleging that the APC was seeking to undermine its chances ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

“The omission of our candidate’s name from INEC’s list is a consequence of the undue pressure allegedly mounted on the commission by the ruling party out of fear of losing the election to our party,” Adebayo stated.

The PDP, however, expressed optimism that Adebutu’s name would be included in the relevant list of candidates, reaffirming its commitment to participating in the 2027 governorship election.

It urged the people of Ogun State not to be distracted by the development, calling on its members and supporters to remain focused on their political objectives and continue mobilising for the forthcoming election.

“While we urge the good people of Ogun State not to be perturbed or distracted from our collective resolve to vote out the APC, we remain resolute, unfazed and unwaveringly confident that our candidate is marching towards a decisive victory in the 2027 governorship election,” the statement added.

The opposition party further maintained that the development would not diminish what it described as the determination of the people of Ogun State to demand better governance and positive change.

“No amount of desperate manipulation, political witch-hunts or calculated distractions can alter the mandate of the people of Ogun State, who are overwhelmingly eager for true leadership and positive change,” the PDP said.

Reiterating its appeal for calm, the party urged its members, supporters and other stakeholders to remain steadfast and undeterred as it intensifies its political activities ahead of the election.

“Once again, we call on all our teeming supporters, party faithful and the general public to remain steadfast, vigilant and unintimidated as the unstoppable movement to rescue Ogun State and bring relief to our people continues to gain momentum,” the statement said.

World.title: Real Madrid edge Villarreal, Vinicius sent off for hair pull
World.content:
Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward #07 Vinicius Junior (C) is restrained by teammates as he argues with referee Isidro Escuderos after receiving a red card during the Spanish league football match between Real Madrid CF and Villarreal CF at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Yan Diomande earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair-pulling.

Brazil international Vinicius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.

Jose Mourinho’s Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to win and go provisionally third.

Champions Barca lead La Liga after a 3-0 win over Getafe, while Atletico Madrid are five points behind in second after they edged Alaves 2-1.

Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break.

There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from other supporters.

Mbappe, a candidate for the Ballon d’Or trophy later this month, was Madrid’s most threatening player in the first half, although he had little competition.

Mourinho started with out-of-form winger Vinicius on the bench, following his trips to Australia and India with Brazil during the international break.

Madrid improved defensively, giving Villarreal few chances of note, but struggled to build much in attack themselves in a drab opening half.

Mbappe struck the post from Alvaro Carreras’s lay-off as Madrid pushed Villarreal back early on.

Villarreal soon gained a foothold and restricted Madrid’s opportunities, until Mbappe forced a good save from Peter Gulacsi.

There was some more mild whistling for Madrid’s display from their fans at half-time, but soon they were able to celebrate summer arrival Diomande’s first goal for the club.

The Ivorian winger, Madrid’s record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, produced a sharp low finish into the far corner after good work from Federico Valverde to play him in.

Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid’s lead after Jude Bellingham charged in down the left and cut the ball back for him.

However the winger’s joy turned to anger after referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called to watch Vinicius’s hair pull on Saliba in the build-up by VAR and sent off the Brazilian, voiding his goal.

Madrid’s Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who had made a couple of smart saves earlier in the half, produced an acrobatic stop to thwart Carlos Romero.

Mbappe was denied again by Hungarian goalkeeper Gulasci as the forward left the Bernabeu frustrated in his hunt for goals, although his team were able to clinch three important points to stay on Barca’s trail.

World.title: Regina Daniels marks 25th birthday in wheelchair
World.content:
Nollywood actress Regina Daniels has disclosed that she has endured months of severe pain and difficulty walking, revealing that her condition has left her dependent on a wheelchair.

The actress shared the update in a video posted on her Instagram page on Saturday to celebrate her 25th birthday, using the opportunity to explain her absence from social media.

Daniels, a mother of two, said what initially appeared to be a minor health problem gradually worsened, leaving her unable to move freely and sometimes preventing her from walking.

“I know many of you may be surprised seeing me in a wheelchair. Well, welcome to another chapter of my life. Let me walk you through what my life has been since many of you have asked questions about my absence,” she said.

Recounting how her condition deteriorated, Daniels said she began experiencing more serious symptoms after hosting a children’s day carnival.

“For several months now, I have lost my freedom to move around as I please. It started as something minor, very minor, but eventually led to this.

“But things took a major turn after the last public gathering I hosted, my children’s day carnival. One test after another, I jokingly started calling myself a lab rat. The pain became excruciating. Sometimes I can walk, and sometimes I can’t move. I cried,” she added.

The actress expressed gratitude for the progress she said she had made in her recovery, noting that recent developments had encouraged her to speak publicly about her health.

“Well, me sitting here today, in front of this camera, sharing this with y’all, it’s because there’s been some really significant developments in my recovery. And I say, thank you, Lord,” she said.

Daniels also described the emotional difficulties associated with her condition, particularly having to rely on others for assistance with routine activities.

Despite the challenges, she said her faith in God had helped her through the experience and expressed hope for healing and peace.

The actress further disclosed that she had moved closer to her loved ones, especially her children, whom she described as being particularly dear to her.

She said she initially rented the property she moved into but later developed an interest in owning it.

Daniels married businessman and politician Ned Nwoko in 2019, and the couple have two children. Their relationship has since been marked by a public and contentious separation.

World.title: Tinubu’ll take Nigeria from reforms to prosperity if re-elected – First Lady
World.content:
First Lady Sen Oluremi Tinubu says President Bola Tinubu will move Nigeria from economic reforms to prosperity if re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Tinubu said this on Saturday in Lafia at the North-Central Mega Rally organised by the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

The First Lady urged party members to take the campaign to communities across the region and mobilise voters for the party’s candidates.

She highlighted some achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors, saying continuity was necessary to sustain the gains.

“President Tinubu is a man who believes in the unity, security and prosperity of our nation.

“The Independence Day message of Mr President was titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’.

“Therefore, Mr President is saying that they are going to reform the sector, but now is the time for prosperity, and we can see our economy is stabilising.

“Foreign exchange is going down, and investors are coming back to Nigeria, our farmers too. You can see all our governors here; they are doing infrastructural development like no other time before.

“I have been in the Senate for 12 years. This is the best time I will see the government fixing roads and building a lot of infrastructure,” she said.

Tinubu also cited the administration’s food support programme, saying it was designed to provide nutritious food for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.

“As you see now, we have just finished the food bank programme, where we are helping every child and mothers who are pregnant and also breastfeeding.

“This is to ensure that they can have more nutritious food, and also the children that are malnourished can get treatment and also get food to grow healthy,” she said.

She added that students were also benefiting from the administration’s education funding initiatives.

The First Lady urged party members to communicate the administration’s policies and programmes to Nigerians in their respective states.

She described Tinubu as a leader willing to take difficult decisions, expressing confidence that his policies would strengthen the economy and improve security.

She said the administration would continue to pursue a stronger economy, safer communities and a greater Nigeria if returned to office.

The First Lady also said the APC women’s wing had united its campaign efforts to promote a common message and goal ahead of the 2027 general elections.

She said the party’s campaign would focus on its programmes and policies without resorting to hate speech or actions capable of undermining national unity.

“Therefore, vote for continuity, vote for capacity, vote for prosperity, and vote for the re-election of Mr President and all the candidates of APC from top to bottom,” she said.

The rally was hosted by Gov. Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa, with governors and other political leaders from the North-Central region in attendance. (NAN)

World.title: US jails Nigerian 30 months over email fraud
World.content:
A United States federal court has sentenced a Nigerian national, Edikan Adiakpan, to 30 months’ imprisonment for his involvement in a business email fraud scheme targeting American companies.

The U.S. Department of Justice disclosed this in a statement issued by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas.

The department said Adiakpan, 35, a Houston resident, pleaded guilty on May 12 to illegally transmitting proceeds from an email fraud scheme.

U.S. District Judge Andrew Hanen sentenced him to 30 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release.

According to the department, Adiakpan operates a company known as Akama Lifestyle, which he advertised as a luxury car service.

However, prosecutors said he used the company between 2020 and 2022 to transfer money received from fraudsters in exchange for a percentage of the proceeds.

The funds originated from a business email compromise scheme that targeted more than 10 victims.

The department explained that the fraudsters sent emails impersonating legitimate suppliers and creditors to deceive businesses into transferring payments to fraudulent bank accounts.

One victim, a small utility trailer company in Mississippi, lost substantial funds after receiving fraudulent payment instructions.

According to prosecutors, the company transferred $927,080 to the fraudsters, believing it was paying a legitimate supplier.

The fraudsters subsequently transferred portions of the proceeds to Adiakpan.

The department said Adiakpan deposited and redeemed several cashier’s cheques payable to himself and his luxury car company.

It said the transactions involved $359,000 belonging to the Mississippi company.

A victim impact statement describing the financial consequences of the fraud was presented during Adiakpan’s sentencing hearing.

The department disclosed that Adiakpan had temporary legal status in the United States when he was arrested.

It also identified another Nigerian, Ayobami Omoniyi, 27, as having participated in the scheme, and was subsequently sentenced on March 24 to 32 months in federal prison for his role.

The investigation was conducted by the FBI’s Houston Field Office and Bryan Resident Agency, alongside the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation Division, while Assistant U.S. Attorney Belinda Beek prosecuted the case. (NAN)

World.title: Amaechi faults Tinubu’s fuel subsidy removal, cites hardship
World.content:
Mr Rotimi Amaechi, vice presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s handling of fuel subsidy removal, citing its impact on Nigerians.

Amaechi, a former Minister of Transportation and Rivers governor, spoke on Saturday at a town hall meeting in Calabar.

He said the government should have consulted economists, political scientists and other stakeholders before implementing the policy.

The former minister argued that adequate measures should have been introduced to cushion the effects of subsidy removal on Nigerians.

According to him, courage in policymaking must be balanced with careful planning and consideration of the consequences for citizens.

Amaechi illustrated his argument with an analogy involving a moving train, warning that bold decisions could carry risks without proper preparation.

He said the administration’s approach raised questions about whether sufficient attention had been paid to the welfare of Nigerians.

The ADC chieftain also suggested that political considerations might have influenced the policy, linking the administration’s approach to the outcome of the 2023 presidential election.

He noted that subsidy removal had significantly increased transportation costs and other essential expenses across the country.

Amaechi questioned the government’s response to the rising cost of living, stressing the need for measures to ease economic pressure on households.

He also expressed readiness to debate members of the administration’s economic team on the policy and possible solutions to its consequences.

The former minister said the opposition would challenge the ruling party through democratic and constitutional processes ahead of the next election.

“The opposition intends to pursue the electoral process without resorting to post-election litigation, and we are confident in our approach,” he said. (NAN)

World.title: CAS Visits Home Unit of Ill-Fated ATR, Reaffirms Support for Personnel, Families
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has visited 107 Air Maritime Group (AMG), Nigerian Air Force (NAF) Base, Benin City, the home unit of the ill-fated NAF ATR 42 aircraft, where he met with personnel and reassured the families of those affected by the recent accident of the Service’s continued support during this difficult period.

Addressing personnel of the unit, Aneke expressed profound condolences over the loss of their colleagues, describing the deceased as dedicated patriots who served the nation with honour and commitment.

“Our thoughts and prayers remain with the families of our fallen colleagues,” he said.

According to a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the CAS stressed that the personnel had made the ultimate sacrifice in the service of the nation and that the nation would not forget them or their contributions to the Nigerian Air Force.

He further assured the bereaved families that the NAF would continue to stand by them, providing the necessary emotional, administrative and institutional support.

Reaffirming the Service’s commitment to their welfare, Air Marshal Aneke also acknowledged the provision of scholarship awards for the children of the deceased personnel, noting that their well-being remained a priority.

“We will continue to do everything within our capacity to support the families and ensure that the children of our fallen comrades are not left without support. Their welfare is our responsibility, and we will remain committed to it,” he stated.

On efforts to restore and strengthen 107 AMG, the CAS assured personnel that the Service would take the necessary measures to improve their welfare, sustain training and facilitate the availability of operational platforms.

“We will support this unit to quickly regain its strength. That support will include welfare, training and the availability of the platforms required for you to continue performing your duties effectively. We expect you to remain focused, professional and resilient,” he said.

In his response, the Commander of 107 AMG, Air Commodore Onu, expressed appreciation to the CAS for visiting the unit at such a difficult time and for reassuring personnel and the families of the deceased of the Service’s continued support.

“Sir, your presence here has strengthened the morale of our personnel. We appreciate your leadership, concern and commitment to the welfare of our people. We remain resolute and committed to our responsibilities, despite the challenges we are currently facing,” he said.

Onu further assured the CAS that personnel of the unit would remain dedicated to their duties and continue to uphold the traditions and professional standards of the NAF.

The CAS also commended the personnel of 107 AMG for their professionalism, resilience and unwavering dedication in the face of adversity, urging them to remain steadfast as search, recovery and investigative efforts continued.

He expressed appreciation to the Nigerian Navy and other security agencies for their invaluable support in the search and recovery operations, noting that the collaboration underscored the importance of jointness and inter-Service cooperation in responding to national challenges.

Reaffirming the NAF’s commitment to its personnel and their families, Aneke assured all those affected that the Service would continue to provide the necessary support while pursuing a thorough and professional investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident.

World.title: Shettima: Nigeria’ll Deepen Nutrition 774 With Lessons From Ethiopia
World.content:
.Back in Abuja after three-day Nigeria–Ethiopia nutrition leadership exchange



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice President Kashim Shettima has said Nigeria will deepen the implementation of the Nutrition 774 Initiative with practical lessons from Ethiopia’s experience in tackling malnutrition, strengthening food systems and coordinating nutrition interventions across different levels of government.

The Vice President said the knowledge gained from the three-day Nigeria–Ethiopia Nutrition Leadership Exchange would be adapted to Nigeria’s realities, particularly in strengthening collaboration among the federal government, states and local governments to improve nutrition outcomes at the community and household levels.

Shettima spoke as he returned to Abuja yesterday after leading Nigeria’s delegation to the leadership exchange in Addis Ababa and Oromia, Ethiopia, themed ‘Moving the Needle on Nutrition’.

During the visit, the Vice President according to a statement issued by his Media Assistant, Stanley Nkwocha, held a bilateral meeting with Ethiopia’s Deputy Prime Minister, Temesgen Tiruneh, where both leaders reviewed bilateral relations and explored opportunities for deeper cooperation in agriculture, trade, investment, food security, aviation and other areas of mutual interest.

At the opening session of the exchange, Shettima emphasised the value of African countries learning from one another, noting that Ethiopia’s Seqota Declaration and Nigeria’s Nutrition 774 Initiative provide useful platforms for sharing home-grown approaches to addressing malnutrition.

He also highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to strengthen nutrition financing, accountability and subnational implementation, stressing that improved nutrition is critical to human capital development, productivity and economic growth.

On the second day of the programme, the Vice President led governors, ministers and other stakeholders on field engagements across Oromia focused on agriculture value-chain transformation.

The delegation visited wheat, banana and papaya farms, the “Bounty of the Basket” Training Centre and households in Mojo, as well as other facilities, to study how agricultural production, food systems and value-chain development are being linked to improved nutrition and livelihoods.

Shettima also visited the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute, where the delegation received briefings on the application of technology, data and innovation to development and public-sector delivery.

The final day of the exchange focused on early childhood development, with engagements covering pre-primary education, healthcare, daycare and parental coaching, followed by a working session on translating lessons from Ethiopia into concrete commitments for the Nutrition 774 Initiative.

The programme culminated in a Nigeria Country Session and a joint closing ceremony attended by Shettima and Deputy Prime Minister Tiruneh, during which both countries reaffirmed their commitment to sustained cooperation and knowledge exchange on nutrition and development.

Shettima said the real measure of the exchange would be how effectively the lessons are translated into improved outcomes for Nigerian families, particularly women and children, through stronger implementation of Nutrition 774 across the country.

World.title: Abia Engages Community Leaders On Accommodation For New Teachers, Offers N30,000 Incentive
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Government says it is engaging traditional rulers, Presidents-General and other community leaders to provide accommodation for the newly recruited 4,075 teachers posted to rural and hard-to-reach areas, while also offering a N30,000 incentive to those who accept the postings.

The Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Elder Goodluck Ubochi, disclosed this in Umuahia during a press briefing to sensitise the Cohort 2 teachers who have just received their letters of engagement and posting, against the backdrop of complaints by the new recruits.

Ubochi said the second batch of recruitment became necessary after the deployment of the first batch of 5,394 teachers, as vacancies still exist in remote schools, which is the essence of the second engagement.

He said the teachers were informed from the outset and even signed a commitment that they would be deployed to where their services are needed, and therefore should not expect postings to places of comfort.

The commissioner acknowledged complaints from some teachers posted to hinterlands, but insisted they must first report to their schools, register their presence with the headteacher or principal, and then report back their challenges.

According to him, government under Governor Alex Otti is passionate about teachers’ welfare and does not want a situation where a teacher spends more than his salary to get to work, hence the interface with communities and School-Based Management Committees (SBMCs) for accommodation.

He appealed to Presidents-General, traditional rulers and Abians in diaspora who own unoccupied buildings in the hinterlands to release even their boys’ quarters to accommodate the teachers.

“We have also opened a help desk in the ministry. When they go to these places, we expect them to come back and report their experiences. Because when a teacher is not comfortable, he will not be able to deliver,” Ubochi said.

On welfare, he disclosed that Governor Otti has approved an additional N30,000 incentive for teachers serving in difficult areas. “There is an additional N30,000 incentive that has been in the cooler waiting to be extended to those who take up this responsibility. As soon as they settle down, we’ll take their details and make sure that this incentive is extended to them.”

Ubochi said the ministry expects feedback from headteachers and principals before the end of the week on teachers who have reported, and urged the new teachers to complete their onboarding at ASUBEB and SEMB within this week and next week to be captured in the payroll and receive salary by end of October as directed by the governor on Teachers’ Day.

He also reminded teachers who retired under the old 60 years of age /35 years of service rule and are willing to return under the new 65 years policy to report to the Ministry for documentation and reintegration.

Responding to questions, the commissioner said errors such as posting secondary school subject specialists to primary schools would be corrected, adding that the Ministry’s Quality Assurance units and satellite offices in LGAs will verify complaints and monitor truancy and connivance with school heads.

World.title: Ifowodo Wins $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Poetry on Religious, Political Violence
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

Poet Ogaga Ifowodo has won The Nigeria Prize for Literature 2026, securing the $100,000 cash award for his collection, Why Does God Need a Gun?, which examines religious and political violence in Nigeria.

In a related development, Beyond Tarkwa Bay by Peter Oghenetega Oke and Mara Mania by Feranmi Abiola have emerged as joint winners of the inaugural Nigeria Prize for Creative Arts, which carries a $20,000 cash award.

The winners were announced at the Grand Award Night organised by Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG) in Lagos on Friday, October 9, 2026.

Ifowodo’s poetry collection was selected from 223 entries, while the two winning documentaries emerged from 98 submissions for the Creative Arts Prize.

Announcing the literature winner, Chairman of the Advisory Board for The Nigeria Prize for Literature, Professor Akachi Adimora-Ezeigbo, described Why Does God Need a Gun? as a sensitive portrayal of religious and political violence in Nigeria, narrated through the voice of an imagined victim.

She commended all three shortlisted poetry collections for their technical skill, confidence and mature use of language, noting that they addressed themes extending beyond Nigeria’s borders.

According to her, the collections explored interconnected issues, including identity and belonging, the promises and disappointments of nationhood, the consequences of extremism and displacement, and the enduring impact of conflict on individuals and communities.

She said that, although distinct in voice and style, the works were rooted in the Nigerian experience while contributing to wider global conversations about humanity.

On the Creative Arts Prize, Technical Adviser to its Advisory Board, Joel Kachi Benson, praised the five shortlisted documentaries for challenging perceptions, fostering human connections and drawing attention to communities and experiences that often remain overlooked.

He said the films brought audiences closer to communities whose stories were rarely told and amplified voices that frequently went unheard.

Benson added that the documentaries celebrated resilience, documented culture, preserved memory and presented perspectives that enriched society’s understanding of itself.

The literature and creative arts awards followed the September 2026 announcement of Mary-Brenda Akoda as the winner of The Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation.

Akoda’s winning innovation, GenScan AI (GenMRI/C-MORE), is an artificial intelligence-powered solution designed to accelerate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Her victory marked two milestones: she became the prize’s first Generation Z recipient and the first woman to win as an individual awardee.

Speaking at the ceremony, NLNG Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Adeleye Falade, said the Nigeria Prizes were established to recognise outstanding achievements and promote scientific innovation, literary excellence and creative expression that enrich society and improve lives.

He noted that the science and innovation prize had recognised groundbreaking contributions across critical sectors, including healthcare, agriculture, engineering, energy, technology, climate resilience and sustainable development.

According to him, the prize had celebrated scientists whose work extended beyond laboratories and research papers to deliver practical solutions capable of improving lives.

Falade said this year’s winning innovation, which focuses on artificial intelligence and information technology, had the potential to transform lives in Nigeria and beyond.

On literature, he said The Nigeria Prize for Literature had grown into one of Africa’s most prestigious literary honours, attracting widespread interest and providing a platform for some of the continent’s finest literary voices.

He said Nigerian writers had demonstrated through the prize that their stories were more than accounts of their origins, contributing meaningfully to global conversations about identity, resilience and shared humanity.

Falade described the Nigeria Prize for Creative Arts as a platform for recognising originality, authenticity and creative excellence, particularly among artists who preserve Nigeria’s cultural heritage while reinterpreting it for a new generation.

He said the three prizes had become enduring national institutions, demonstrating what could be achieved when excellence was recognised, rewarded and encouraged.

Congratulating the winners and finalists, Falade said their achievements reflected discipline, dedication and perseverance.

He expressed hope that the awards would inspire a new generation of scientists, writers and creative professionals to develop solutions to future challenges, tell compelling stories and shape the country’s future.

In his remarks, Nobel laureate Professor Wole Soyinka called for closer collaboration between the humanities and the sciences, describing imagination as a vital link between literature, creative arts and scientific inquiry.

He argued that imagination was not confined to the humanities, noting that disciplines such as mathematics and physics also depended on vision and the ability to conceive new possibilities.

Soyinka urged practitioners in both fields to work together to expand the boundaries of imagination and combine their strengths in the service of humanity.

He stressed that human wellbeing should remain central to creative expression and scientific advancement.

NLNG said the Nigeria Prizes reaffirmed its commitment to recognising excellence and encouraging achievements capable of contributing to a sustainable future.

World.title: Dangote Cement  Awards Scholarships, Empowers Farmers, Market Women in Kogi
World.content:
Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja

Dangote Cement Plc, Obajana Plant, has strengthened its support for the Jakura community through scholarship awards and empowerment programmes for farmers and market women.

The Plant Director, Obajana Plant, Engr. Azad Nawabuddin, said the scheme was part of the company’s commitment to implementing the provisions of the Community Development Agreement (CDA).

The director who was represented by the Head of Social Performance at the Obajana Plant, Prince Ademola Adeyemi, said the empowerment programme benefited students, farmers and market women.

Nawabuddin said the programme, which focused on students, farmers and market women, underscores DCP’s continued commitment to sustainable community development, poverty reduction and economic empowerment across its host communities.

He said a total of 20 beneficiaries drawn from several tertiary institutions and 60 beneficiaries from secondary schools received educational grants running into several millions of naira.

He disclosed that 20 farmers were provided with essential farming implements and funds, noting that the initiative is designed to enhance agricultural productivity, encourage the adoption of improved farming practices and contribute to greater food security in the community.

Twenty market women were each provided with start-up capital and business support to strengthen their enterprises, promote financial independence and enhance household incomes.

The event attracted several stakeholders, traditional rulers, government representatives, and community leaders including His Royal Highness, Oba Usman Adoga Ajibola, the Obaro of Jakura., Representative of the Olu of Oworo, Chief K.A Mahmood, (The Obalumema of Oworo Land), Engr. E.O. Olaitan, Ministry of Solid Minerals Development (MSMD), Mrs. A. O. Onimode, Kogi State Ministry of Solid Mineral and Natural Resources, youth and women groups, members of Jakura traditional council, among others.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Chairman of Jakura CDA Committee, Chief Bonibade Ajiboye, appreciated Dangote Cement Plc Obajana Plant for keeping to commitments noting that aside the empowerment programme, the electrification project is almost completed.

He commended the plant for the kind gesture towards the Jakura community despite the security challenge. Goodwill messages were brought to the event by members of Jakura Traditional Council, Oworo Traditional Council, federal and state representatives with all commending and joining Jakura community to express appreciation to Dangote Cement Plc, Obajana Plant.

In his remarks, His Royal Highness, Oba Usman Adoga Ajibola, the Obaro of Jakura, expressed gratitude to Almighty God for blessing Jakura with abundant mineral resources and commended Alhaji Aliko Dangote for choosing to invest in the area.

The royal father also lauded Dangote Cement Plc for its numerous developmental interventions in the community, describing the latest empowerment initiative as another demonstration of the company’s commitment to improving the welfare and livelihoods of its host communities.

He pledged that the community would ensure the sustainability of the projects and see to it that the beneficiaries put their respective benefits to good use.

He prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Alhaji Aliko Dangote for his generosity, philanthropy and contributions to humanity.

World.title: Flood: Youth Leader Urges Rivers to Extend Assistance to Ogoni Victims
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The President General of the Ogoni Youth Federation (OYF), Legborsi Yamaabana, has urged the Rivers State Government to extend its flood relief programme to Nyokhana and other flood-affected communities across Ogoniland.

Yamaabana, who is also the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Khana Constituency II in the 2027 Rivers State House of Assembly election, called for N200,000 cash assistance and one year of free healthcare for verified flood victims in the affected communities.

In a statement yesterday, he commended Governor Siminalayi Fubara and his Deputy, Prof Ngozi Odu, who chairs the Rivers State Flood Prevention and Management Committee, for the government’s reported decision to provide the same package to flood victims in Eneka, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area.

He, however, appealed to the government to extend similar consideration to affected households in Ogoniland.

“Humanitarian relief must be guided by need, not geography,” Yamaabana said, stressing that families whose homes, farmlands and livelihoods had been damaged by flooding also required urgent assistance.

He identified more than 23 affected Ogoni communities, including Lueku, Lorre, Luebe, Yeghe, Bera, Kono, Kereke Bo-ue, Zor-Sogho and Okwale, as areas requiring government attention.

According to him, the flooding has submerged homes, damaged properties, disrupted academic activities, destroyed farmlands and threatened the livelihoods of residents.

“The suffering is real, the needs are urgent, and the response must be inclusive,” he said.

Yamaabana disclosed that he had formally written to Odu, in her capacity as chairman of the state flood management committee, requesting urgent intervention in the affected Ogoni communities.

He said the appeal was aimed at securing practical assistance for residents through constructive engagement with the state government.

The OYF president-general also called for an urgent assessment of flood damage, immediate support for displaced and vulnerable households, rehabilitation of drainage channels and the implementation of sustainable flood-prevention measures.

He maintained that the request was not for preferential treatment but for the needs of flood victims in Ogoniland to receive adequate consideration.

“We are not asking for special privileges for Ogoni; we are demanding fair consideration for Ogoni people whose homes, farms and livelihoods have been devastated by flooding,” he said.

He urged the governor and the flood management committee to ensure that relief efforts covered all communities where residents had suffered flood-related losses.

Yamaabana added that he would continue to advocate for the welfare and protection of affected residents in his capacity as leader of the Ogoni Youth Federation and a prospective representative of Khana Constituency II.

“Ogoni flood victims deserve relief. Our communities deserve protection. Our people must not be left behind,” he said.

World.title: Military Clarifies Misconceptions Surrounding Implementation of Newly Approved Pension Rates
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian military has clarified misconceptions surrounding the implementation of the newly approved pension rates.

The Military Pensions Board (MPB) provided these clarifications during a consultative meeting with representatives of military veterans’ associations at the Board’s headquarters in Abuja, yesterday.

According to a statement by the Public Relations Officer of the Military Pensions Board, Squadron Leader Aliyu Mohammed, the engagement provided an opportunity for the Board to explain the implementation process, address concerns raised by the representatives and promote a shared understanding of the new pension rates.

“During the meeting, the representatives expressed their understanding of the explanations provided by the Board and appreciated the opportunity to engage directly with its officials. The discussions also reinforced the importance of continued dialogue, mutual understanding and the use of established communication channels to address pension-related concerns,” he said.

Mohammed said the Board reaffirmed its commitment to the welfare of military pensioners and assured the representatives that it remained dedicated to transparent communication, constructive engagement and the timely resolution of issues within its mandate.

World.title: Gbenga Hashim’s Court Victory: INEC, Accord Party Served With Court Judgement
World.content:
.Mgbudem mounts opposition, appeals judgement of lower court



Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Certified True Copy of the Federal High Court judgement affirming Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as the presidential candidate for the 2027 election has been served on the Accord Party and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

This sets the stage for implementation of the court’s orders.

Justice Mohammed Garba Umar, of the Federal High Court in Abuja, ruled on October 5, 2026 that Hashim emerged as Accord’s presidential candidate from the May 30, 2026 primary and ordered the party to submit his name to INEC.

The court further ordered INEC to accept and recognise him as the party’s presidential candidate.

The judgement followed a suit filed by Hashim against Accord Party and INEC over the party’s failure to submit his name after the disputed primary.

Accord Party’s counsel, T.W. Olusesi, told the court that the primary had been validly cancelled.

Hashim’s counsel, Henry Akunebu (SAN) challenged the purported cancellation and the documents relied upon by the party and INEC, arguing that the cancellation letter lacked the party’s official stamp and raised questions about how it was received within the electoral commission.

Justice Umar ultimately rejected the objections and held that the evidence before the court established that Hashim had emerged from the May 30 exercise.

The judge also relied on evidence that the Accord Party had accepted N50 million from Hashim for Expression of Interest and nomination forms.

What has particularly intrigued political and legal observers was the extent to which INEC became involved in the dispute.

The court has now given judgement on the dispute and the CTC of the judgement has been served on both defendants.

“The immediate issue is, therefore, no longer simply whether Hashim won the Accord primary. It is whether the party and the electoral commission will give effect to the orders of the Federal High Court.”

The development also marks a new phase in Hashim’s candidacy.

Following the judgement, the legal dispute that had cast uncertainty over Accord’s presidential ticket has moved into the implementation stage, with the court directing the party to recognise Hashim and forward his name to INEC for the 2027 presidential election.

Indications have emerged however, that the party chairman may still be spoiling for a fight at the appellate court despite Hashim’s call for reconciliation.

The latest development, however, has renewed attention on the unusual legal battle surrounding Hashim’s candidacy.

Meanwhile, Accord Party Chairman, Maxwell Mgbudem, has appealed the judgement delivered by Justice Umar in his suit: FHC/ABJ/1268/226, filed at the Court of Appeal.

World.title: First look: Meet Mr and Mrs Dricus du Plessis!
World.content:
Dricus du Plessis and Vasti Spiller are officially husband and wife! The couple tied the knot in a picturesque wedding in the Western Cape on Saturday, 10 October.

The MMA fighter and his boxing coach partner have been dating since 2023.

FIRST LOOK: DRICUS DU PLESSIS AND VASTI SPILLER WEDDING

On her Instagram Stories, Vasti Spiller has shared a first look at her wedding day to Dricus du Plessis.



The couple wed at a picturesque venue in Paarl in the Western Cape.

Vasti wore a custom Anel Botha creation during the ceremony, while Dricus wore a crisp black tuxedo.

The blonde bride changed into an Amara Bespoke gown, adorned with sequins and pearls, for the reception, and her husband donned a cream blazer to match her.



The wedding was attended by the couple’s close family and friends, with entertainment including the likes of Bobby van Jaarsveld and Ricus Nel.

Take a look at the first images from the day…

Inside Dricus du Plessis and Vasti Spiller’s wedding day.

Images via IG

PRAISE FOR ‘UNDERSTANDING PARTNER’

Dricus du Plessis and Vasti Spiller met at the CIT Boxing in Hatfield, Pretoria, in 2023, where he trained, and she worked as a boxing coach.



They crossed paths after Vasti pursued boxing coaching a year earlier.

Fast forward to 2025, Dricus and Vasti announced their engagement.

Speaking to KFM about their relationship, the former UFC World Champion praised his partner for being supportive and empathetic to his career.



He said: “I kind of feel sorry for her because it’s like she’s dating two different human beings… when a fight comes around, it’s such a selfish sport and everything needs to go around this fight, and what needs to happen for me, so everything else takes a backseat – family, friends, everything.

“Because you have to give it your all, and it’s amazing to have a partner understanding all of that.”

World.title: Roosevelt High School principal defended over ‘Hitler’ comment
World.content:
The public have defended Roosevelt High School's principal against racism allegations. Images via Facebook

Pastor Curt van Heerden’s comments chastising Roosevelt High School principal Cristèl Venter, who likened her actions in shutting down a Matric Dance disaster event to that of Adolf Hitler, have been met with strong resistance from the public.

The Johannesburg school has come under fire after Venter’s viral open letter condemning a handful of Grade 12 learners for underage drinking, drug use, and a firearm incident at the event, which took place at Avianto Hotel in Muldersdrift.

ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL: PRINCIPAL QUESTIONED OVER ‘HITLER COMPARISON’

In a Facebook post, Pastor Curt van Heerden called for Roosevelt High School to refund ticket sales after principal Cristèl Venter shut down the Matric Dance early due to allegations of learner misconduct.



Van Heerden, a social media community activist, supported his argument by quoting Avianto Hotel, which claimed that Venter had decided to cut the event short.

The venue also disputed allegations that learners were served alcohol, damaged property or that a firearm incident involved minors.

He also quoted several parents and learners, who were left disappointed and frustrated at the sequence of events.

The preacher and social media influencer also chastised Venter over a screenshot of her WhatsApp status comparing herself to German dictator Adolf Hitler.

The status, which came after the principal learned of the Matric Dance fiasco, read:

“I am an extremely embarrassed principal, when parents pull firearms at the poor Avianto staff and Grad 12 learners pitch up drink as can be and vomit all over the bathroom 

“Stick a fork in me, I am done. This will be the last one. Class of 2026, can you be any bigger of a disappointment? Your marks are horrendous, and then you can’t even behave.

Venter added the hashtag “#Hitlerloading”

Curt van Heerden claimed that the hashtag hinted at racial undertones.

He asked: “Why would the principal of Roosevelt High School – who is white – put this on her status? What was she trying to say?”

PUBLIC DEFENDS PRINCIPAL

Curt van Heerden’s insinuation was met with opposition from many of his followers, who disagreed with his sentiment in the comment section.

Here’s what a few had to say…

Angelo Major: The hashtag was not intended to be racist. In my opinion, she was saying she would need to be ruthless in her actions, like Hitler was in his actions, in order to take control of the sh!t show that was going on. While the reference to Hitler is completely inappropriate, let’s not make this about a white woman being racist. This is about kids getting out of hand and the unfortunate reality that the consequences affected everyone”

Maxine Cero Louw: “I stand with the principal. Not everything has to be an issue. Things should not be taken out of context. Great job, principal”

Estelle Kriek Venter: “Why do you stand up for those children? This is why they behave so badly: no accountability. That woman teaches them a life lesson about consequences. Stop vilifying her”.

WHAT HAPPENED AT ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL’S MATRIC DANCE?

In a lengthy open letter posted on the school’s official Facebook page last week, Roosevelt High School principal Cristèl Venter expressed her shock and disappointment at the behaviour of some learners who attended the Matric Dance at the Avianto Hotel in Muldersdrift.

Venter had initially skipped the event due to illness, but had been called in to intervene after things took a turn for the worse.

Venter revealed that learners had arrived under the influence of alcohol and drugs, and that one particular entourage had threatened staff with firearms during their rowdy procession and reckless driving into the venue. Intoxicated learners reportedly became violently ill, vomiting all over the five-star venue.

The principal decided to cut short the Matric Dance in a bid to de-escalate the deteriorating situation, but was met with contempt and verbal abuse from parents, who angrily confronted school staff.

Venter vowed to launch an investigation into the incident and hold a disciplinary hearing for those involved.

A few days later, podcaster Penuel Mlotshwa addressed the school learners, urging them to exercise responsibility and accountability.

When approached for comment, principal Cristèl Venter stated that she was not authorised to speak to the media.

The school has since disabled its social media platforms.

World.title: Sundowns star reveals his brother was stabbed
World.content:
Teboho Mokoena celebrates scoring for Mamelodi Sundowns against Orlando Pirates in the 2026 MTN8 final at the Moses Mabhida Stadium. Image: Official PSL

Following Sundowns’ triumph in the MTN8 final over Orlando Pirates, Mokoena revealed that he has been dealing with the emotional struggles.

The Bethlehem-born star dedicated his goal to his late grandfather and his brother who remains in hospital.

MAMELODI SUNDOWNS STAR TEBOHO MOKOENA ADMITS TO EMOTIONAL TURMOIL

“It’s been tough two weeks for me, I lost my grandfather two weeks ago,” Mokoena told SuperSport TV after the game.



“I almost lost my brother who got stabbed the day before we played Guinea. They stabbed him multiple times, it’s been tough, but I’d like to dedicate this game to him, he is in the hospital bed. I hope justice will be served.”

The 29-year-old admitted that he has struggled emotionally despite continuing to represent his country on the pitch.

“I’m happy that we but inside I’m not really okay because it’s sad what happened to my family and you always have to show up doesn’t matter how you’re feeling.”

“I dedicate this game to him, my brother and I hope he recovers.”

KEY PLAYER FOR THE AFRICAN CHAMPIONS

Mokoena has established himself as a key figure in the Sundowns midfield since joining the club from SuperSport United in January 2022. He has marked 110 appearances, scoring 14 goals and providing 9 assists across all competitions.

Operating as a deep-lying midfielder, Mokoena plays a crucial role in controlling the tempo, winning possession and transitioning the team from defence to attack.



During the 2022/23 season, Mokoena made 27 league appearances, scoring one goal and providing two assists. He improved his attacking output in the 2023/24 campaign, registering three goals and three assists in 18 league matches. He remained a regular in the starting lineup during the 2024/25 and 2025/26 seasons, adding a combined five league goals and three assists.

Mokoena’s contributions have also helped Sundowns enjoy considerable success. He has won three Premier Soccer League titles (2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24), one Nedbank Cup (2022) and the inaugural African Football League title in 2023. His outstanding performances during the 2022/23 season also earned him the PSL Footballer of the Season award.
