World.title: Ouaddou explains why Lungu took penalty ahead of Appollis against Sundowns
World.content:
Orlando Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou has explained why Ghampani Lungu stepped up to take a penalty during the Buccaneers’ 2-0 defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final on Saturday.

The Zambian international had an opportunity to bring Pirates back into the game after Teboho Mokoena conceded a penalty. However, Lungu’s effort was saved by Sundowns goalkeeper Ronwen Williams.

At the time, Downs were leading 1-0 and had he scored, the goal would have changed the match.



Lungu’s decision to take the spot-kick raised questions among Pirates fans, with many believing Oswin Appollis should have stepped up instead, having regularly taken penalties last season.

After the match, Ouaddou clarified that Lungu was among the club’s designated penalty takers and was first in the pecking order for the opportunity.

Lungu’s penalty miss cost Pirates MTN8

“He [Lungu] is one of the designated takers. Of the players, he was first among the takers. After him, we have Appollis, we have…” Ouaddou said.

Despite the disappointment of losing the final, the Pirates coach acknowledged Sundowns’ victory and insisted his side would continue working hard.

“It’s moments like that, it’s football. We have to respect.

“Congratulations to Mamelodi Sundowns. Of course, we are disappointed, but in football, you have to be fair play.



“For us, we have to continue to work, and people are going to see a fantastic season because we are not going to give up.

“And we are going to try to keep our title,” he added.

Many Bucs fans feel Lungu should allowed Appollis to take the penalty given his experience. Appollis has scored crucial spotkicks for both club and country in the past.

Who should have taken that penalty?

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns 2-0 Orlando Pirates: Who Fired, Who Flopped
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns claimed their first MTN8 trophy in five years after beating Orlando Pirates 2-0 in the final on Saturday afternoon.

Goals from Teboho Mokoena and Iqraam Rayners handed the Brazilians their first cup victory over Pirates in 19 years.

Despite the win, Masandawana were far from their best but still did enough to get the job done against the Buccaneers, who struggled to find their rhythm for much of the encounter.



Sundowns edge Pirates to win MTN8

Here are the players who fired and those who flopped in the MTN8 final.

Players who fired

Ronwen Williams – 9/10

The Bafana Bafana captain was at his best once again against Pirates. He saved Ghampani Lungu’s penalty in the second half with Sundowns leading 1-0, a moment that proved crucial in changing the complexion of the match.



Williams made several more saves later in the game to preserve his clean sheet and help Masandawana secure the trophy.

Sipho Chaine – 9/10

Although he conceded twice, Chaine was one of Pirates’ standout performers. He made three excellent saves in the first half to keep his side in the game and give the Buccaneers hope of fighting back. However, poor decision-making and a missed penalty from his teammates meant his impressive performance ultimately counted for little.



Khulumani Ndamane – 8/10

The towering defender delivered a solid performance and hardly put a foot wrong. Ndamane dealt effectively with the Pirates attack, winning aerial duels and important challenges against the likes of Yanela Mbuthuma and Tshepang Moremi.

His defensive contribution helped Sundowns maintain control when Pirates tried to find a way back into the contest.



Players who flopped

Tshepang Moremi – 2/10

Having been preferred to Oswin Appollis, Moremi endured a difficult afternoon. The winger struggled to make an impact and was often forced to resort to shots from distance.



He spent much of the match chasing shadows and failed to trouble the Sundowns defence consistently. His performance raised questions about whether he should have been substituted earlier.

Sundowns controlled Pirates attackers

Thalente Mbatha – 4/10

Mbatha was guilty of surrendering possession on several occasions as Pirates struggled to establish control in midfield. Although he tried to make an impact, he ultimately lost the midfield battle against Sundowns.



Having spent a lengthy period on the sidelines, the talented midfielder appeared short of match sharpness, raising questions about whether he was ready to start a final of such magnitude. Sundowns benefitted more from Mbatha’s mistakes in the end.

Simphiwe Selepe – 3/10

Selepe struggled to rise to the occasion as Pirates were overrun in midfield. He failed to influence the game and offered little in terms of creativity or control.



With Sundowns dominating the central areas, the midfielder was largely ineffective and struggled to make his presence felt.

Ghampani Lungu – 4/10

Lungu endured a frustrating evening, missing a second-half penalty that could have changed the complexion of the final. He also had a promising opportunity when through on goal but opted to cut back instead of taking a shot or attempting to dribble past Thapelo Morena, who recovered to clear the danger.



His missed chances proved costly as Pirates failed to mount a serious comeback against their Sundowns.

Orlando Pirates were far from their best against Sundowns and paid the price for their shortcomings in both boxes. While Chaine did his best to keep the Buccaneers in the contest, their lack of cutting edge and struggles in midfield ultimately proved decisive.

Sundowns, meanwhile, were not at their fluent best but showed the composure and clinical finishing needed to win a final. Williams’ penalty save was a defining moment and ultimately won the match for Masandawana.



Which players impressed for the most?

World.title: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
World.content:
ESHOWE – A police constable allegedly shot and killed three women and injured a man before turning the gun on himself at a tavern in KwaMsane, KwaZulu-Natal.

Police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said police responded to reports of a shooting at a liquor establishment at Nkodibe area in KwaMsane, and when they arrived they found four bodies with gunshot wounds, and one victim with a gunshot wound who was taken to hospital.

“It was reported that the off-duty police constable also disarmed another man of his firearm during the incident. Both firearms were found at the scene. The cause of the shooting is unknown at this stage.”

In a separate incident, police in Eshowe are tracing a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a grocery chain store in Eshowe on Saturday.

“Reports indicate that the suspect, who is former employee of the store, had gone to the store for his internal disciplinary hearing. The suspect allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people who were declared dead at the scene. A manhunt for the suspect is underway.”

World.title: SANDF arrives in Durban
World.content:
DURBAN - The army has been spotted in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, amid tensions over asylum applications and illegal immigration.

Protests erupted after the Constitutional Court ruling that everyone must be given a fair chance to apply for asylum, regardless of documentation.

Violent unrest led to looting and the torching of vehicles.

Government has called for calm as tensions simmer.

World.title: Joburg Water warns of possible outages
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A power outage at the Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant has crippled pumping at the Palmiet Booster Station.

Johannesburg Water warns that parts of Sandton, Diepsloot, Rabie Ridge, and surrounding areas could face low water pressure or total outages.

The utility said it is monitoring the system and taking steps to stabilise supply.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly.

World.title: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Ex-Pollsmoor Correctional Centre inmates are using visual art to depict the realities of life behind bars.

This they say helps them deal with past trauma, their reintegration into society, and also to make a living.

Dubbed "Captured", the visual storytelling project, is set to eventually become a coffee table book.

Life behind bars is often reduced to statistics, without the human factor.

Enrico Samuels, an artist, served sixteen years behind bars for armed robbery said art connected him with people helping him to navigate life now as a free man.

"I want to become a successful artist, doctor is helping me to get there with the projects...lovely projects and I enjoy myself in the projects and from there I see a brighter future from doc's side, because she is taking me that way, so I can see the sun on the other side already,” said Samuels.

Michael Sauls said art serves as a conduit in helping them deal with their past and educate the public.

“People have no an idea of what prison is like, they think that everything is happy go-lucky or it's like a journey to another paradise, it's not worth it being there...you see it's easy to commit a crime, but it's not easy serving the time."

Dr Suzette Leal, the founder of Words Set Free, said the art tells the stories of the people behind it.

"If you say the work is beautiful, that's a complement to our artists and their ability, but the story is not beautiful. It's real and true and painful and traumatic. So, I think if anything I hope it discourages someone from getting involved in crime, but I think we don't reduce crime by making prison sentences longer or by making the conditions within them worse. We reduce crime by creating opportunities for people to create a livelihood outside of crime.”

Another artist, Kleinbooi Hendricks said: "I said to myself, although the parole board gave me a date to go out of prison, I'm not going. I will either complete my entire sentence but I'm not going out if I haven't worked on myself being a changed man or a different person. I did that because I said I'd either eat out of a dustbin outside, but I'm not going to commit crime again."

World.title: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Real change begins with communities taking responsibility for their own development.

Those are the views of Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, Founder of the Batho Pele Convention.

The initiative calls on South Africans to take the lead in improving their own living conditions.

“We are here to say you are the solution you are looking for. We are here to say you are the saviour, the developer, the healer and the builder you are looking for. We are here to vote for you to do it on your own.

“We are here to say you are the saviours you are looking for. We are not a corporate think tank. Long have we interpreted our misery from broadcast to podcast, think shops to talk shops.

“The point is to change our living conditions, one pothole at a time, one classroom at a time and one production hub at a time,” Ndlozi said.

World.title: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg's public pools are missing out on the summer rush.

And most are still closed despite the rising temperatures.

Community leader Dulton Adams said poor planning, lack of proper budgeting and no clear management plans, are leaving residents without these facilities.

The city has 57 public pools, but only 13 are open so far.

Ten more are expected to open on Monday.

"Every season there's just no budget.

There's just no management plan. There's no vision to make sure that the children come off the streets and you look at the pool. This is not the only pool.

"Remember spring day, pools must open first. Then the City Council asked for 1 October, pools would be open. That was missed and then now the 7th," Adams said.

World.title: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC could emerge as the biggest loser in this year's municipal elections.

This is the view is political strategist Brutus Malada.

He said the party’s declining support could leave it with less influence across key metros and this could push it into a weakened position ahead of the 2029 elections.

“ANC will be the big loser in this. The trend is clear. It's clear that they are losing at a margin of 10 to 12 percent and that will actually mean the end of the ANC and it will become lame duck for this period in between the two elections.

“That it will sit, it will be a national government President Ramaphosa sitting in Tshwane. The Union Buildings which is led by another party and in Cape Town which is the legislative arm of the state which is led by the DA.

“So here is a political party that is running the country as the head of the State but it has no control of the economy hub, it has no control of administrative hub, it has no control of legislative hub,” Malada said.

World.title: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi
World.content:
Mamelodi – The family and friends of the slain 14-year-old twins have gathered in Mamelodi West to bid farewell to the boys.

Bonolo and Botlhale Makena were found dead in their home a week ago. They had multiple stab wounds.

The boys' mother made the gruesome discovery at home, when she returned from work.

As police investigate, residents are demanding that this case does not become another unresolved killing.

Neighobour Padi Matlala said the Mamelodi West community is demanding justice.

“The community has been here before. The community is saying, ‘please justice system, don't take us there.’ We were there in 1982. Two members of the community were brutally murdered. 44 years later, nobody has been held responsible.

“The community is saying justice system never, never again should you go through this. The pressure that you put on the government throughout the week, the outrage you showed must bear fruit. Somebody or some people must be held responsible for this. We are better than this,” Matlala said.
